News.title: France preparing to evacuate entire tourist city as ‘erratic’ fire ‘whirlwinds’ wreak havoc & firefighers ‘overwhelmed’
News.content:
FRANCE is preparing to evacuate an entire city as “erratic” fire whirlwinds push flames towards its nearly one million residents.

Two major wildfires have broken out on Bordeaux‘s western flank, which “overwhelmed” firefighters are “far from having under control”.



More than 300,000 people in France and Spain have been forced to flee their homes as fires stoked by arid, tinder-box conditions and strong winds continue to rage.

It has led the Bordeaux Council to consider a total evacuation as acrid smoke looms over the city.



A spokesperson told Sky News that it is “currently studying scenarios for all possible ways the fire could evolve”.



Air quality and atmospheric pollution are a major concern in the popular tourist destination, famed for its wine quality.

Firefighters battling the encroaching blaze in the Gironde area are said to be “overwhelmed” as concerns grow about Bordeaux.



Sebastien Berge, head of the Gironde firefighters union, said: “When there’s a fire of this magnitude, it creates its own weather pattern…it’s difficult to monitor.

Have you been caught up in wildfires in France, Spain or elsewhere in Europe? Email joseph.mannion@the-sun.co.uk or WhatsApp 07353 096414 to share your story

“Especially when there’s a fire front that stretches for more than 20km (12.5 miles).

“When you see how far it’s spreading, I think we can now be concerned about the city of Bordeaux.”



Le Barp, a municipality less than 20 miles from Bordeaux, has been ordered to evacuate immediately via the south – in the opposite direction to the city.

Thousands of evacuees in the area have already been forced to bed down in an exhibition hall as they face an anxious wait over the state of their homes.

Residents and tourists were forced to flee the holiday hotspot Cap Ferret in their droves on Friday as the blaze took hold.

The French military has even been deployed to help with the response.



Reinforcements are also being sent in to help firefighters clear brush and create fire breaks – land that is cleared of fuel such as plants and wood.

Meanwhile in Spain, where a national emergency has been declared, favourable weather conditions have helped firefighters in their fight against merging fires outside Madrid.

But Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez conceded there were “complex times ahead”.

A man, believed to be in his 70s, was found dead in his car by firefighters as they extinguished a blaze in Valencia.

The fire near the Salt de l’Aigua ravine raged throughout Saturday but has been brought under control.



But three huge fires have merged to the west of the Spanish capital, where around 77,000 people have been evacuated and another 28,000 locked down in their homes.

The major fire near Madrid was described yesterday as being “at its peak” and “beyond the capacity” of firefighters to control.

The city’s emergency management chief Carlos Novillo told the BBC: “It is not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken.”

Madrid president Isabel Díaz Ayusohas said the inferno was “the worst fire in the history of the region”.

Díaz Ayusohas called the situation “catastrophic”, as residents in the capital were warned to stay inside their home and avoid going out unless absolutely necessary.



Dramatic footage showed police kicking down doors to rescue residents before the blaze consumed their homes.

It comes after Brit tourists near Bordeaux airport were forced to evacuate their hotels in the middle of the night.

Holidaymakers staying at a Holiday Inn were woken up at 3.30am and told that approaching smoke was forcing the hotel to close.

Nicola Smith, 49, told the Daily Mail: “We were all fast asleep when a member of hotel staff knocked on the door about 3.30am and said that we were having to evacuate.

“It was a shock to the system and quite dramatic but I’d been getting alerts on my phone all night by the local French authorities warning about other areas nearby being evacuated.”



Her husband Martin, 55, added: “It’s not great to be honest but what can you do?

“Apparently everywhere is being evacuated because of all the smoke drifting across to Bordeaux from the fire.

“I must admit you could really smell the smoke when we first arrived, there was a kind of haze in the air.”

News.title: Gatwick Airport left without running WATER with ‘toilets not working, water fountains stopped & no drinks’
News.content:
FLUSHING HELL Gatwick Airport left without running WATER with ‘toilets not working, water fountains stopped & no drinks’

GATWICK Airport has been left without running water following issues with low pressure and loss of supply.

Travellers at the airport have reported that there’s no flushing toilets, no running water at drinking fountains, and no drinks can be made at restaurants or cafes.



SES Water, which serves customers in Surrey, West Sussex, Kent and south London, said this morning that some of their customers are experiencing water shortages.

An issue at its Bough Beech Water Treatment Works has caused problems with the water supply.



While the company have said their most vulnerable customers are receiving bottled water as they work quickly to fix the issue, the UK’s second largest airport has been left in the lurch.

Parched holidaymakers have taken to social media to share their frustrations with the situation.



Have you been affected by this? Contact Hannah at hannah.bentley@thesun.co.uk

Julia Hartley-Brewer said on a post to X that she was disappointed the airport didn’t announce the water supply issue quickly.

“If you’re on your way to Gatwick Airport, it might be helpful to know that there is no running water across the entire airport,” she said.

“That means no coffees, no water fountains, no flushing toilets and no hand washing.



“Gatwick hasn’t bothered to make a public announcement about this to passengers. How helpful…”

Another person said: “Gatwick Airport has lost access to running water after days of disruption

“We’re talking about the UK’s second busiest airport here… Our country is crumbling.”

One traveller added: “Gatwick Airport currently has no running water so no restaurants, no bars, no coffees, no flushing toilets, no washing of hands and no free drinking water.

“I can’t even have a airport pint because they have………(checks notes) no running water. Gatwick is the worst!”



In a statement posted to their social media account, the airport said: “A water issue in the Horley area is causing disruption at the airport this morning.

“The problem is affecting water supply in both terminals and is currently under investigation. At present, there has been no impact on flights.

“Bottled water is being made available to passengers and staff across the airport and other contingency measures are being put in place to ensure the welfare of our passengers.

“We apologise for any inconvenience to passengers.”

News.title: Man and two children airlifted to hospital after getting into difficulty in sea at popular UK beach resort
News.content:
SEA RESCUE Man and two children airlifted to hospital after getting into difficulty in sea at popular UK beach resort

A MAN and two children have been airlifted to hospital after getting into difficulty at sea.

Major emergency responders scrambled to Main Sands, Margate, as an air ambulance and coastguard helicopter landed on the beach.

The alarm was raised following reports swimmers were in difficulty at the boating pool area at around 4.30pm yesterday.

Paramedics, police, Margate RNLI, coastguard teams and the Coastguard rescue helicopter and the KSS air ambulance raced to rescue the three.





Passersby were said to have pulled at least one of the children from the water before emergency crews arrived, reports The Isle of Thanet News.

Dozens of cop cars, ambulances and specialist response vehicles were said to be seen near the seafront.

Lifeguards and paramedics were seen giving treatment to the victims on the side of the tidal pool, reports Kent Online.

A stretch of the beachfront was closed as emergency services dealt with the incident, causing traffic heading in and out of Margate.



It is understood the children were airlifted to King’s College Hospital, London while the man was taken to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford.

A police spokesperson said: “Kent Police was called at 4.36pm to a report that a man and two children had come into difficulty in the sea at Margate, and were receiving medical treatment at the scene.

“Officers attended to manage traffic in the area and to allow an air ambulance and coastguard helicopter to land.

“The three casualties were all airlifted to hospital for further treatment.”



A HM Coastguard spokesperson added: “HM Coastguard responded to reports of a medical incident involving three people in the water in the Margate Main Sands area today, 25 July.

“First informed at around 4.30pm, Margate and Herne Bay Coastguard Rescue Teams, a lifeboat from Margate RNLI and an HM Coastguard helicopter were sent to the scene, alongside other emergency services.

“All three people were transferred to hospital.”

News.title: Girl, 17, critical after e-scooter carrying two teens crashes with car in city centre ‘hit-and-run’
News.content:
E-SCOOTER HORROR Girl, 17, critical after e-scooter carrying two teens crashes with car in city centre ‘hit-and-run’

A TEENAGER is fighting for her life following a crash involving a van and an e-scooter.

Two 17-year-old girls riding an e-scooter collided with a Mercedes Vito on Great George Street, Liverpool at around 1.20am this morning.

Emergency services rushed to the scene where one of the girls was quickly taken to hospital.



She remains in critical condition.



The other girl has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving, drug driving and driving without insurance.

The van driver did not stay at the scene, and instead drove away after the crash occurred.

But following enquiries, cops tracked down a 57-year-old man from Liverpool.

He has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and failing to stop.

Police are now appealing for any information relating to the incident.

Detective Sergeant Simon Duffy from the Matrix Serious Collision Investigation Unit said: “This was a very serious collision that has resulted in a teenage girl in hospital where she is currently in a critical condition.

“As part of our initial inquiries, we have arrested two people and they both remain in custody where they will be questioned about their possible involvement.



“In the meantime, I’d like to take this opportunity to appeal to any possible witnesses.

“We know this happened very early this morning, but if anyone saw what occurred or were driving through the area just before the incident, then please get in touch.

“I would also ask anyone who travelled through other parts of the city and saw two girls on an e-scooter to let us know.

“Similarly, if you live or work in the area and have CCTV or smart doorbell footage, please take a moment to review to see if you captured anything that could assist our investigation.

“Even the smallest of details could be vital, so please don’t hesitate to get in touch and let our team review your footage.”



Anyone who witnessed the collision or captured the incident on CCTV or dashcam is being urged by police to contact the SCIU on (0151) 777 5747.

Or, you can email SCIU@merseyside.police.uk quoting incident reference 072 of 26 July.

Alternatively, DM @MerPolCC on X or Facebook, or contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website here: https://crimestoppers-uk.org/give-information/forms/give-information-anonymously

News.title: Cyclist who tried to catch out driver with bike cam vid is fined £1,200 for his OWN bad riding as complaint backfires
News.content:
AN angry cyclist who reported a motorist for bad driving has been slapped with a £1,200 fine after footage revealed his dodgy pedalling.

Footage shows the pedal biker space- invading oncoming cars and riding “without due care and attention” according to cops.



The cyclist uploaded footage of motorists to West Yorkshire Police hoping to dob in a bad driver near Leeds.

But the video ended up exposing his own mishaps as he cycled in the middle of the road narrowly avoiding a motorist who was forced to “hug the kerb” to prevent a scraping.



Now the cyclist has been ordered to pay over £1,200 in fines and court costs by a Magistrate in Bradford for “riding without due care and attention”.

West Yorkshire Police said: “The Leeds-based cyclist uploaded a video showing a car passing too close to his pedal cycle to our Op Snap portal.



“But later on in the same submission, he captured himself riding without due care and attention as he approached a parked car and an oncoming vehicle.

“Rather than slow down or have to unclip from his pedals, the rider chose to travel between the parked car and the vehicle heading directly towards him.”

News.title: Dramatic moment ‘lethal’ US forces board tanker in Strait of Hormuz amid blockade – as Trump weighs next move on Iran
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment US forces boarded a tanker amid their ironclad Strait of Hormuz naval blockade.

It comes as Trump mulls his next move on Iran – but warned “lethal and vigilant” troops remain ready to take action in the highly contested waterway.



The president walked back from staging the “massive attack” he had vowed on Friday, but still promised “major punishment” for Tehran and its Houthi puppets.

Dramatic footage showed US troops rappelling onto the Comoros-flagged M/T Charminar in the embattled Arabian Sea as Trump continues his stranglehold on Iranian ports.





Another tanker – the Mozambique-flagged M/T Lavine – was “disabled” in the Gulf of Oman after trying to flout the blockade “multiple times”.

US Central Command shared footage of their high-stakes mission to X, adding that since its blockade was reinstated 12 commercial vessels have been redirected, two disabled, and two boarded.



It added: “American forces remain highly vigilant, focused, lethal, and ready.”

Trump’s decision to row back on planned strikes was caused by a diminished stockpile of Patriot antimissile interceptors, according to the New York Times.

It comes as the Houthis have waded into the conflict by claiming to have attacked several Saudi Arabian vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait – a key trade waterway linking the Red Sea to Europe.

Trump has promised “major military punishment” for the Yemeni Iranian-backed proxy if it hits another tanker.



The Houthis also claimed they launched dozens of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at two Saudi oil depots in the Red Sea cities of Yanbu and Jizan.

Daily US airstrikes on Iran have meanwhile stopped after nearly two weeks of intense bombing.

Peace talks have been pushed forward again as Washington and Tehran look to avert resuming all-out war.

The warring nations are said to be keen on returning to an interim ceasefire deal, but Iran‘s control over the Strait of Hormuz remains a sticking point.



Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei, confirmed that Tehran had held technical talks about the waterway with Oman.

After being besieged for nearly four months, the Strait was reopened to commercial shipping after a memorandum of understanding (MOU) was signed on June 17.

There was hope that negotiators could hash out a deal, bringing an end to the brutal conflict and stabilising global fuel prices.

But that turned out to be a false dawn as Iran’s trigger-happy Islamic Guards began firing on ships in the strait.

After two weeks of bombing, Trump is reportedly reluctant to keep widening the war.



An escalation risks alienating key Gulf allies who have been targeted by Iran , as well as a global economic crunch if the strait remains closed.

White House Communications Director Steven Cheung has said that after enduring repeated strikes and crippling sanctions, “it would be wise for Iran to work towards a negotiated deal; otherwise, they know what will happen.”

Trump is said to be considering an attack on Pickaxe mountain, a heavily fortified underground complex where Iran is believed to have hidden its nuclear stockpiles.

He told Axios on Thursday: “I am considering a massive attack. Bigger than ever before. I am close to making a decision. We are all set for it.”

It comes as US spies fear that new Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei is even more determined to develop a nuclear bomb than his late father.



Fresh US intelligence suggests the killing of Supreme Tyrant Ali Khamenei in February has led to the intensification of Tehran’s nuclear ambitions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

While Mojtaba has never publicly called for use of nuclear bombs, he reportedly has fewer ideological qualms about weaponization and may back a more advanced arsenal, according to The New York Times.

If true, it could deal a blow to any peace agreement, given Iran’s long-term denuclearisation is Trump’s top priority.

News.title: Kira Cousins blames ‘stupid’ loved ones who fell for her fake baby scandal as her ex finally breaks silence
News.content:
FAKE baby ‘mum’ Kira Cousins has blamed her “stupid” loved ones for falling for her twisted scandal – as her ex opens up about the ordeal for the first time.

The 23-year-old bogus ‘mum’ duped family, friends and the supposed father into believing she was pregnant, and even hosted a baby shower before pretending a life-like doll was her tot.



She introduced the doll to loved ones as her daughter Bonnie-Leigh Joyce, and hundreds of doting comments flooded in congratulating her.

Days later, she is said to have lied that the make-believe child had died from a heart condition.



However, the ruse was exposed when her mum found the doll in her bedroom, and a betrayed friend posted the story online.

Kira later fled the house she shares with her mum in Airdrie, Lanarkshire, and went into hiding to escape the backlash after being bombarded with hate online when the story went viral in October last year.



But in a tell-all interview, she blamed her closest friends and family for being “stupid” to believe the twisted lies she created.

Speaking to The Sunday Mail, Kira admitted to faking giving birth to a little girl and accepted that what she did was wrong.

However, she claimed that her lies started after she suffered a miscarriage and was unable to tell her then-boyfriend Jamie Gardner, who believed the doll was real.

The former supermarket worker said: “I couldn’t tell him. I did lose a child. I’d tried to tell him when I first lost the child.



“I still have messages on my phone which said, ‘Jamie, we need to sit down,’ but I couldn’t speak to him about anything.

“I can hold my hands up and say, ‘No, I shouldn’t have used a doll’, but at the same time, nobody knows what our relationship was like.”

Kira said the deceit spiralled out of control because she was worried about telling Jamie the truth about her miscarriage.

She added: “I think there was a bit of fear and shock as well. I’d gone through that myself.

“Before all this, we had also fallen out, and it was really bad. He hadn’t wanted the baby at first, and I think that didn’t help.



“He had gone from that to, ‘Here we go, we are actually going to have it,’ and then to wanting it.”

The bogus mum hosted a gender reveal party, and photos and videos apparently show Kira bending over and crying with joy as a cannon and pink confetti burst out.

The supposed mum also allegedly bought a fake baby bump and wore it to weddings and later bombarded her social media profiles with videos and photos of her supposed baby.



She even used AI to make it look like the “baby” was moving in videos, friends previously said.

After the fake birth, Kira is said to have posted a date, time and weight of the doll dressed in a hat with a dummy in its mouth.

She then posted pictures of the doll in different outfits in carriers and pushchairs gifted to her by allegedly duped friends and family.

But days later, she is said to have lied that the make-believe child had died from a heart condition.

Kira managed to keep up the lies with the fake baby after the birth by keeping her unsuspecting family away from the doll, only allowing Jamie and herself to hold it.



Loved ones thought she was just being protective, not letting anyone touch or hold her baby as a new mum, but it is understood that eventually her ruse came to light when her mum later discovered the doll in her bedroom.

However, she said that she was worried that her lies about her baby would be exposed sooner than she thought, after family members began to become suspicious.

Younger relatives said they thought the baby was a doll during a car journey, and her family raised concerns that the baby wasn’t moving, crying, or opening her eyes.

Kira Cousins ‘pulls out of tell-all TV documentary’ about scandal KIRA was set to tell her side of the atonishing story after signing up for an explosive TV documentary with an unknown production company. But in April earlier this year, the fraudster quit the tell-all TV documentary over fears about how it would be edited. Taking to Instagram, an account linked to the shamed Scot confirmed she pulled the plug on the explosive documentary. The post stated: “Before any rumours start to circulate I would like to address this matter directly. I have taken the decision to withdraw from the documentary after discussions with the producers, as I believe this is the most appropriate out come for all involved. “While I may choose to share my story at some point in the future, I may equally decide not to. At the moment I don’t feel that this is the right time. “I acknowledge that my actions may have caused confusion or upset and have apologised privately to those most closely affected, and now online to those who it also may have caused upset and distress. “It is most important that those closest to the situation are given the time and space to heal. I am focusing on myself and prioritising the mental health of both myself and others involved, which has informed my decision. “I would also like to thank everyone who has been involved, and who has offered me support and guidance during this time. I will continue to work upon myself to be the best version I can be for myself, family and friends.” And in a grovelling apology to the man she claimed was the dad, she added: “I apologise to my ex and his family, I wish them all the best and hope this decision brings them peace. Thank you for your understanding.” At the time, Two Rivers Media and Soho Studios told The Scottish Sun: “We can confirm that we have halted our documentary project, telling the story of Kira Cousins. “After much thought, Kira has decided that she no longer wants to share her story. We have worked closely with, and supported, Kira every step of the way, in exactly the same way as we have with this decision. “We pride ourselves on our relationships with our key contributors and their wellbeing is paramount to us. We wish Kira all the best for the future.”

But Facebook posts claim that Kira said they went to the doctor to get checked out and everything was normal.



Kira also revealed that Jamie took the baby to his parents‘ home alone to meet the baby and said: “Everyone in that house saw it and none of them twigged.”

And she said that those who believed her lies should have realised earlier that the baby was actually a life-like doll.

She said: “If they didn’t, they were stupid.”

Kira was forced to tell Jamie the truth days later and said she hasn’t seen him since he “walked out” after saying, “You’re a psycho”.

But she told The Sunday Mail that the pair later spoke on the phone after the scandal came to light.



Kira said: “When I first got back in contact with Jamie after this, one of the first things I asked him was if he really knew.”

She added: “No one was near that doll except me and Jamie. So if anyone should have known, it was Jamie.”

Jamie told The Sunday Mail that he would have left Kira if he knew, or suspected, that his daughter was really a doll.

He also claimed that Kira never directly told him about the baby being a doll, and said that when he found out, it wasn’t “through her”.

Jamie also disputed claims that Kira ever tried to tell him that she had suffered a miscarriage.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “If I had ever known that was really a doll, I’d have run off sooner. I’ve not got a clue what really happened to be honest.”

He added: “I want to get as far away from her as possible. I just want to move on with my life.”

News.title: Furious locals blast £4.2m taxpayer-funded revamp of traveller site where PC Andrew Harper’s killers hid from cops
News.content:
FURIOUS locals say a £4.2million taxpayer-funded traveller site linked to the sick killers of hero PC Andrew Harper leaves a “stain” on their community.

Residents slammed the lavish and controversial upgrade this week, questioning why it was allowed to go ahead despite a raft of objections – including from cops.



The controversial site is now operational after the old one was bulldozed and redeveloped under the swanky multi-million pound council scheme following the officer’s tragic death in 2019.

Council bosses went ahead despite 50 formal objections – including from Thames Valley Police and PC Harper’s mother – arguing there was no other location for the site.



When The Sun visited this week, villagers remain up in arms – describing the site and its controversial renovation as a “stain” on their area.

It comes amid fears that two of PC Harper’s killers could soon be released from prison under the Government’s controversial early release scheme.



Though new PM Andy Burnham confirmed Henry Long will not be released early, Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole could be freed this year – something Andrew’s widow Lissie Harper branded “deplorable”.

The three teenage quad bike thieves were jailed after brave PC Harper, 28, was dragged for more than a mile behind a car while responding to the theft.



After the killing, Long, Bowers and Cole hid out for more than a month at the Four Houses Corner traveller site in Ufton Nervet, Berkshire, where they destroyed evidence before they were eventually nicked.

The rundown site was bulldozed in February 2024 ahead of West Berkshire Council approving the controversial £4.2million redevelopment.

It has since been transformed into a modern site with 17 double-berth caravan pitches, parking spaces, electric vehicle charging points and a children’s play area.

But villagers say the expensive revamp has done little to ease concerns, with some fearing Bowers and Cole could one day return if they are released.

Retired Carol Harris, 81, who has lived nearby for more than three decades, blasted: “It is a law to itself down there.



“We get mess up the lane, they fly tip on the lane when their bins overflow, which they always are. Just go down there and see for yourselves.



“The taxpayers splashed out on that camp for them and they just show no respect to it, I just despair really.”

Carol said the prospect of Bowers and Cole being released left her horrified.

She added: “To think that those evil boys could be released early from prison makes me feel sick.

“I am very worried about it and I feel so sorry for the poor police officer’s wife and family, his death has left a scar here.

“I know that they didn’t live there initially and just used it as a hideout, but who’s to say they won’t try to come back.”



Another resident, who has lived on the road for more than 40 years, said he had watched the traveller site change dramatically over the decades.

He said: “I have seen families come and go for four decades now, previously I felt families managed their own communities better. They have passed on, and then it became a bit of a free-for-all down there.

“And now we just don’t really know what is going on, they keep themselves to themselves.”



He also criticised the taxpayer-funded redevelopment.

He claimed: “The site itself is a waste of money, it is not right.

“They have pulled fences out, extended the site, and made it their own.”

However, he insisted it was important not to unfairly tar everyone living at the site with the same brush.

He added: “From a resident’s point of view though, they largely keep themselves to themselves.



“I think they probably are worried about how they are viewed by the local community.

“I think it would be a good step forward for the local community if we had more of an open relationship.

“As long as they behave themselves and are polite, then I have no issues.



“I think as well it is fair to say that they are scapegoated, a shed gets broken into or something gets broken and everyone always immediately just assumes who was accountable. And that probably is unfair.”

A woman who moved to the road around 10 years ago said she remembered the aftermath of PC Harper’s death.

She said: “They [the travellers] have always been there. So when we moved here we knew the travellers were close.

“It was a really rough time when the police officer was killed. I remember the police coming to ask for CCTV which we didn’t have.

“The thing that was disappointing for us was that the police put in a letter to the council to explain they felt it was a bad idea to redo the traveller site there but they went ahead regardless, that was the bit we found confusing.



“Surely if the police have concerns that should be the biggest concern.”

She also questioned whether the redevelopment represented value for taxpayers.

She added: “The council seemed willing to spend £4m of tax payers money, surely there are more pressing things that the money could have been spent on, filling pot holes for starters.”

Despite her apprehensions, she said relations with the travelling community had largely been peaceful.

She said: “Anyway the new site is there now, the travelling community have always been here and we know that and there is nothing we can do about it.



“We had one incident where a young lad fired a stone at my car window and smashed it, besides that there has been no bother from them.”

Pensioner Colette, who has lived in the village for 46 years, said she believed the millions spent on the redevelopment should have gone elsewhere.

She said: “I think the mood of the whole village and country is the same. It is disgraceful that the killer could be released early.



“Instead of giving us £45 a year on fuel, we don’t need that money, why don’t they build more prisons. That site cost millions.”

She added: “The main issues on the doorstep relate to rubbish though, it gets dumped on the lane all the time.”

Another local said his biggest concern remained the cost of the development.

He said: “My main gripe though is that the plans went ahead to build it in the first place, it cost a fortune, and is that really money well spent?

“This is a really scenic and pretty area, with beautiful countryside, yet the traveller site is a stain really.”



Their fears come as fresh concerns have been raised over the possible release of Bowers and Cole later this year.

The pair, who were both 17 when PC Harper was killed, are eligible for release halfway through their 13-year sentences under the Ministry of Justice’s controversial early release scheme.

Long, who drove the Seat Toledo that dragged the 28-year-old officer for more than a mile, is not eligible and will only be able to seek parole after serving half of his 16-year sentence.

A former prison officer who dealt with Cole and Bowers said the pair showed “no remorse” after the killing and even mocked PC Harper’s widow, Lissie Harper.

He claimed: “I saw their behaviour first-hand. They thought the whole thing was a joke and had no respect for PC Harper or his widow.”



The former officer also alleged the pair laughed and joked throughout proceedings and openly discussed blaming Long for the death, adding they were “the last” prisoners who should be considered for early release.

However, West Berkshire Council defended the redevelopment.

A spokesperson said: “Four Houses Corner Caravan Site has been a formal traveller’s site for many years. This site has been redeveloped and operational since September and provides important homes for the Gypsy and Traveller community.



“We need to deliver traveller accommodation and ensure we meet legal requirements. Suitable alternative sites do not exist in West Berkshire.

“Since the site re-opened, no specific concerns regarding site management have been raised directly with the council.

“The council have also not received any complaints or reports regarding animal welfare or illegal dog breeding.

“The site is managed by our Traveller Liaison Officer and council officers are on site every week.

“The redevelopment scheme which received planning permission is what has been implemented, including the boundary fences to the site.



“There have been no additional pitches created, and no additional residents have moved into the site. We are aware of a previous issue relating to a fence panel, which has since been resolved.

“Since the site re-opened, we have been working closely with tenants, local residents, the local community and partner organisations to support the successful and smooth running of the site.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’re confident the arrangements we have in place are appropriate and will keep these under review to ensure they remain so.”

The Sun approached the travellers for comment, but they simply asked our reporter to leave.

News.title: Gatwick Airport left without running water with 'no flushing toilets or drinks'
News.content:
Gatwick Airport left without running water with 'no flushing toilets or drinks'

Gatwick Airport is facing water supply problems at both terminals

View Image Gatwick Airport is facing a water shortage (Image: UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Gatwick Airport has been left without running water across both terminals.

‌



Travellers have reported issues with flushing toilets due to the shortage. People are also struggling to get tea or coffee at the airport.

‌



Gatwick said it is giving bottled water to passengers and staff.

‌



The shortage is understood to have come following an issue at SES Water's Bough Beech Water Treatment Works. The firm said earlier that some customers were experiencing water shortages

Gatwick Airport said: "A water issue in the Horley area is causing disruption at the airport this morning. The problem is affecting water supply in both terminals and is currently under investigation.

‌



"Bottled water is being made available to passengers and staff across the airport and other contingency measures are being put in place to ensure the welfare of our passengers.

"We will provide further updates and apologise for any inconvenience to passengers."

It remains unclear when the water shortage will be resovled.

News.title: Berlin Pride crash updates: Police hunt suspect Abdul Ballout as van hits crowd killing 1
News.content:
An image of the vehicle after the crash

Police in Berlin say a major manhunt is underway after a white minivan ploughed into a crowd of people in the Tiergarten park around 10pm on Saturday night

One person has died and 16 more have been injured after a v ehicle drove into the crowd during a Pride event in Berlin, with the suspect fleeing the scene.

At around 10pm on Saturday night, a white minivan drove at speed into a group of people in the city centre's Tiergarten park during the annual Pride event, also known as Christopher Street Day.

Witnesses said they saw a vehicle driving "very quickly" into the crowd and heard screams as people ran. Police spokesman Florian Nath told reporters that witnesses also reported people lying on the ground with stab wounds.

Berlin Pride was cancelled with attendees told to “evacuate" immediately. Police named the suspect as 21-year-old Abdul B, who is "associated with the Islamist scene", and a major manhunt is underway.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed to "make sure this horrific act is fully investigated and punished".

News.title: DJ Fat Tony wades back into Brooklyn Beckham's bitter feud with parents David and Victoria
News.content:
DJ Fat Tony wades back into Brooklyn Beckham's bitter feud with parents David and Victoria

DJ Fat Tony wades back into Brooklyn Beckham's feud with David and Victoria

View 4 Images Brooklyn Beckham publicly called out his parents in a scathing statement (Image: Samir Hussein/WireImage)

DJ Fat Tony has urged fans not to judge the Beckham family over their ongoing feud, as he stepped back into the drama.

‌



The 60-year-old has been a longtime friend of Victoria and David Beckham, and has been on hand to perform at many of their events over the years - including Brooklyn’s wedding to wife Nicola Peltz in 2022.

‌



Following the nuptials, the budding photographer distanced himself from his loved ones and publicly called out his parents, claiming that they were controlling, and that his mum behaved inappropriately on their big day.

‌



Rehashing the fall-out in a new interview about his career, the acclaimed DJ reflected on his now infamous stint behind the decks at the ceremony, and the subsequent headlines.

View 4 Images DJ Fat Tony has rehashed the drama (Image: ITV)

“I've been blessed to work at some amazing events, including Brooklyn Beckham's wedding where I DJ'd for three days,” he told the Times.

‌



“Before judging, people should remember that two parents have lost their first-born son and a son has lost his parents.

“All families have dramas, but they just happen to be the Beckhams, and once that story came out - sparked by Stav making a comment on an Instagram post about how Victoria was dancing - I got dozens of interview requests from media all over the world, including a personal call from Piers Morgan, which I turned down.”

This isn’t the first time that the musician, real name Tony Marnach, has spoken about the rift as he previously shared his insight while appearing on This Morning.

‌



"It's always sad when there's a rift in any family. It just so happened that I got dragged into one," he later told Hello Magazine. "[The Beckham family] are incredible and [David and Victoria] brought up those kids impeccably.

"They are who they are; they're an amazing PR machine, they do wonderful things and I've just gone in a different direction. I love Brooklyn, I love Nicola. I see Romeo all the time, he's always around. He's doing incredibly. He's just dropped his new clothing range, so it's amazing. They're all doing well, and Cruz."

View 4 Images Things became strained after Brooklyn and Nicola's wedding (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Brooklyn has been locked in a bitter feud with his family in recent months after slamming Victoria and David in a scathing six-page statement in January, branding them “performative”.

Discussing his wedding with Nicola, he fumed at the time: “My mum hijacked my first dance with my wife, which had been planned weeks in advance to a romantic love song.

“In front of our 500 wedding guests, Marc Anthony called me to the stage, where in the schedule was planned to be my romantic dance with my wife but instead my mum was waiting to dance with me instead. She danced very inappropriately on me in front of everyone.

‌



“I've never felt more uncomfortable or humiliated in my entire life. We wanted to renew our vows so we could create new memories of our wedding day that bring us joy and happiness, not anxiety and embarrassment.”

View 4 Images The rest of the family have put on a united front (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Despite David and Victoria making several attempts to publicly extend an olive branch to their son, and including him in their social media posts for milestone birthdays, anniversaries and holidays, he has continued to ignore their gestures.

‌



The Spice Girls icon was previously questioned about the drama in a candid interview with the Wall Street Journal and, although she didn’t mention her eldest son’s name, she insisted: “We love our children so much. We've always tried to be the best parents that we can be.

"And you know, we've been in the public eye for more than 30 years right now, and all we've ever tried to do is protect our children and love our children. And you know, that's all I really want to say about it."

When asked if she had any remorse about bringing her family into the spotlight, she added: "I wouldn’t say it comes with guilt, I’d say that there was a lot of adjusting from my mum and dad, when all of a sudden there were paparazzi outside their house. We’ve really taken our families on this ride with us."

News.title: Teacher, husband and six kids found dead in potential 'murder-suicide' house fire
News.content:
Teacher, husband and six kids found dead in potential 'murder-suicide' house fire

The deaths of a teacher, her husband and their six kids, aged five to 15, following a Michigan house fire are being probed as a possible murder-suicide

View 5 Images Police at the scene in Grand Haven Township, Michigan (Image: Joel Bissell/Kalamazoo Gazette v)

Police are probing the deaths of eight family members, including six children, following a Michigan house fire which is being treated as a possible murder-suicide.

‌



Amanda 'Mandy' Karolkiewicz, 39, her husband Kristopher, 47, and their six children, aged five to 15, were discovered inside their home in Grand Haven Township at around noon on Friday around noon, Mandy's family said.

‌



Police in Ottawa have not yet formally identified all the victims and do not have an official cause of death for them, Capt. Jacob Sparks of the Ottawa County Sheriff's Office said in a press conference on Saturday.

‌



Some of the victims had gunshot wounds, NBC reports.

View 5 Images Amanda and Kristopher Karolkiewicz (Image: facebook/kkarolkiewicz)

Healthy baby suddenly dies just hours after nurse told mum he was 'thriving' READ MORE :

The incident is being investigated as a possible murder-suicide and officers are not looking for any outside suspects, Sparks said.

‌



Mandy's sister, Molly Cessna, wrote on Facebook alongside an article about the shocking deaths: "My little sister Mandy, her husband, and my six nieces and nephews."

She added: "Everything's just blurry. Please continue to pray, friends. please continue to pray as we try and piece everything together. Our hearts are utterly shattered. Tragic doesn't even touch it."

View 5 Images The family lived in Grand Haven Township (Image: Google Maps)

‌



Mandy's parents, Steve and Becky Lawwill, also shared a smiling family photo on the beach alongside a short tribute.

"So grateful for the joy they brought into our life. We are just so shattered," the pair wrote.

Mandy, a substitute teacher at Grand Haven Area Public Schools, had been married to her husband for around 16 years, according to his social media.

‌



View 5 Images Amanda Karolkiewicz worked as a substitute teacher (Image: GrandHavenAreaPS/Facebook)

The district said in a review posted in January that she "goes above and beyond" for students at Peach Plains Elementary School.

Superintendent Kristin Perowski said in a statement on Friday evening that support and mental health resources would be offered to the school community.

‌



A caption alongside a photo on Kristopher and his wife on Facebook, shared in 2019, said: "Going on 10 years with this pretty lady. I'm a very lucky guy."

View 5 Images Eight people, including six children, have died in the fire (Image: Joel Bissell/Kalamazoo Gazette v)

Capt. Jacob Sparks described the scene as "complicated" during yesterday's news conference.

Article continues below

He added that the fire was "suspicious" and that there was reason to believe it was intentionally set.

Firefighters swarmed the area on the morning of the a smell of smoke was reported between 8:30am and 9am.

An investigation into the fire remains ongoing.

News.title: Girl, 17, fighting for her life after e-scooter crash in Liverpool city centre
News.content:
Girl, 17, fighting for her life after e-scooter crash in Liverpool city centre

A teenage girl is fighting for her life in hospital following a collision involving an e-scooter and a car in Liverpool city centre

View 2 Images The crash occurred in the early hours of this morning (Image: Liverpool Echo)

A 17-year-old girl is fighting for her life after a crash in Liverpool city centre in the early hours of this morning.

Merseyside Police received a report that two 17-year-old girls riding an e-scooter had been involved in a collision with a Mercedes Vito on Great George Street at around 1.20am.

Emergency services attended the scene, and one of the girls was taken to hospital where she remains in a critical condition.

The second teenager was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving, drug driving, and driving without insurance, Liverpool Echo reports.

Police said the driver of the Mercedes Vito failed to stop at the scene, but following enquiries the vehicle was located nearby, and a 57-year-old man from Liverpool was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and failing to stop.

View 2 Images The second teenager was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Detective Sergeant Simon Duffy from the Matrix Serious Collision Investigation Unit said: “This was a very serious collision that has resulted in a young girl in hospital where she is currently in a critical condition.

“As part of our initial inquiries, we have arrested two people, and they both remain in custody, where they will be questioned about their possible involvement.

“In the meantime, I'd like to take this opportunity to appeal to any possible witnesses.

"We know this happened very early this morning, but if anyone saw what occurred or were driving through the area just before the incident, then please get in touch.

“I would also ask anyone who travelled through other parts of the city and saw two girls on an e-scooter to let us know.

“Similarly, if you live or work in the area and have CCTV or smart doorbell footage, please take a moment to review to see if you captured anything that could assist our investigation.

"Even the smallest of details could be vital, so please don’t hesitate to get in touch and let our team review your footage.”

Anyone who witnessed the collision or captured the incident on CCTV or dashcam is asked to contact the SCIU on (0151) 777 5747, or email SCIU@merseyside.police.uk quoting incident reference 072 of 26 July.

The Duchess of Sussex, 44, was seen giving tips to aspiring cooks on the hit TV show, alongside judges Poh Ling Yeow, Sofia Levin and Jean-Christophe Novelli.

Her appearance was a surprise to the contestants, who stood either side to applaud her as she entered the studio. The episode was filmed during Meghan's visit to Australia with Prince Harry in April. But Meghan had her own suprise when Harry joined in the show via live videolink.

News.title: New Chancellor John Healey promises 'buy British' blitz in government overhaul
News.content:
New Chancellor John Healey promises 'buy British' blitz in government overhaul

New Chancellor John Healey has ordered government departments to 'buy British', promising a focus on UK goods and services on a sclae

View 2 Images Chancellor John Healey has promised an overhaul of the way contracts are awarded (Image: Getty Images)

Government departments have been ordered to "buy British", Chancellor John Healey has said in an overhaul of procurement rules.

‌



Former Defence Secretary Mr Healey said every pound spent will support British jobs. He promised that under his watch there would be a "determined drive" to focus on UK goods and services on a scale never seen before.

‌



The Treasury chief - who was Andy Burnham's first appointment when he became Prime Minister on Monday - said he wants to roll out the ethos he had at the Ministry of Defence (MOD) across government.

‌



View 2 Images Mr Healey and Andy Burnham have announced a string of measures including support for pubs in their first week (Image: Richard Pohle/The Times/PA Wire)

Mr Healey said: "You will see this as a determined drive that you have not seen before from a British government. Buying British not 'if possible', but by design. So every procurement pound supports British jobs, British apprenticeships and British skills."

In an interview with The Sun, he pointed out that when he was Defence Secretary. over 86% of the 1,200 major defence contracts handed out went to British firms.

‌



He said: “I am as concerned about the cost of business as I am the cost of living. I am really concerned that where we make government policy and government decisions, these can help raise the levels of investment, innovation and profit in British business.”

In their first week in government, Mr Burnham and Mr Healey announced an end to VAT on household electricity bills and a £2 bus fare cap across England, outside London. They also announced plans to slash business rates for pubs and small music venues by 20% in a major boost for the struggling sector.

Asked where the money will come from, he said: "Fiscal credibility is the bedrock of economic stability. Both Andy and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules and ensure we have got a buffer against uncertainty."

‌



The Chancellor will set out his first Budget in the autumn after replacing Rachel Reeves, who returned to the backbenches at the start of the week. One of his major challenges will be to find £5billion to fund extra spending in the defence investment plan (DIP).

The government is yet to set a timetable for reaching 3% of the UK's gross domestic product (GDP) on defending the nation. Mr Healey told the Sun this was "not a matter for this first week".

Mr Burnham has vowed to build a country where "nobody is written off" and everyone is treated with respect. The new PM swooped into power on Monday, and immediately moved to cut business rates for pubs, bring in a £2 cap on bus fares, and slash VAT on energy bills.

Article continues below

In a pledge to go further, the former Greater Manchester Mayor claimed he was used to being told things can't be done, and that the era of Government's giving up trying to solve the issues impacting people was over.

Writing for The Mirror, Mr Burnham claimed this week had shown how politicians could make lives a "little bit easier", but that his job won't be done until people aren't just living, but "living well'.

Sukanya Thawichokkamthon, 30, was reportedly discovered by a fisherman, with her body lodged on a raft on the River Kwai in Thailand. An investigation has now been launched.

News.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
News.content:
Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."

Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".

The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor John Healey resigned from the previous government saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.

But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that.

"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

News.title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
News.content:
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, Andy Burnham explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election, saying "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it."

Explaining his decision, the new prime minister suggested the majority of the electorate "voted for a manifesto" in the last election, and vowed he would "honour that manifesto" with the support of parliamentary colleagues.

Burnham went on to say, "I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working."

Andy Burnham: The Laura Kuenssberg Interview will be available across BBC News on Sunday and the interview will be shown in full on Panorama on BBC One on Monday at 20:00 BST.

News.title: Iran's 'sabre-rattling' should not intimidate UK, Wes Streeting says
News.content:
When asked if Iran had the capability to attack the UK, Streeting said: "I think we shouldn't put too much stock in the sabre-rattling of Iran, and we certainly shouldn't be intimidated by what the regime has said this week".

He also repeated the UK's position from the outset of the US war against Iran saying "we have not joined and will not join offensive US military action in Iran.

"That's an area where we have not agreed with the United States, but when it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the straight Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned".

Streeting said he is to meet with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in the coming week after "kicking around" ideas for ways "to bring the countries together" and had been "delighted" to speak to Hegseth by phone already.

He also said that the UK is ready to lead a naval mission to help remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz "when the conditions are right".

Securing safe shipping routes through the area was important because of the impact the crisis is having on energy prices and the cost of living, he added.

Streeting also dismissed a Russian warship's recent live-firing exercise in the English Channel as "performative" but added it was a "reminder of the frankly unsafe and unprofessional way in which they have been conducting themselves".

Branding the Channel incident "irresponsible", Streeting said Russia posed a threat to UK security, adding that the public does not see "the enormous efforts that take place every day to counter Russian aggression".

News.title: Pizza, pasta, potatoes, protein - how Italian children became so overweight
News.content:
Daily life is not easy for Salvatore. At 17, he weighs 170kg (26st 10lb) and struggles to walk.

He can't tie his own shoelaces and his Vespa scooter strains to bear his weight - in one week, its wheels broke seven times.

"He eats constantly," says his mother Anna.

Salvatore is among a growing number of Italian children and teenagers living with obesity. The problem is particularly acute in the south: in parts of the Campania region, more than 40% of eight and nine-year-olds are overweight. The town of Ponticelli, on the outskirts of Naples, has earned the unenviable reputation as one of the world's child obesity capitals.

It is a striking development in a country long regarded as the spiritual home of the Mediterranean diet. Yet today, Italian children are among the most overweight in Europe, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Salvatore is waiting for life-changing surgery at the Betania Hospital in Ponticelli, where Dr Sonja Chiappetta has spent 15 years treating patients with severe obesity.

Until recently, she says, most of her patients were in their fifties. "Now I see those same patients when they're teenagers, as young as 16. They are getting younger, and it's frightening."

The surgery she carries out removes up to 90% of the stomach - meaning people are unable to eat large quantities of food. Demand has risen sharply in this part of Italy.

But Salvatore has been told he cannot get the operation. His weight is so excessive it makes the surgery too dangerous.

Instead, Dr Chiappetta has prescribed him a GLP-1 weight-loss injection to reduce his appetite and help him lose enough weight for the operation.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty in tears after missing out on gold again
News.content:
After tears in Paris, tears again in Glasgow.

It leaves even the great Adam Ramsay-Peaty wondering how much of this is worth it.

"I work a lot harder than what it says on the scoreboard," the Englishman said after taking 100m breaststroke bronze at the Commonwealth Games, his eyes and cheeks red with emotion.

"It hurts too much. I have got to approach training differently now because it hurts too much."

Ramsay-Peaty has done it all in this sport.

Three Olympic gold medals. Eight world titles. The 14 fastest times in history.

But after taking a break from swimming amid a wave of mental health issues in 2023, he is still searching for that winning feeling again on the big stage.

He was pipped to Olympic gold in Paris two years ago. In Glasgow, despite coming into the final as the fastest qualifier, he had to settle for bronze.

He was beaten by Australia's Sam Williamson but also Jersey's history-maker Filip Nowacki, the 18-year-old he has taken under his wing.

Ramsay-Peaty was third at halfway and could not close the gap. His time - 59.65 seconds - was more than four-tenths slower than his semi-final swim and three seconds off his personal best from seven years ago.

"It took a lot of courage to get back into the sport, so we should be happy with everything we get, but then that contradicts the athlete inside me and what I work for," he said.

"I just think I deserve more. I know sport isn't about what you deserve or even what you work for - it's who gets it on the day.

"I just know I'm a better athlete than that. It's very disappointing."

Ramsay-Peaty has spoken about the difficult decisions that come with being an elite athlete. The time away from his son, whom he held in his arms after the Paris silver. The events at home he has to miss.

"They are not even sacrifices; they are choices," he said.

"It's like getting knocked out in the group stages in the World Cup for a very good team. You know you're better and it hurts because you know you have to wait for a very long time for the next championships.

"This is probably - realistically - my last Commonwealth Games and I thought I'd trained for better. I could do better. I've been faster this season. That's where the frustration is."

News.title: I thought the Lockerbie bombing was a closed case until I started asking questions
News.content:
I was only a year old when the UK's deadliest terror attack shocked the world.

In December 1988, Pan Am flight 103 exploded - killing all 259 people on board as well as 11 on the ground in the Scottish town of Lockerbie.

I was a teenager by the time Libyan intelligence officer Abdelbaset al-Megrahi was convicted of the bombing in 2001 and, when he later died, I thought that was largely the end of the story.

It wasn't.

The case still rumbles on and, later this year, a man suspected of making the bomb which blew up the plane, Abu Agila Masud, goes on trial in Washington DC.

As part of a Radio 4 Intrigue podcast series, I had an opportunity to delve into this complex case with fresh eyes.

The deeper I dug, the more complicated Lockerbie became and there have been times that I don't know what to believe.

News.title: What Love Island tells us about the changing face of dating
News.content:
On the fourth series of Love Island UK in 2018, Megan Barton-Hanson pulled fellow Islander, Wes Nelson, for a chat.

Just moments earlier, she had ended her relationship with Eyal Booker after admitting the pair had little more than physical chemistry. Now, sitting opposite Wes, who had been coupled up with Laura Anderson since the start of the competition, she decided not to wait for him to make the first move.

"I think it's pretty obvious that I do really fancy you," she told him. "And I just felt like, if I didn't say something, I'd regret it massively."

By the end of the episode, viewers had a new nickname for her: "Muggy Megan". Critics accused her of moving too quickly between relationships and breaking "girl code". Others admired her honesty.

At the time, Barton-Hanson argued that she had been treated differently to her male counterparts. "People definitely do give girls a harder time than menâ¦ It's sexist."

But eight years later, scenes like Barton-Hanson's no longer feel quite so out of the ordinary. Until this series, the opening coupling had always seen the men choose first. This year, the show's rules were changed, with the women making the first choice.

News.title: Primark's new 'supermarket tactic' to woo customers in online price war
News.content:
"Primark isn't as cheap any more."

It is something I keep hearing shoppers say when I ask them whether they shop at the fast-fashion giant.

"It's definitely got more expensive," says 19-year-old student Eshal Malik as she browses the jewellery at Primark with a friend.

But that might be about to change. Primark said on Monday that it was lowering prices on hundreds of clothing items, including jeans, jumpers and socks.

"It's the kind of headline you'd expect from M&S or Next," says retail analyst Natalie Berg, explaining that price cuts like this from such a low-cost retailer are surprising.

"You don't want to join a race to the bottom," she says. "But when Shein is selling dresses for Â£3, you've got to respond, right?"

Primark, which has more than 190 UK stores, has been experiencing a drop in like-for-like sales, a key measure in the retail industry.

Increases to the price of fabric, minimum wages, shipping and energy costs and a focus on higher standards overall has contributed to the rising price of clothes for the likes of Primark in recent years.

The announcement of price cuts comes ahead of parent company Associated British Foods' plan to spin off the business onto the London stock market next year.

The level of competition among fashion retailers has "evolved dramatically" over the past few years, and Chinese online marketplaces Shein and Temu are now competing for Primark's customers, says Berg.

But there is also competition from other online retailers like TikTok Shop and Vinted, she says.

By slashing prices on some core items, Primark is likely hoping to woo shoppers with low-cost staples, in the same way that supermarkets attract customers with cheap milk and bananas, Berg says.

News.title: Another UK heatwave looms after cooler end to weekend
News.content:
Sunday will be a cooler day for all of the UK as it begins cloudy with a little bit of rain for southern and eastern areas.

As temperatures fall widely by a couple of degrees, a few locations will finally mark the end to their third heatwave of the year, including Usk in Monmouthshire and Exeter in Devon.

Both places are forecast to see temperatures drop beneath the heatwave threshold for the first time in 21 consecutive days.

A breezier and fresher day for all, temperatures will largely be in the mid-20s Celsius for the south-east of the UK and in the mid-teens Celsius further north.

For many, the relief from the heat will be short-lived as high pressure is set to build close to the south of the UK next week.

This will stall rain-bearing weather fronts and any wet weather will become confined to northern and western areas - especially north-west Scotland.

In southern parts of the UK, temperatures look set to climb once again.

Tapping into the heat over the near continent, the UK is likely to enter another heatwave, with temperatures in England and Wales likely to peak around 25-32C for much of next week.

News.title: What a week's work experience taught these Year 10s about their futures
News.content:
When Kelsey first arrived at secondary school, she said she wanted to be almost anywhere else but there.

She struggled with friendships, clashed with teachers and often tried to avoid coming into school.

But after a week's work experience placement at Whipsnade Zoo, in Bedfordshire, her outlook could not be more different.

She said it made her a "completely different person" - more confident, with a "good group of friends" and a greater sense of purpose about where her education could lead her.

Children across the UK are strongly encouraged to do work experience while at school. In England, the government published new legal guidance in June for schools to deliver two weeks of "in-person and immersive" work experience in future, one between Year 7 and Year 9, and one between Years 10 and 11.

But not all work experience placements are equal, and finding the right one can be tricky.

Organisations like the Sutton Trust and the Social Mobility Foundation said some students could be limited by the availability of placements in their area, or a lack of family connections with local employers.

BBC News spoke to three Year 10 pupils, one year ahead of their final GCSE exams, about how they decided what areas of work they were interested in, their experiences of trying to find the right placement, and what it taught them about their future education and ultimate career goals.

News.title: Residents allowed to return after Cairngorms wildfire evacuation
News.content:
Residents of the village of Nethy Bridge, near the wildfire that has been burning in the Cairngorms, have been told they can return to their homes after being evacuated on Friday night.

The fire was declared a major incident due to a change in weather, but that has now been stood down by Police Scotland.

First Minister John Swinney said the government and emergency services will continue to treat the blaze with the utmost seriousness until the last flames are out.

Locals have criticised the handling of the wildfire, which has been burning for 10 days, saying the move to declare it a major incident came too late and the government had been slow in scaling up their response.

In a statement on Saturday night, Police Scotland said "after an extensive multi-agency response to a large fire within Cairngorms National Park, residents of Nethy Bridge are being advised that they can now return to their properties".

Police Scotland's deputy assistant chief officer, Kenny Barbour, said the decision to stand down the major incident followed a detailed assessment by emergency responders.

He added in a statement: "The extensive work carried out over recent days, including the creation of effective fire breaks, has significantly reduced the risk to nearby communities, allowing evacuated residents to safely return home."

Supt Judy Hill added that the "ongoing multi agency response remains a high priority, with significant partnership resources and volunteers working tirelessly and in challenging circumstances, to support our efforts to extinguish the fires".

Firefighters will continue to maintain a significant operational presence until the incident is safely concluded, with 75 remaining on the ground on Saturday, police said.

At a meeting of the Scottish government's resilience room on Saturday evening, the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said there had been "good progress" in strengthening fire breaks to protect residential areas and said the number of fire hot spots was reducing.

First Minister John Swinney welcomed the lifting of the evacuation notice but stressed that "the Scottish Government, the emergency services and all relevant authorities will continue to treat this wildfire, as has been the case since its onset, with the utmost seriousness and necessary resources until the last flames are out."

News.title: Police investigate donations by Tice company to Reform UK
News.content:
Police are investigating payments to Reform UK by a company controlled by the party's deputy leader, Richard Tice, BBC News has learned.

Britain Means Business gave the party two donations of Â£250,000 in the run-up to the 2024 general election, when Tice was party chairman.

Tice has said the money was given to his firm by Fiona Cottrell, a significant donor to Reform UK and mother of a convicted fraudster with close links to Nigel Farage.

Tice said: "This is the first I have heard of it - if true why are the Met Police briefing the BBC before contacting interested parties? Is the Met leadership now engaged in the widespread politically motivated smear campaign against Reform and its leaders?"

Earlier this month, the Times newspaper, external revealed that two donations given directly by Fiona Cottrell to Reform UK in May 2024 were being investigated by the Metropolitan Police.

That investigation relates to legislation governing elections, which bans concealing or disguising donations derived from an "impermissible" donor, or the use of "false" information about a donation including the amount or the identity of the donor.

The BBC has asked Fiona Cottrell for comment.

News.title: Man in critical condition after sea rescue
News.content:
A man is in a critical condition in hospital after three people got into difficulty in the water near an Essex pier.

Emergency services were called to an incident at Clacton-on-Sea shortly after 16:30 BST on Saturday.

A man aged in his 50s is in a critical but stable condition, Essex Police said.

Two other people, a man aged in his 20s and a teenage girl, remain in hospital but are "recovering well", the force added.

All three people knew each other.

News.title: 'It was like a movie - I looked up and an exploded barn rained on me'
News.content:
The photographer was driving to his studio for a meeting when he realised the fire on the horizon was at the farm where it was based.

"It was about 150 metres (492ft) from my front door, and I quickly cancelled the meeting and thought, 'I'm not happy with where the wind is going on this'," he said.

Johnson began removing some of his more expensive kit from the studio and was putting it in the van when the explosion took place.

A unit housing fertiliser had exploded.

He said: "It blew me into the door and I just ran to the van, dropped the bit I went back in for - maybe it saved my life, I don't know."

As it happened: Twenty firefighters taken to hospital after major Essex explosion

The photographer was shocked to see his studio roof had completely caved in.

Having driven to a safe distance, "I pulled over, and I was just in shock and started to shake", he said, although he was reassured after an ambulance crew checked him over.

Johnson managed to cover his wedding booking on Saturday, praising his "amazing assistant" James Musselwhite for driving from Portsmouth to help him out.

"I'm in a little bit of shock still, to be honest," he said.

"I'm completely unscathed apart from a bit of a dodgy ear from the pressure - but how I've got away with it unscathed I have no idea."

News.title: Tourists describe their escape from France wildfires
News.content:
Families have relived how their tranquil holidays in France turned into a race to escape raging wildfires.

Tourists told the BBC of emergency alerts in the middle of the night, desperate drives just metres from six-storey high flames and the sight of people flocking to beaches with their suitcases.

Huge forest fires in south-west France and central Spain have displaced more than 220,000 people, with the French military drafted in to help and the Spanish government declaring a national emergency.

Winds and continued heat are still helping to fan the flames with some tourists reporting smelling acrid smoke like a "bonfire" far outside the affected areas.

Flights to Bordeaux and Madrid, the closest cities to the blaze-hit regions, are currently not affected. Earlier on Saturday, a French foreign minister described the fires as a "tragedy" but urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans.

Among those caught up in the crisis is Zac Morrison, who arrived in Cap Ferret - a popular peninsula blanketed with pine trees 40 miles (65km) south-west of Bordeaux - on Thursday.

The 21-year-old from London, who is on holiday with 10 members of his family, woke up to two text alerts at 04:00 and 06:00 local time ordering him to evacuate "by all means necessary".

News.title: Man charged with possession of explosive substance after bomb found in car
News.content:
A Dublin museum employee has been charged in connection with an investigation into the discovery of a bomb in a car in the Republic of Ireland.

Simon O'Donovan, 44, with an address at Sperrin Road in Dublin 12, was charged with being in possession of an explosive substance at St Lawrence Rd in Chapelizod, Dublin 10 on 22 July.

He appeared before the Special Criminal Court on Saturday evening, where the court heard he was employed by the Collins Barracks National Museum of Ireland.

A vehicle was stopped on the N2 near Carrickmacross near the Irish border on Wednesday. On Friday, a 25-year-old woman was charged in relation to the same incident.

Errol Spence Jr has confirmed that he will retire from boxing after the former world welterweight champion lost his comeback fight to Tim Tszyu.

Spence, 36, had not fought since losing the WBA, WBC and IBF belts to Terence Crawford three years ago, snatching away his zero as well as his titles after being undefeated in 28 previous fights.

The American returned to action in Sydney but came up short against Tszyu, who had Spence on the back foot throughout the bout.

Tszyu won 118-110, 117-111, 117-111 on the scorecards and Spence Jr assured that result spelled the end of his career in the ring.

"I think yeah, for sure," Spence said when asked if this was the end of the road.

"I've got my faculties intact. My money is good at working for itself. Everything's good, man.

"I've got a beautiful family, and I thank God I'm gracious to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family still by my side."

Spence won his first world title in 2017 when he stopped British fighter Kell Brook at Bramall Lane in the 11th round.

open image in gallery Tim Tszyu wants a title shot after beating Errol Spence Jr ( Getty )

But there would be no joy against a hometown hero this time, with Sydney-born Tszyu never looking particularly in danger against Spence as he grew in confidence.

The 31-year-old Australian now wants a title shot of his own.

After years of speculation, Ryan Gosling will officially be taking over the flaming helmet and fiery motorbike of Ghost Rider.

Amid a flurry of news for Marvel fans at Comic-Con this week – including a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer and Black Panther casting announcement – it was also announced on Saturday (25 July) that Gosling will be joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

The Barbie actor, 45, will play supernatural horror hero Johnny Blaze, aka Ghost Rider, in a forthcoming film directed by Deadpool & Wolverine’s Shawn Levy. The character was previously portrayed by Nicolas Cage in a 2007 film co-starring Eva Mendes, who is now married to Gosling.

The big reveal was met with huge applause from fans at Comic-Con in San Diego, and follows years of deliberation with several actors throwing their hat in the ring.

“Wow, is this really happening?” said Gosling on stage. “OK… As you know this is a character I’ve wanted to play for a very long time so Kevin [Feige, Marvel boss], Josh Horowitz, Hall H, thank you.” The film is scheduled for a theatrical release in 2028.

Gosling revealed his ambitions to play the character in 2022 during an appearance on Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast.

News of his casting will be welcomed by many, but some will be disappointed to learn that the role did not go to Norman Reedus who has long campaigned to play the part.

open image in gallery ‘The Walking Dead’ star Norman Reedus also threw his hat in the ring ( AFP/Getty )

The Walking Dead star became a fan-favourite choice for the role after he first expressed interest in the character in 2016.

Marvel boss Kevin Feige, however, seemed to reject the suggestion of Reedus as early as 2022 when he was asked for his thoughts on who should play Ghost Rider following Gosling’s interview.

“Hey man, if Ryan wants to be Ghost Rider…” Feige said at the time, going on to ask the interviewer who else wants to play the role, to which the reporter responded that Reedus famously has his eye on the character.

open image in gallery Ryan Gosling revealing himself as Ghost Rider at Comic-Con 2026 ( Getty )

After naming Reedus, the interviewer asked Feige what he thinks, to which Feige replied: “... Gosling is unbelievable.”

He went on to say: “Ryan is amazing. I’d love to find a place for him in the MCU. He’s dressed up as Ken on Venice Beach and gets more press than giant movies coming out that weekend, it’s amazing.”

In 2022, photos of Gosling and Margot Robbie rollerblading on Venice Beach went viral. The two stars were in character as Barbie and Ken for Greta Gerwig’s blockbuster hit Barbie.

Elsewhere at Comic-Con, Marvel fans got a better look at Avengers: Doomsday in a new trailer that many praised as “50 bazillion times better” than the first clip that debuted earlier this week.

British actor David Jonsson was also unmasked as the new Black Panther in the forthcoming third entry of the franchise, in which he will play the son of Chadwick Boseman’s T’Challa.
