Rob Clancy lit up every room he entered. The 29-year-old’s big and bubbly personality left a mark on all his friends.

“He was the funniest guy,” Rob’s best friend Dean Perryman says fondly. “He was the life and soul of every get together.”

Rob’s death by suicide, in November 2025, left Dean grappling with profound guilt as he struggled to come to terms with the loss of his best friend, wishing he could have done something to help.

Statistics show suicide is the leading cause of death in young people under the age of 35 in the UK. In 2023, 1,840 young people under the age of 35 died by suicide in the UK – around five young people every day.

open image in gallery Rob Clancy, left, and Dean Perryman, right ( Dean Perryman/Supplied )

“The more you learn about suicide and the more people you talk to who know those who have taken their own lives, Rob’s story is a really typical one,” Dean explains.

“He was the life and soul of every get-together. It was really shocking to everyone around him that someone who had such a big personality and was so fun, bubbly, kind, and caring could be in such a negative headspace and not have the confidence to share it.”

As Dean attempted to process his grief at losing Rob, he set himself a personal challenge. A month after Rob’s death he went to the pub every day with the aim of having one or two conversations to help him open up about his feelings, but also provide an opportunity for others to talk to him, if they needed.

It took just one trip to realise that what he was doing could ease someone else’s pain too. “I thought, what am I good at? I'm okay at talking to strangers, and I'm good at drinking beer,” Dean explains. “So if I go to the pub, that seems like a place that Rob might have actually gone to if he was ever having a low moment or wanted somewhere to just be in his own space.”

Dean decided the best way to get noticed was to don a bright orange top and post information on social media about which pub he would be at. Within four days, someone turned up to chat.

open image in gallery Dean and fellow Empty Chairs attendees ( Dean Perryman/Supplied )

In January, Rob would have turned 30. This milestone prompted Dean to offer others the chance to host their own events. Hoping he might be able to give one person an opportunity to speak openly in a way that his best friend might have needed before he died, Empty Chairs was born.

“I’ve kind of struggled to come to terms with the whole thing, if I’m being honest,” Dean says when asked how he feels about the speed at which Empty Chairs has grown. In just shy of eight months, the campaign has seen 1,000 meetups and has even expanded to locations including Colombia, the Falkland Islands, and the United Arab Emirates.

“I didn’t realise it at the time, but it was a really good outlet for me to grieve and talk openly about Rob and how I was doing. To now be in a position where it feels as though we might be able to create a legacy for Rob is just incredible, and more than I could ever have hoped for,” he adds.

The lack of pressure seems to be the driving force behind its success. Every event is free and open to anyone. Attendees are encouraged to stay for as long as they want, whether that’s five minutes or an entire session, with no requirement to share anything personal.

open image in gallery Dean and Empty Chairs attendees at a pub ( Dean Perryman )

”It really is: go to the venue, look for the person wearing bright orange, and sit down and have a conversation,” Dean says.

He stresses that it’s not crisis support, and that anyone in urgent need of help should contact Samaritans or call the emergency services. However, he believes Empty Chairs has created an environment where “real human connection can happen.”

It is also helping pubs to return to their rightful place as community hubs at the heart of the community, Dean asserts. “It's always been a place where this stuff should be happening; it's just unfortunate that the world that we live in now requires people to wear bright orange to make that work,” he adds.

Rob’s love for sport is now driving Dean’s future plans. He has launched a “Matchdays” edition of Empty Chairs to be held before Southend United home games and dreams of his events being held next to every football ground in the country.

Dean wants anybody attending to know one thing: “Strangers are so much kinder than we give them credit for, and that's the biggest thing I've learned about this whole experience. Everyone who has come to sit with me has been so incredibly kind.

“The one thing I hear so much is ‘Oh, I would have just stayed at home alone again tonight.’ And to know that this has come from something that was personally the lowest point of my life is so beautiful.”

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

The Clacton by-election is a chance to “put Brexit back on the political agenda” and force the mainstream parties to consider rejoining the EU, a former Member of the European Parliament (MEP) who is running against Nigel Farage has claimed.

John Stevens, who is standing for the Rejoin the EU Party in the Clacton by-election, has warned that voters in the Essex constituency are unhappy with the media portrayal of the by-election as an unserious contest between Mr Farage and comedian candidate Count Binface.

“This is not a joke election from the perspective of people in Clacton,” he tells The Independent. I can tell you the Binface saga is going down like a lead balloon. People feel they are the butt of an inside Westminster joke.”

Instead he claims that voters in the constituency, particularly young people and women, are much more receptive to the idea of rejoining the EU, even though Clacton was one of the strongest areas for Leave a decade ago.

open image in gallery John Stevens is running for Rejoin the EU in Clacton ( Rejoin the EU Party )

But he warned that Nigel Farage wants “North Korean levels of support” of 95 per cent or more in the by-election which the main parties have refused to contest.

Mr Stevens, who was a Conservative MEP for a decade up to 1999, told the Independent: “People nationally need to understand this is not Binface versus Farage. It is an opportunity to hit Farage where it really hurts.

“If he gets a significant anti-Brexit vote... that is far more damaging to him and to the Reform cause than simply being humiliated by a dustbin.”

However, with Clacton voting 70 per cent for Leave in 2016 and Essex 62 per cent overall, he admitted: “It may not work, but this is an opportunity and it's worth a risk for me because it could embolden the pro-European side.”

open image in gallery Farage 'is hoping for North Korean levels of support' in Clacton, Mr Stevens has claimed ( Reuters )

Mr Stevens added: “Having a by-election in Makerfield to make someone prime minister is one thing, but to get us back into the EU is another. If I can do well here I hope the main parties will be emboldened to put rejoining back on the table.”

He insisted that his message is getting a hearing in Clacton as he knocks on doors.

“Quite a few people say ‘no, well, Brexit hasn't worked,’ or ‘I was against it,’ particularly many women more than men,” Mr Stevens says.

“On these new estates, younger people with families question Brexit, and I'm saying, ‘this is your chance to have an absolutely clean fight to express an opinion on something which nobody's talking about – not even Nigel Farage wants to talk about Brexit.’”

Mr Burnham said last September that he supported rejoining, but then retreated from that remark when he stood in a pro-Leave seat in Makerfield.

However, Mr Stevens believes: “Labour backbenchers all are all in favour of rejoining the EU.”

open image in gallery Count Binface is running in Clacton ( PA )

The candidate, a former City trader like Mr Farage, believes though that the answer to reversing Brexit is for former Remainers like him to admit they made mistakes a decade ago as well and not just blame Leave voters.

“I do believe very strongly that we mustn't have a confrontation between Leavers and Remainers. It's important for Remainers to say that, and I do believe this actually completely, that we had as much of a role in getting the Brexit result in 2016 as the Leavers.

“So this is all about not saying, well, ‘you were wrong and you know we were right and we've been vindicated.’

“It's got to be much more. It's got to be different. It's got to be much more reconciliatory. It's just ‘we all made a mistake and we're all going to correct it together.’”

This is not the first time he has taken on Mr Farage. In 2010 he stood against him in former Speaker John Bercow’s Buckingham constituency where he came second with more than 10,000 votes beating Mr Farage.

Malaysia will return to the Formula 1 calendar for the first time since 2017 as the sport executes its contingency plan for the second half of the 2026 season.

After races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were cancelled in April due to the conflict in the Middle East, F1 was keen to add to its current 22-race calendar and was hopeful of racing in Bahrain in October, in between already scheduled races in Azerbaijan (26 September) and Singapore (11 October).

However, given the recent escalation in the region after the ending of the US-Iran ceasefire, F1 bosses were forced to seek alternatives and the Sepang International Circuit, just outside Kuala Lumpur, is the option they’ve landed on.

Malaysia withdrew from the sport in 2017 when they couldn’t match the host fees required, yet the racetrack is still used regularly for other series such as MotoGP.

In this instance, its proximity to Singapore means a Europe-Asia triple-header, over the last weekend in September and the first two weekends in October, added to its feasibility. However, and rather oddly, it will be known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia for contractual reasons.

Turkey’s Istanbul Park, which returns to the sport in 2027, was another potential option and could still be used at the end of the season.

Another potential scheduling issue ahead for F1, who are keeping an eye on developments in the region nervously given their season is scheduled to end with Qatar (29 November) and Abu Dhabi (6 December), would be to race in Portugal after the third-last race in Las Vegas (21 November). Imola, which hosted a race in 2025, is another option.

The Algarve International Circuit is scheduled to return to the calendar next year on a two-year deal, having last hosted a race in the Covid-impacted 2021 season. Other European circuits have also offered to help out if needed, though colder temperatures towards the end of the season could work against them.

What triple header looks like? Saturday, 26 September - Azerbaijan GP Sunday, 4 October - Bahrain GP in Malaysia Sunday 11 October - Singapore GP

However, F1 executives will leave the end-of-season quandary as late as possible, given the huge hosting fees at play for staging the last two races of the season. Abu Dhabi, in particular, pays an estimated £31.5m ($42m) to host the final race of the season every year.

F1 will also race in its first new location in three years in September, when a street circuit in Madrid hosts the new-look Spanish Grand Prix.

The sport races in Hungary, the final round before the summer break, this weekend.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.content:
Man Utd 'won't make Champions League spots' due to major concern and Bruno Fernandes factor

Manchester United enjoyed a stunning second half of last season but they still have their doubters as Michael Carrick looks to make an impact across an entire campaign

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is out to prove himself in his first full season at Man Utd (Image: MARKKU ULANDER, Lehtikuva/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United won't make the Champions League places next season according to Troy Deeney - who believes they'll struggle with the added amount of games.

‌



The Red Devils enjoyed a huge renaissance under Michael Carrick, who took charge in January. They had been inconsistent until his arrival before going on an impressive run, winning 12 of their final 17 games to finish third.

‌



That run came with United not in any European competition and out of both domestic cups at the first hurdle. It means, from January, they only had their Premier League assignments to focus on, which was advantageous.

‌



They will not enjoy that benefit again as Carrick looks to prove himself across a full season - and Deeney cannot see Bruno Fernandes having the same level of influence. The Portuguese playmaker won numerous individual accolades and set the record for assists.

Mason Mount opens up on new Man Utd role handed to him by Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts READ MORE :

He told talkSPORT: "I don’t think they’ll make the Champions League places right now. The reason is we don’t know what Carrick’s like with three games in a week at this level. Obviously, we saw a bit of Championship, but not at this level.

"Now, having to look at the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cups, Carabao Cups, you can’t go out as early as you have done in previous years. There’s an expectation now to do more. Bruno Fernandes, do you really think he’s going to have the season he had last season again this season?

‌



"I just think that with the squad currently constructed as is, I don’t think there’s enough depth to get through all of those competitions, which I think will ultimately leave them short."

View 2 Images Man Utd finished an impressive third last term (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

United have made it a priority to add midfielders this summer as they look to prepare themselves for next season. They built up some impressive momentum last term and have since added Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos with the middle of the pitch cited as a problem area.

Article continues below

Deeney has backed Arsenal to retain their title with Manchester City again second best. Liverpool, now under new management, are his pick for third whilst he's backed Xabi Alonso to get Chelsea back into the top four after a dire season last time out.

Real Madrid president has already made Vinicius Jr to Arsenal stance very clear

Arsenal are eyeing up a move for Vinicius Jnr as his Real Madrid contract winds down but Florentino Perez is determined to keep him if a deal can be struck

View 2 Images Arsenal are weighing up a sensational move for Vinicius Jnr (Image: Denis Doyle, Getty Images)

Real Madrid president Florentino Perez admits he'd "love Vinicius Jnr to stay forever" as Arsenal look to seize on the uncertainty surrounding his contract situation.

‌



The Gunners have talked up a move internally as they consider making a move for the Brazilian, who is out of contract next season with no major progress yet made on an extension.

‌



Arsenal have just claimed the Premier League and want to add more star quality as they look to take the final step in the Champions League. Adding more firepower in attack is seen as an area where Mikel Arteta's side can improve and Vinicius is regarded among the best wingers in the world.

The Brazilian has been at the Bernabeu since 2018 and has continued to blossom. He scored in Champions League final victories in 2022 and 2024 and Perez is on record stating his admiration for him.

He said on his future: "Vinicius' renewal? There's time. I'd love for him to stay forever. He's won us the last two Champions Leagues and he identifies really well with the club. You know who doesn't like him? Those who aren't Real Madrid fans."

Talks between Arsenal and Real haven't taken place, reports the Athletic, but the La Liga giants may have to cash in on Vinicius if there's a risk of seeing him leave on a free transfer in 2027. The report adds that the winger would be due a significant loyalty bonus next season, having been at the Bernabeu for eight years.

Arsenal have not made any bid yet but it is understood that Jose Mourinho, who has just returned to Real last year after having a public spat with Vinicius, would oppose Arsenal signing the forward this summer - he wants all his big names to stay. Real Madrid have reportedly moved a step closer to completing a deal to sign RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande, which could have implications for Vinicius Jr’s future at the club.

‌



It was reported on Saturday that Arsenal have joined the race to sign Vinicius, adding the 26-year-old to their list of potential transfer targets this summer.

Sports.content:
Man Utd 8th and Liverpool 15th in list of biggest earners from World Cup payouts

Premier League clubs picked up handy bonuses thanks to their players' exploits at the World Cup

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister's progress at the World Cup help their clubs bank millions (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Almost half of the Premier League banked tidy sums from the World Cup as part of FIFA compensation payments. The competition will be viewed as an inconvenience to many clubs, given the risk of injury and interruption to pre-season.

‌



However, there is a financial benefit for players' clubs, as they receive compensation through the FIFA Club Benefits Programme. It was designed to recognise and financially reward clubs for their role in developing, employing and releasing players to participate on the global stage.

‌



Clubs are entitled to roughly £3,750 per day, per player from the release date of May 25 to their national team's final match in the competition. Therefore, the maximum payouts will be due to players from Spain, Argentina, England and France, who played the most games in North America.

‌



Given the Premier League's reputation as the world's top domestic league, English clubs figure prominently in the top 20 of clubs that earned the most from the tournament.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Tottenham Hotspur, who came in at 17th, are due £1.58m, one place behind Chelsea (£1.65m), reports The Athletic. Liverpool, in 15th, earned a similar amount to the Blues. The Reds had eight players at the tournament, including Alexis Mac Allister of runners-up Argentina.

‌



Sunderland are the next English club in 13th, one spot behind Aston Villa. Manchester United (£1.95m) are eighth on the list. They received payments for Kobbie Mainoo, despite the fact that he didn't play a single minute at the tournament, and Marcus Rashford, who spent last season on loan at Barcelona.

Crystal Palace (£2.03m), in seventh, were also well represented at the tournament with 12 players, including England back-up keeper Dean Henderson, France pair Maxence Lacroix and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Spain's Yeremy Pino.

View 3 Images Rodri of Manchester City led Spain to World Cup glory (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



Paris Saint-Germain (£2.4m), Arsenal (£2.48m), Bayern Munich (£2.55m), Barcelona (£2.93m) and Manchester City (£3.3m) make up the top five. Barcelona had eight Spain players alone - Ferran Torres, Eric Garcia, Gavi, Dani Olmo, Joan Garcia, Lamine Yamal, Pedri and Pau Cubarsi.

Arsenal had 16 players at the World Cup, three fewer than City, who lost virtually their entire first-time squad to the tournament. Many of those players are enjoying post-World Cup breaks before returning to their clubs in August.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job

Trent Alexander-Arnold's England career has stalled under Thomas Tuchel

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold's England career under Thomas Tuchel has yet to take off (Image: PA)

Trent Alexander-Arnold's dream of reuniting with Jurgen Klopp was shattered after the former Liverpool boss became the new Germany manager. Klopp, 59, has returned to management with the national team in his first coaching role since departing Anfield in the summer of 2024.

‌



The Real Madrid defender spent the entirety of his professional career at Liverpool under Klopp and previously admitted his desire to play under him again - but on the international stage.

‌



Speaking after Gareth Southgate stepped down as Three Lions boss following their Euro 2024 final defeat, Alexander-Arnold was asked about his thoughts on Klopp replacing him as the England boss.

‌



The 27-year-old said: "I enjoyed every moment I worked with him, we shared amazing memories, forged an amazing relationship, an amazing bond. So of course if that were to happen, we would pick up where we left off."

Klopp made the shock decision to depart Liverpool due to a lack of energy. His former pupil admitted at the time that he would have been surprised if he took the role just two months after leaving Merseyside.

Alexander-Arnold added: "I would be surprised if he did take it. It was clear when he announced when he was leaving, the conversations I have had with him, everything on social media, he seems to be enjoying his time off, so it would be a huge surprise."

‌



Klopp's first press conference as Germany boss on Friday started with a bang. He immediately handed an ultimatum to the German press by threatening to quit the job if they do not leave his family alone.

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold was managed by Jurgen Klopp for the entirety of his professional career at Liverpool (Image: Andrew Powell, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

"Now is the time where I'm really in the middle of the media focus," Klopp began. "I was surprised, not negatively or positively surprised, at how fast news spread. And it's sometimes hard for people to just think 'let's turn a blind eye to things' and not to divulge any information.

‌



"Sometimes that is the right thing to do, not to publish things that happened. I know full well this is job number one for me. It is my mission to make the national squad better and to hope the pool for me to choose from is bigger.

View 3 Images The Real Madrid defender missed out on England's World Cup squad this summer (Image: PA)

"But it is not something I will do against you, but I’m doing it for you. It is an honour. I will be remunerated very graciously and if tomorrow it's 'Jurgen Klopp is s***', then I will be gone. But if the DFB (German FA) says ‘Come on let us not continue the job’ then that’s it.

‌



"And if you (the media) behave badly and don’t let my family live in peace. I’ll be gone and I'll just turn away. I know there are other countries where the national team head coaches are treated even worse. But I love this job, but I’m always ready to call just call it quits if need be.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Jurgen Klopp is not going to have any ‘career’ after the national team, this is the absolute pinnacle of my footballing career as a coach. I will give everything I’ve got."

Article continues below

The ex-Liverpool star's international career has stalled under Thomas Tuchel, who stunningly left out the full-back from his World Cup squad this summer. Alexander-Arnold suffered an injury-hit debut campaign with Spain and made just 30 appearances across all competitions in what was a trophy-less season for Madrid.

Sports.title: Real Madrid in pole position to sign RB Leipzig's Diomande
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are in pole position to sign RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande, according to Sky in Germany.

The Spanish giants have already had a £85.4m (€100m) bid rejected for the 19-year-old but Leipzig want significantly more to let him go.

Sky in Germany are reporting that Real were working with RB Leipzig on Saturday night to strike an agreement for the player.

Diomande had previously indicated a preference to join Paris Saint-Germain earlier this summer and agreed a contract with them until 2031.

Real have now also agreed personal terms with Diomande.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at all of the reasons why Yan Diomande is high on the radar of clubs from across the world.

Jose Mourinho's side have been active in this window as Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries and Marc Cucurella have all been snapped up.

Liverpool have also expressed an interest in winger Diomande but aren't willing to pay more than £85m.

Premier League clubs Arsenal and Manchester City also remain interested in Diomande.

With six weeks left of the transfer window, the situation has been described as an open race by sources close to any potential deal. Real have now come to the table with an offer amid uncertainty around the future of Vinicius Junior.

The fee Liverpool are ready to pay at this stage would dwarf the Premier League's record transfer for a teenager, surpassing the £58.9m Manchester United agreed to sign Leny Yoro from Lille for in the summer of 2024.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News brings you the latest transfer news with updates on the likes of Cristian Romero, Yan Diomande and Maxence Lacroix.

Arsenal are looking into a potential deal for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

At this point there has been no club-to-club contact, but the interest is real. Vinicius Jr is one of a number of forward targets Arsenal are exploring, with Julian Alvarez, Diomande and Bradley Barcola also players of interest.

The Brazilian international, 26, has entered the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Real could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Bayern confident of Olise stay amid Real links

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Olise produced left foot magic to open the scoring for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga game against Wolfsburg last season...

Bayern Munich director Christoph Freund has rebuffed claims that Real Madrid could come in for Michael Olise.

Olise has been linked with a move to the Spanish giants but Freund says such a move is not on his mind.

"This is not a topic for us at all," Freund told reporters on Saturday

"We are delighted that Michael Olise has returned from his holiday. He will continue to play an important role at Bayern Munich this season, just like last year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande opens up about his football journey so far, including trials at Premier League clubs such as Chelsea and Crystal Palace

"Everything went fast," says Yan Diomande. Indeed, it is extraordinary now to think that this time last year Diomande's entire senior career amounted to half a dozen starts for Leganes at the back end of last season as they were relegated from LaLiga.

He scored in two of those six games, against Espanyol and Valladolid. Even his team did not find the net in the other four. But the teenager did enough to persuade RB Leipzig to part with €20m to bring him to the Bundesliga. Once there, he has been a revelation.

Thrilling to watch and impossible to defend, Diomande is lightning, full of unpredictable enterprise. He has the things that cannot be coached and by listening to the things that can he is getting better. The very biggest clubs want him. The rest cannot afford him.

Sports.title: Impressive Liverpool beat Sunderland in Iraola's first game in charge
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola won his first match in charge of Liverpool as his new side produced an impressive display to beat Sunderland 4-2 in their opening game of their summer tour of the US.

Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot at Anfield in June, will have been delighted with some of the football Liverpool produced in the Nashville heat, especially a fine team move that led to the opening goal for young midfielder Kieran Morrison after 13 minutes.

The Basque, like his opposite number Regis Le Bris, rung the changes after the first half, with Liverpool improving after the break to turn around a 2-1 deficit thanks to a characteristic Dominik Szoboszlai piledriver, followed by further strikes from fellow substitutes Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas.

However, there was one negative for Iraola, who saw stand-in captain and long-serving defender Joe Gomez forced off early on with what looked a muscle issue in an area of the team where Liverpool really could do without any injuries heading into the new campaign.

The key moments from Nashville SC Stadium

8: INJURY! A big worry already for Liverpool with captain Gomez down with an injury and this does not look good for the centre-back.

13: GOAL! The first goal of the Iraola era is scored by Morrison after a wonderful team move involving some impressive build-up from the likes of McConnell, Ngumoha and Elliott, who fed the midfielder in space on the right of the box and he then found the bottom corner with a low shot.

28: GOAL! Sunderland are level as McConnell loses possession deep inside the Black Cats' half allowing Le Fee to break upfield and as the Reds defence backed off, the playmaker fired an unstoppable effort past a helpless Mamardashvili from 25 yards.

49: GOAL! Sunderland have turned this one around to now lead after Frimpong lost possession in a bad area, with the ball then slipped through for Tuterov, with the half-time sub finishing confidently.

56: GOAL! It is now raining goals as Szoboszlai hits an absolute worldie to bring Liverpool level after an excellent break down the left involving Koumas and Kerkez and after Sunderland only half clear the danger, the Hungary midfielder lashes home an unstoppable volley from the left edge of the box.

72: GOAL! And now Liverpool are back in front as Ramsey feeds Chiesa in space in the box and from a tight angle and faced with the onrushing Moore to beat, the sub finds the back of the net from a tight angle.

85: GOAL! Liverpool score another excellent goal to surely wrap this game up as Sunderland initially give the ball away and Szoboszlai finds Koumas in the box and the sub does well to find the net with a confident finish.

'A lot of things to correct, but a good starting point'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola:

"I think it was different halves. Especially, they were a lot stronger in the first half. We kind of balanced both teams, and you could feel the difference. A lot of things to correct, obviously, it's the first day.

"You could feel the heavy legs, the players have been training. So, we lacked some freshness. But it will give us a good starting point to improve things.

"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe [Gomez]. We were happy because we were kind of going through all the training without losing any player. Unluckily for us, straight away we've lost Joe."

Lots of positives for Iraola to take

Sky Sports' Rich Morgan:

Lots of positives for Iraola to take from his first match in charge of Liverpool, starting obviously with the win, although this being preseason in many ways it was the performance of his players and how well they gelled at times that will have most pleased the new Reds boss.

Liverpool scored some eye-catching goals, the team got better as the game wore on, despite the heat in Nashville, and all 22 players used with be better for this first competitive runout of preseason.

Iraola sweating on nature of Gomez's latest injury

Sky Sports' Rich Morgan:

Iraola may have won his first match in charge of Liverpool, but there was some worrying injury news as Joe Gomez was forced off early on.

Image: Joe Gomez was substituted early on with an injury

The long-serving defender appeared to suffer a muscle issue and was replaced in the centre of defence by youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe just 10 minutes into the club's first preseason game of their summer tour of the US.

Gomez, 29, has a long history of injuries at Anfield, although Iraola will hope it is nothing too serious with Ibrahima Konate having left on a free transfer at the end of last season, while both Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet missed the game in Nashville also with injury.

Leoni, signed last year from Parma, will not be back to full fitness for at least a few months after suffering an ACL on his Reds debut last September, while Jacquet, who joined the club from Rennes this summer, missed the game with a minor knock having only just recovered from a shoulder issue.

Sports.title: Sheeraz escapes with narrow points win as he sets his sights on Canelo
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz escaped with a narrow points win, while Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose on the Anthony Joshua vs Kristian Prenga undercard in Saudi Arabia on Saturday.

Londoner Sheeraz, who sealed his first world title with a second-round stoppage win against Alem Begic to claim the vacant WBO super-middleweight crown in Egypt, defeated Germany's Simon Zachenhuber.

After a 12-round fight that ended with boos around the arena the judges returned scores of 114-114, 115-113 and 116-112, in favour of Sheeraz, who posed with Jacob Bank in the ring following his win.

"I am a champion in the division. I'm sure people are champing at the bit after [my] performance," said Sheeraz, who said he would be sat ringside on October 31 to watch Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez challenge for Christian Mbilli's WBC belt.

"I got the win, that's all that matters. I could make a million excuses. I'll be better in the next fight.

"I need a step up now, someone who will mentally present a challenge. I was switching off at times, I was too comfortable when I didn't have a threat in front of me."

Image: A bloodied Josh Kelly wins his IBF World Super Welterweight title contest against Caoimhin Agyarko

Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose as he secured a unanimous points win against Irishman Caoimhin Agyarko in an IBF Light-Middleweight title fight in Saudi Arabia.

Nicknamed 'Pretty Boy', Kelly was left bloodied as the pair clashed heads in the 11th round with the Brit's face left a mess.

But he did enough to get the win with scorecards of 115-112, 115-112, 114-113.

"I told Caoimhin, don't take it as a loss, take it as a learning. If he wants it bad enough, he will bounce back," said Kelly.

Agyarko said: "I thought I won it, but if it's not good enough for the judges, I accept that. I'm heartbroken, I wanted to make history. Josh Kelly is a class act, but I think he underestimated me a bit, there.

"Listen, it will come. I will be the first Black Irish world champion, there's no doubt about that."

After the bout, Kelly said he wants to face unified 154-pound champion Jaron 'Boots' Ennis.

Promoter Eddie Hearn, who represents both Kelly and Ennis, said a clash between the two in the States is now a real option.

"He's had a defence of the title and before that mandatory comes again, really you want to be looking at those big money fights and trying to roll the dice," Hearn said.

"I think that comes with 'Boots' Ennis. If I'm Josh Kelly I'm looking at the big payday out in America against 'Boots' Ennis. It's a three-belt unification fight. [WBC champion] Sebastian Fundora, all those guys."

Sports.title: Joshua devotes win to late friends as 'lovely treat' of Fury fight looms
Sports.content:
An emotional Anthony Joshua remembered his late friends as he staved off a seismic shock against Kristian Prenga to rubberstamp a fight with Tyson Fury that he says will be a "lovely treat" for fans.

Joshua knocked out Albanian heavyweight Prenga in the second round in Jeddah on Saturday night, after twice being floored himself in the first, including just 20 seconds into the contest.

The British star displayed tremendous character to battle back from the brink of defeat, a trait he has had to show in abundance since the deaths of team members Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele in a car crash in December in which he was a passenger.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Anthony Joshua dedicates his win over Kristian Prenga to his late friends after the tragic car crash. Courtsey of DAZN.

Speaking after overcoming Prenga, Joshua told DAZN: "It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it.

"It has been tough. It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

Image: Joshua was sensationally knocked down by Albanian Prenga inside 20 seconds of their clash in Saudi Arabia

Joshua: I respect everything Fury has done

Joshua was able to discuss Fury, with the British boxers now set to end over a decade of circling each other by locking horns in November, with America seemingly the most likely destination.

Fury beat Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in his own tune-up fight in Thailand on Friday.

AJ added of his countryman, who did not head to Saudi Arabia for a face-off with his rival: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment Anthony Joshua sealed victory over Kristian Prenga with a huge second round knockout. Courtesy of DAZN.

"All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.

"I've learnt I can't be stopped. I won't be stopped and I won't be denied. We're here and we're coming. Trust me."

Image: Joshua celebrates after his second-round KO of Prenga in Jeddah on Saturday night

'No one can imagine what Joshua has been through'

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn confirmed that contracts have been signed for the blockbuster showdown before going on to praise his fighter's "astonishing" return to the ring after the "grief and pain" he had to deal with following the car crash shortly before Christmas.

Hearn said of Joshua on DAZN: "To be honest with you, tonight is all about the strength AJ has showed to even be here tonight - and the strength in that fight.

"No one can imagine what he has been through in the last seven months. During the first round, I was thinking, 'we came back too soon'.

Image: Joshua was floored twice in the opening round but bounced back to win and stay in course for a clash with Fury

"I feel boxing once saved him and I feel like he needed boxing to help him get through this. That camp allowed him to focus while he was facing so much grief and pain.

"He is a strong man and he likes to deal with his problems on his own - I'm not saying that is the right way but that is his way to do it. To even be in the ring tonight was astonishing.

"When you go down a couple ​of times in the first round and you're looking like ​your career might be over, he had to go to the depths one more time to get ‌up and fight on."
