Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's astonishing letter congratulating Argentina on finishing second at the World Cup is LEAKED as FIFA president hails Lionel Messi and Co's 'professionalism' despite thuggish post-match antics
Sports.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has shamelessly praised Argentina’s ‘professionalism’ in a tone-deaf letter to the nation's FA - despite launching an investigation into their behaviour after losing the World Cup final against Spain.

While congratulatory letters are customary after the World Cup, with all three medal-winning nations receiving one from Infantino, his choice of words is questionable.

In the letter - first leaked by the Argentine media and since verified by Daily Mail Sport - sent to the President of the Argentine FA, Claudio Tapia, Infantino thanked Argentina for their impact on a successful World Cup and applauded their professionalism.

‘Dear Mr. President, Yesterday, Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the magnificent New York New Jersey Stadium, Argentina won the silver medal of the FIFA World Cup 2026, after an exciting final against Spain,’ Infantino said.

‘I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine soccer.

‘The FIFA World Cup 2026 will remain in memory as an unforgettable celebration of football, marked by spectacular matches, the irruption of new promises, the presence of the great figures of the sport and the extraordinary atmosphere lived in stadiums full of fans.

Gianni Infantino handed Lionel Messi his silver medal alongside President Trump

Infantino watched the World Cup semi-final with Argentine FA chief Claudio Tapia

The Argentina squad turned their back as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy

Join the discussion Should teams showing poor sportsmanship still be praised for professionalism by football’s top officials?

‘The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world.

‘Please send my sincere congratulations to all who have contributed to this magnificent result: to the players, to coach Lionel Scaloni, as well as to the coaching and medical staff and, of course, to the many fans who have accompanied and encouraged the team throughout the competition.

‘These victories are always the fruit of constant work, professionalism and attention to detail, but also of passion, commitment and love for this wonderful sport. All this augurs a very promising future and, without a doubt, will pave the way for new and great successes for Argentine football.

‘I wish you, dear Mr. President, all the best for the next competitions and I hope to see you again very soon. With all my friendship, Gianni Infantino.’

Argentina, who lost in extra-time in the final, frustrated opponents throughout the tournament with their anti-football style of play.

The 2022 winners failed to register a single shot on target in the final and following the defeat, they turned their backs as Luis de la Fuente’s side lifted the trophy.

Leonardo Paredes attacked Eric Garcia in a post-match fracas that also appeared to involve Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala - an incident FIFA are investigating.

The final itself was packed with controversy. Lionel Messi attempted to con referee Slavko Vincic into sending Marc Cucurella off after the Spain defender covered his mouth while speaking to the official. Argentina had attempted a similar tactic on Jude Bellingham during their semi-final against England.

In that semi-final victory, Argentina were also guilty of frequent simulation and gamesmanship in a provocative display.

They also drew complaints from British dignitaries after celebrating with a banner reading ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’, which translates as ‘The Falklands are Argentine’.

Fighting in honour of Ghami and Ayodele, Joshua paid tribute to his friends by having their names printed on his military camouflage trunks.

Meanwhile, ‘Latz x Sina, My Brother's Keeper, MBK’ was printed on the canvas in his corner.

Anthony Joshua wears jacket featuring medal bar with 'Sina' and 'Latz' pennants

Joshua's friends were honoured by having their names printed on the canvas

Asked about how he has been coping after beating Prenga, Joshua said: 'It's been tough,' before becoming emotional. 'That's my brothers. I don't want to talk about that.'

Speaking on DAZN, Matchroom Boxing chief Eddie Hearn added: 'Nobody can imagine what he's been through in that last seven months. In that first round, I thought we'd come back too soon.

'Boxing got him through. To even be in the ring tonight is astonishing. You don't know what he's been through. He had to go to the depths one more time to get up, like he has done the last seven months.'

In February, Joshua memorialised Ghami and Ayodele by having their names tattooed on his arm.

Oleksandr Usyk was ringside for the clash in Jeddah to support Joshua, whom he beat twice in world title fights. Usyk has been working closely with Joshua, supporting his training camp.

Victory for Joshua means he is on track to finally fight Tyson Fury in a long-awaited British heavyweight showdown.

Sports.title: Adam Peaty breaks down in tears and makes heartbreaking comment about family feud
Sports.content:
Adam Peaty breaks down in tears and makes heartbreaking comment about family feud

Adam Peaty was in reflective and emotional mood after his bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games

View 3 Images Adam Peaty had to settle for bronze in the 100m breaststroke (Image: Getty Images)

A tearful Adam Peaty appeared to bring up his family feud after being forced to settle for bronze in his premier event at the Commonwealth Games. The three-time Olympic champion's private life has been a source of intrigue since he got engaged to Holly Ramsay, the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon .

‌



The pair got married in December last year following a much-publicised rift with the majority of his family, which escalated after his mother, Caroline, was not invited to the bride's hen do. Peaty, who has taken on the Ramsay name, has not publicly spoken about the feud, a stance that has continued in the build-up to the Games in Glasgow.

‌



But after he surprisingly fell short in the 100m breaststroke final, he broke his silence, saying: "It's hard because I know how hard I work. I know the s**t I've been through, which is no fault of my own, but it does take its toll.

‌



"I'm not crying because it's bronze instead of gold. I'm crying because I know I am better than that. I feel like I couldn’t have put any more in and that's where it hurts, because I'm like, 'What’s the point of all the metres every day, what's the point of being exhausted all the time?'

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"What's the point of having to say no to family events so you can go to training? It has to mean something and for me, it has to be human excellence and that is not excellence for me. So that's the emotion that is unfortunately coming out."

‌



Heartbreak for Adam Peaty's mum as he competes in first race since fallout with new name READ MORE :

Adam Peaty issues defiant statement after wedding scuffle and family fallout READ MORE :

Peaty also took aim at his critics, declaring, "you can't hurt me" and telling them to "do better." He was cheered on by his wife, Holly, who is expecting the couple's first child in December. Peaty has another child from a previous relationship.

After collecting his medal, he kissed his new wife on the belly and said: "She's always going to be proud of me. And as a father, it doesn't matter if you come home with gold. As long as you come home with a teddy. That's really what matters.

View 3 Images Peaty couldn't hold back the tears (Image: TNT Sports)

‌



"But I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness, because it's so important for making stronger people, making stronger men, stronger fathers, husbands. And it's a realisation of how much I do work."

The 31-year-old was pipped by Australia's Sam Williamson and 18-year-old Filip Nowacki of Jersey in a race he had dominated for eight years before shockingly finishing out of the medals in Birmingham four years ago.

View 3 Images Peaty's wife Holly was proud of his efforts in Glasgow (Image: Getty Images)

Meanwhile, England's William Ellard and Georgia Sheffield both set new Games records as they won the respective men's and women's S14 200m freestyle finals. Sheffield pipped team-mate Poppy Maskill, who took silver.

England's Ollie Morgan won a silver medal in the men's 50m backstroke final, finishing behind South Africa's Pieter Coetze. England's mixed 4x100m freestyle relay squad took silver behind Australia, with Wales in third.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy 'hit with £1.6million tax bill' as huge major earnings laid bare
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy 'hit with £1.6million tax bill' as huge major earnings laid bare

Rory McIlroy's major success this year has come at a heavy cost as the golf superstar's tax deductions from 2026 come to light

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy will pay the most of any golfer this year when it comes to his majors tax bill (Image: Warren Little/Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy made history in 2026 as he became just the fourth golfer to successfully retain the Masters title. However, his success at the biggest tournaments the sport has to offer has also led to some serious tax deductions.

‌



McIlroy, 37, concluded his major season on Sunday with a T40 finish in The Open at Royal Birkdale. The Northern Irishman struggled to come back following a particularly disappointing two-over-par first round, ultimately finishing nine strokes behind eventual winner Ryan Fox.

‌



That was still sufficient to bag around £52,000 in prize money, though nothing compared with his £3.4m winnings from adding a second Green Jacket. His second straight win at Augusta unsurprisingly accounted for the vast majority of his major money in 2026, which was also supplemented by his £478,000 winnings for a T7 finish at the PGA Championship.

‌



When you add in in his £97,000 reward for tying 32nd at the US Open in May, McIlroy's total major prize haul for 2026 amounts to almost £4m on the dot. However, calculations courtesy of golfclubs4cash estimate that also means he's paying the most tax of any golfer this year when it comes to the major tournaments.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

His total tax bill from those four competitions amounts to approximately £1,634,840, accounting for fluctuations in the dollar to sterling conversion rate. As such, he's expected to have handed back a little more than a third of his major winnings this year.

‌



Golf news: Rory McIlroy sends invite to Bryson DeChambeau as star withdraws from 3M Open READ MORE :

That leaves around £2.35m of McIlroy's earnings that he can take straight to the bank. However, that's in addition to the other £2.4m or so he's won on other PGA Tour events this year (or around £1.5m once you apply for the same tax rate on those earnings).

That amounts to an estimated total take-home sum of £3.85m from all PGA Tour events so far in 2026. Not bad for a season's work in which McIlroy de-escalated his activity to focus more solely on the major competitions.

View 2 Images McIlroy endured a disappointing Open Championship, tying for 40th as he registered his worst major finish of 2026 (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

‌



It's close at the top of the majors tax bill totem pole, however, as Wyndham Clark almost paid an identical sum. The American finished in second place on the list, having forked over an estimated £1,630,278 in deductions, just £4,000 less than McIlroy.

Clark, 32, won the US Open for the second time in his career to bag the £3.4m top prize. His T21 finish at the Masters also came with a £184,000 reward, though he missed the cut at both last weekend's Open and the PGA Championship.

It should come as a surprise to nobody that world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler also worked his way onto the tax podium. This year marked the first since 2023 that the Texan failed to win a major, though he placed top four at three (and T14 at the PGA Championship), leaving him with £3.4m in prize money and a tax bill of a little more than £1.4m.

Scheffler and Sam Burns (fourth) are the only names among the top six on the list who made the cut without winning a major. And while the tax costs may be a burden, McIlroy will know he's doing something right if he features among the leaders once more in 2027.

Sports.title: Man Utd can solve two problems after approval to sign star Bryan Mbeumo hates playing
Sports.content:
Man Utd can solve two problems after approval to sign star Bryan Mbeumo hates playing

Manchester United continue to bolster their squad during the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Antonee Robinson is on United's radar (Image: Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Manchester United continue to be linked with Fulham star Antonee Robinson in a move that could provide two benefits to the Red Devils. Not only is the American defender is one of the most experienced left-backs in the Premier League, he's also the one Bryan Mbeumo hates coming up against the most.

‌



Robinson has drawn widespread admiration across the top flight, but it is the verdict of the United striker that is likely to carry the most weight. Mbeumo named Robinson as the toughest defender he has ever faced while appearing on the Obi One podcast last year.

‌



He said: "I used to play against him when he was at Wigan and (he) changed completely. When he arrived he was really athletic, quick, but with his feet he was like, not so good, you know?

‌



"But throughout the years he improved a lot, and I think now he can do everything. He can attack, he can defend, he's strong, he's good with his feet now, and yeah, I think really, really hard to play against him."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Coming from a forward who tormented Premier League defences for years before his switch to United, that endorsement is far and above a huge compliment.

‌



Michael Carrick is understood to be monitoring Robinson closely as he looks to provide competition at left-back. Luke Shaw remains the only recognised senior option in that position following Tyrell Malacia's departure.

After Malacia's contract expired, Harry Amass became backup to Shaw. However, the teenager is considered too raw to shoulder the burden alone after just seven first-team appearances.

Robinson has become one of the Premier League's most consistent and dynamic full-backs, making 26 goal contributions across 215 appearances. He has also earned 58 caps for the United States national team, netting five times.

‌



View 2 Images Antonee Robinson has given Bryan Mbeumo plenty of bother in the past (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

His age has been flagged as a potential obstacle, with The Guardian reporting that Robinson falls outside United's preferred target profile. However, the quality of his performances continues to attract suitors regardless.

United can kill two birds with one stone in signing Robinson. He can provide cover - and competition - at left-back and allow Mbeumo to enjoy playing alongside him rather than coming up against him.

Article continues below

Robinson is believed to be available for approximately £25million - a fee that could represent outstanding value for any club willing to invest in a proven performer. For United in particular, securing Robinson alongside the returning Shaw would not only provide Carrick with dependable cover but also hand youngster Amass the breathing room to develop at a sensible pace.

Sports.title: Liverpool star was banished from pre-season after boss called him out on camera
Sports.content:
Liverpool star was banished from pre-season after boss called him out on camera

Liverpool's pre-season was disrupted after one of their players broke the rules

View 3 Images Mamadou Sakho joined Liverpool in 2013 (Image: VI-Images, VI-Images via Getty Images)

Liverpool's current pre-season tour of the USA is underway. However, one of the club's previous trips Stateside was marred by a falling out between former manager Jurgen Klopp and ex-defender Mamadou Sakho, which was partly caught on camera.

‌



Sakho, 36, officially retired from football earlier this year after being without a club since May 2025. The French defender was brought to Liverpool by ex-manager Brendan Rodgers in September 2013 in a bid to toughen up the club's backline, arriving from Paris Saint-Germain for £18 million.

‌



After taking over in October 2015, the following summer marked Klopp's first pre-season with the Reds. The German was clearly unafraid to make his presence felt among those in the squad who treated strict rules as merely guidance, as Sakho was sent home prematurely from the club's American tour.

‌



The grievance came to light after Sakho was handed a GoPro camera as the Liverpool squad visited Alcatraz prison in San Francisco. As Klopp was being interviewed by club staff, Sakho snuck up and laughed in the background and the German let slip that Sakho had violated a club rule on lateness.

“We could have left Mama Sakho here because he is filming me while I give the interview here,” Klopp said. Sakho interjected: “I have just one question. How long do you think you can live here?”

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jurgen Klopp favourite has told Andoni Iraola all about Liverpool target Maghnes Akliouche READ MORE :

"Actually, I don't have to think about it. You should think about it," Klopp said back. "Because only one of us came late last night, for departure in Liverpool. It was not me."

Speaking after Sakho was sent home from the USA, Klopp explained: “I thought maybe it made sense for him to fly home to Liverpool and after eight or 10 days, when we come back, we can talk about it. It's not that serious.

“He nearly missed the departure of the plane, he missed a session and was late for a meal. We have some rules and we have to respect them. If somebody doesn't respect it or somebody gives me the feeling he is not respecting it, then I have to react, that's all.

‌



View 3 Images Mamadou Sakho and Jurgen Klopp's relationship was tested at Liverpool (Image: 2015 Liverpool FC)

“It is private how he reacted. But we had no argument. You cannot argue when only one person is speaking. That's all. I think missed a session is missed a session. Even injured players have sessions.”

Speaking in France later, Sakho admitted his penchant for tardiness to Canal Football Club, saying: “It is true that I turned up late. There was a rule that I should have observed. I do not at all see myself as above the rules, I respect everyone.

‌



“I paid my fine, I was sanctioned, I apologised to my team-mates and my manager. Aside from that… I do not want to go into the controversies.”

Sakho's debut campaign nearly delivered the Reds their first Premier League title in almost 25 years. Yet he featured in just 18 Premier League games as Liverpool's backline leaked 50 goals, ultimately costing them the championship and, while he impressed in Klopp's early days, his career never fully got off the ground at the Reds.

View 3 Images Sakho had a difficult end to his Liverpool career (Image: Colin Lane)

‌



The centre-back's actions in the USA proved to be the breaking point for Klopp, whose patience had worn thin. Sakho was demoted to the Under-23s and never featured for the senior side again.

January 2017 came around and Sakho departed Liverpool, sealing a loan switch to Crystal Palace. Sakho performed so impressively in south London that the Eagles even signed him permanently in the summer of 2017, shelling out £25m.

He departed in the summer of 2022. Sakho later featured for Montpellier and finally for Torpedo Kutaisi in the Georgian first division before calling time on his colourful career.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish's dream summer move set to be blocked following transfer announcement
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish's dream summer move set to be blocked following transfer announcement

Jack Grealish spent last season on loan to Everton from Manchester City

View 3 Images Jack Grealish is now facing a tough summer (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Jack Grealish's dream Aston Villa homecoming could be off the cards following the signing of Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea. The left winger agreed a season-long loan in Birmingham with an obligation to buy clause set for next summer.

‌



Garnacho arrived at Villa Park following the Blues' acquisition of Morgan Rogers for a record £117million fee. While these transfers represent positive reinforcements for both clubs, it could also spell disaster for Grealish.

‌



The England international joined City for £100m in 2021, signing a six-year deal. During his time at the Etihad, Grealish has secured three Premier League titles and the Champions League.

‌



However, his time on the pitch diminished rapidly and he sought a loan move after being left out of Pep Guardiola's plans. Grealish joined Everton for the 2025/26 campaign and regained his old form with six assists in 22 games.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Jack Grealish offered Man City lifeline by Enzo Maresca after Pep Guardiola snub READ MORE :

Enzo Maresca insists Man City won't repeat what Man Utd did after Sir Alex Ferguson READ MORE :

But a stress fracture in his foot killed his momentum and left him sidelined. The 30-year-old now has a decision to make: whether he tries to find a way under Enzo Maresca or move on to pastures new.

‌



A return to Villa could've been the dream for the boyhood fan, who joined the club aged six and became one of their modern heroes. Grealish appeared 213 times in claret and blue, making 75 goal contributions and leading them back to the Premier League as captain in 2019.

View 3 Images Alejandro Garnacho's arrival in Birmingham throws a wrench into the plans (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

The money from his transfer to City helped stabilise Villa and Grealish shared his die-hard love with one clear message. He said: "I'll always be a Villa fan. I love this club with all my heart and I hope you understand my reasons for seeking a new challenge. The club are in great hands, the manager, the lads, the new signings coming in. It's an exciting time to be a Villa fan. I'll see you all again soon. Until next time. UTV."

‌



A return for the winger looks like a no-brainer for both parties, with former teammate Robert Snodgrass telling OLBG that the club simply have to think 'why not.' He said: "Listen, it is certainly possible that there might be a few openings available at Villa, as they may be looking to bolster their ranks. You just never know what a club like that might be planning.

View 3 Images Now Grealish will need to fight for his dream transfer (Image: Laurence Griffiths/Getty Images)

"When you look at the overall situation, I think Jack would absolutely love a return to that environment. It's well-documented that he is a die-hard Villa fan who is incredibly passionate about that club, so if the chance arose, you really have to think why not?"

Article continues below

Now, this transfer has become more difficult following Garnacho's arrival in Birmingham. The 22-year-old will provide cover in Grealish's natural position while also having age and speed on his side.

The left winger is eight years Garnacho's senior and has struggled with injury in recent seasons.

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha made thoughts clear after taking Marcus Rashford's shirt number at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha made thoughts clear after taking Marcus Rashford's shirt number at Man Utd

Matheus Cunha made a telling comment about Marcus Rashford after taking the forward's Manchester United shirt number

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford will return to Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Matheus Cunha expressed how much of an honour it was to take Marcus Rashford’s No.10 shirt after he signed for Manchester United. Cunha was signed last summer from Wolves for a fee of £62.5million.

‌



The Brazilian forward was handed the jersey number when it was freed up following Rashford’s own move to Barcelona on a season-long loan with an option to buy. Many believed the Englishman would never return to his boyhood club, given the acrimonious nature of his departure following a falling out with then-head coach Ruben Amorim.

‌



But Barcelona opted not to activate their £26m purchase option this summer and, with Michael Carrick now in charge instead of Amorim, Rashford is set to return to United. The 28-year-old will re-join the side’s pre-season training following his post-World Cup summer break.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It is reported that Rashford’s representatives have had encouraging discussions with United about his pre-season return to Carrington. However, the forward will face an uncomfortable, awkward situation whereby he will no longer have his old iconic jersey, having lost his shirt number while away from Old Trafford.

Cunha, 27, will still occupy the number despite Rashford’s return. Prior to notching 10 goals and four assists in 35 appearances in his first season at Old Trafford last term, the Brazil international mentioned how he was relishing the chance to follow in the footsteps of former United players who wore the No.10 shirt, including Rashford.

‌



Marcus Rashford will have to confront awkward Man Utd reality when he returns to Old Trafford READ MORE :

Man Utd hatch transfer plan as Man City star Rodri gives green light to summer move READ MORE :

He admitted it was a "privilege" to wear it and hoped it would inspire him to match the exploits of his illustrious predecessors at United. Cunha said: "I can mention many players that used this shirt. It's so easy for me. Of course, I think the one that I always think about when I see this number in this shirt for me was Wayne Rooney. He was someone that I grew up to watch him play and I have watched many games now.

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha took the No.10 jersey in Rashford's absence (Image: Getty )

"Then I swapped shirts with Marcus after a game. I have his shirt in my home. But, of course, we know many players used this shirt – Ruud van Nistelrooy and Zlatan Ibrahimovic. It's the dream not only to use the shirt, but with all the history they have around the number, it's something beautiful that I have the privilege to do it.

Article continues below

"With every single number, it will be a pleasure to wear the shirt. But, yeah, with this one it’s something different. Then, of course, the responsibility comes."

Previous wearers of the No.10 shirt at United include Denis Law, Teddy Sheringham, Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy and Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
