Sports.title: Hamilton demoted to fifth on grid for impeding Piastri | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has been given a three-place grid drop for impeding Oscar Piastri at the end of qualifying.

Piastri caught Hamilton at turn one as the McLaren driver began his final flying run. After being held up by the Ferrari, Piastri backed off and gestured at his rival – Hamilton gave an apologetic wave in reaction.

Hamilton had the quickest time in the session and was preparing to begin his final run when he had his encounter with Piastri. He admitted afterwards his concern over the incident affected his final lap.

The stewards subsequently summoned both drivers over the incident. They ruled Hamilton received a late warning about Piastri from his team and should have left him space.

Hamilton said he did not have enough time to react to the warning Piastri was behind him. “I was told literally when he was at the apex behind me, so I had no idea he was coming,” he said.

“I thought everyone was on an out-lap. Everyone came out behind me. I was the first out, so I thought everyone had finished their lap.

“Charles, I think, was the car that was behind me when I left the pit lane, as far as I was aware. So it’s crazy, because it had been clean, and obviously it wasn’t intentional.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton’s three-place grid drop moves him from second on the grid to fifth. His team mate Charles Leclerc takes his place on the front row.

The stewards’ verdict on Hamilton

The stewards heard from the driver of car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), the driver of car 81 (Oscar Piastri), team representatives and reviewed video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. At the approach to turn one, car 44 was travelling at a significantly reduced speed on the racing line while car 81 was approaching on a push lap. The driver of car 44 explained that he had just completed a fast lap and did not receive the team’s radio message regarding the approaching car 81 until the latter was already in close proximity. He further stated that, due to the positioning of his car on the track, car 81 was not visible in his mirrors. Car 81, which was on a push lap, was forced to take avoiding action by running wide and being obliged to abort the lap. Having examined the available evidence, the stewards determined that car 44 unnecessarily impeded car 81 during qualifying. In accordance with the FIA F1 Regulations and the established penalty guidelines for this type of infringement in qualifying, the stewards impose a three-place grid penalty on the driver of car 44.

Sports.title: Norris snatches pole position off Hamilton, Antonelli under investigation | 2026 Hungarian GP qualifying report
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed his first pole position as reigning world champion with a superb final lap in qualifying at the Hungaroring.

The McLaren driver was one of few people to improve on their final runs in Q3. Lewis Hamilton held provisional pole position after the first runs but failed to find any further time, allowing Norris to pip him by just 0.012 seconds.

Hamilton therefore fell to second on the grid ahead of Charles Leclerc. Andrea Kimi Antonelli had to settle for fourth place despite beginning his final lap well – he encountered yellow flags at the final corner.

The yellow flags were caused by Max Verstappen, who had his third significant spin in the last four weekends. As in Austria, it occured late in qualifying, the Red Bull driver spinning at the final corner.

Verstappen’s spin also obliged George Russell to slow down. The Mercedes driver then came to a stop at turn one immediately after finishing his final lap. Verstappen and Russell will line up immediately behind Oscar Piastri. The McLaren driver and Hamilton are under investigation for a potential impeding incident.

Isack Hadjar rebounded from a spin in Q2 to claim eighth on the grid ahead of Arvid Lindblad and Nico Hulkenberg. Antonelli also had a drama in Q2 as his first flying lap was deleted as he cut the inside of turn seven, and the decision came so late he had already committed to starting his final run on a used set of tyres. Nonetheless, he pulled out a quick enough time on old rubber to reach the top 10.

However as the session came to an end race control announced Antonelli was under investigation for a potential yellow flag infringement.

Aston Martin’s upgraded car proved quick enough for the team to earn their first fully-merited participation in the second round of qualifying this year (Fernando Alonso have reached SQ2 in Montreal, but not participated in it, after crashing). He did his final run in Q2 early, however, and ended up 16th.

Liam Lawson failed to join his team mate in the final 10, saying the Racing Bulls was difficulty to drive. He took 11th ahead of the Alpines. Gabriel Bortoleto, 14th, lost his first attempt to a track limits infringement like Antonelli.

Alonso reached Q2 at the expense of Oliver Bearman, who had been less happy with the balance of the Haas than his team mate after sitting out first practice. The dejected Williams pair also fell at the first hurdle.

Lance Stroll, whose Friday was badly disrupted by a suspension failure, ended up half a second behind Alonso in 20th place. The Cadillac drivers occupied the back row.

Sports.title: Norris heads Hamilton in final practice at the Hungaring | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris denied Ferrari a sweep of all three practice sessions for the Hungarian Grand Prix, setting the fastest time of the weekend so far in his McLaren.

With the soft tyres surprisingly proving resilient enough to yield two competitive times, Norris lowered the benchmark to a 1’17.939. That ensured he came out on top after a spate of runs by the drivers from the leading teams.

Norris displaced Lewis Hamilton from the top of the times by a tenth of a second, the Ferrari driver enjoying a strong run through the final sector. There was almost nothing to choose between him and Andrea Kimi Antonelli in third.

Charles Leclerc put his Ferrari fourth while Oscar Piastri and George Russell were each almost half a second slower than their respective team mates.

The Red Bull drivers did not look especially happy with their cars, Isack Hadjar branding his “undriveable” after a mistake at turn 12. Max Verstappen was the quickest of the pair, albeit seven-tenths of a second off Norris.

Liam Lawson took ninth for Racing Bulls but his team mate Arvid Lindblad missed most of the session with a technical problem. He emerged from the pits just in time for a single flying run. The Audi drivers completed the top half of the field.

Sergio Perez failed to set a time as he came to a stop immediately after leaving the pits. The Cadillac driver’s rear brakes were smoking alarmingly, prompting race control to red-flag the session.

Without that, the Williams drivers might have ended the session slowest of all. Valtteri Bottas outpaced his former team’s drivers and the upgraded Aston Martins were ahead of all four.

Fernando Alonso ended practice just under two-and-a-half seconds off the pace, but set his time early in the session, indicating there could be more pace in the heavily revised AMR26. The team had a fright early in the session, however, when Alonso caught his team mate at turn 12, who did not seem to realise he was there, provoking a worrying near-miss.

Sports.title: Gene Tunney Halts Tom Heeney In Final Championship Defense
Sports.content:
A paid crowd of 43,191 attended, with thousands more admitted on complimentary tickets. The gate reached approximately $691,014.50, producing a net of about $521,422 after expenses. Tunney received a remarkable $525,000 purse, while Heeney earned $100,000. Motion picture rights generated another $20,000. Radio rights produced $15,000.

Referee Eddie Forbes officiated. Charles F. Mathison and Tom Flynn served as judges.

Heeney fought exactly as expected, charging forward in an effort to force exchanges at close range. Tunney relied on disciplined footwork. His steady left jab repeatedly disrupted the challenger before sharp counters landed cleanly. Much of the early action featured clinches as Heeney struggled to trap the champion along the ropes.

By the eighth round, Tunney had opened a damaging cut over Heeney’s left eye. The punishment increased in the 10th when a double jab followed by a chopping right hand dropped the challenger near the ropes. Heeney rose immediately. He kept pressing forward despite absorbing heavy punishment.

The finish came at 2:52 of the 11th round. Tunney unloaded another sustained attack, but Heeney refused to fall. Seeing the exhausted challenger taking unanswered punches, Forbes stepped between them and awarded Tunney a technical knockout victory.

The victory became the final chapter of one of boxing’s finest championship careers. Tunney retired as heavyweight champion. Later that year, The Ring magazine selected him as its inaugural Fighter of the Year for 1928. Heeney earned lasting respect for his determination, although the defeat effectively ended his pursuit of the world heavyweight title.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Outworks Errol Spence Jr. Over 12 Rounds
Sports.content:
The opening rounds were competitive. Tszyu stunned Spence with a right hand in the closing seconds of the first round, but Spence answered in the second with effective body work and a hard left that briefly shifted the momentum. The third round also favored Spence, although Tszyu finished strongly with another right hand.

Tszyu regained momentum in the fourth before another close fifth round. He began taking control in the sixth and seventh, landing the cleaner punches while increasing his work rate. Both fighters developed swelling under their left eyes.

Referee Will Soulos warned Spence several times for low blows in the eighth round as blood began flowing from Spence’s nose. Tszyu continued pressing the action over the final four rounds, repeatedly landing right hands while Spence’s output slowed.

Tszyu finished strongly in the twelfth, rocking Spence with another right hand during the closing minute to seal the victory.

Following the decision, Spence applauded Tszyu before announcing his retirement from boxing.

Reda Defeats Fleming

In the co-feature, Ahmad “Bloodshot” Reda earned a unanimous decision over former Olympian Paul “Showtime” Fleming after 10 entertaining rounds.

Reda controlled most of the early action with his speed and activity, although Fleming enjoyed his best success in the fifth after inviting Reda to exchange while standing against the ropes.

A clash of heads opened a cut over Fleming’s left eyebrow in the seventh. Reda continued to outwork the veteran over the closing rounds despite suffering a cut late in the fight.

The judges scored the bout 99-91, 97-93 and 96-94.

Peters Stops Actis

Australian Olympian Callum “50 Cal” Peters remained unbeaten by stopping Ivan “Gringo” Actis in the seventh round.

The opening rounds featured heavy exchanges before Peters gradually took control with sharper punching. A right hand opened a cut over Actis’ left eye in the fourth, and Peters continued to wear him down until referee Will Soulos halted the bout at 55 seconds of Round 7.

Aokuso Knocks Out Tejeda

Former Olympian Paulo “Sweet P” Aokuso captured the vacant IBF Intercontinental light heavyweight title with a dramatic 10th-round knockout of Luis Antonio Tejeda.

Aokuso rocked Tejeda early, but the Dominican battled back and had the Australian badly hurt against the ropes during the seventh round.

The fight ended suddenly in the final round when Aokuso landed a crushing counter left hand that flattened Tejeda for the count.

Rahimi Wins Pro Debut

Former Olympian Tina Rahimi opened her professional career with a unanimous decision over Sacha Ryan Dryden.

Rahimi boxed well throughout the four-round contest, using her speed and combinations to edge most of the rounds before finishing strongly.

The judges scored it 40-36, 40-36 and 39-37.

Grach Defeats Pluto

Heavyweight Brandon “The Bull” Grach earned a unanimous decision over Ike “From Pluto” Pluto in a five-round battle.

Grach hurt Pluto with a right hand in the third round and scored a knockdown in the fourth. Pluto rallied late and landed several solid punches in the fifth, but Grach had already done enough to secure the victory.

The judges scored the fight 49-45, 49-45 and 48-46.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer for the main event.

Sports.title: Errol Spence Jr. Retires After Tim Tszyu Loss
Sports.content:
Errol Spence Jr. brought his boxing career to an end Saturday night after losing a unanimous decision to Tim Tszyu, saying his health, family and financial security made retirement an easy choice. The former unified welterweight champion made the announcement moments after suffering a 12-round defeat at Afterpay Arena in Sydney, Australia.

“It was a great fight. Congratulations to Tim and Jeff Fenech. It was a good showing by Tim. I answered a lot of questions about myself, and now it’s time to go home with my family and start a new life,” Spence said before confirming his decision. “Yeah, for sure. I’ve got my faculties intact. My money is good and working for itself, so everything’s good, man. I’ve got a beautiful family and I thank God that I’m able to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family by my side. Everything’s going to go well.”

The judges scored the fight 117-111, 117-111 and 118-110 for Tszyu, who gradually took control after a competitive opening. Spence was returning from a layoff of nearly three years and showed flashes of his former ability, but Tszyu’s pressure and higher punch output proved decisive over the second half of the contest.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Hands Errol Spence Jr. Tough Return Defeat
Sports.content:
“Middleweight is my new division and I feel strong,” said Tszyu. “This was one hell of a show. There were sleepless nights where I was thinking about facing a legend like Spence. I understand why he’s one of the greats.”

The opening rounds were competitive, with Spence finding success behind his jab and left hand while investing in body shots. Tszyu refused to give ground, walking the former unified welterweight champion down and landing hard right hands whenever Spence paused in front of him.

The fight changed as the rounds wore on.

Tszyu began timing Spence with increasing regularity, connecting with right hands to the head and body while forcing the Texan backward. Spence’s timing and punch output declined as the pace caught up with him, a predictable challenge after such a lengthy absence from the ring.

By the championship rounds, Tszyu had taken firm control. Spence continued fighting back and showed the toughness that defined much of his career, but he spent long stretches covering up, holding and trying to slow the Australian’s momentum. Tszyu never allowed him to regain control, continuing to press forward and outwork him until the final bell.

“The advice from corner was to get in there,” said Tszyu. “I’m trying to replicate Kostya Tszyu and my trainer Jeff Fenech. if I can be half as great as them, I’ll go down as a great man.”

The victory gives Tszyu one of the biggest wins of his career and strengthens his position among the leading names at 160 pounds. He entered the bout under pressure after a difficult run over the last two years, but responded with a disciplined performance against one of boxing’s most accomplished former champions.

“I’d love to fight for a world title. I want Erislandy Lara and all the champions,” said Tszyu. “That’s what I’m aiming for. But beating a great like Errol Spence tops any world title for me.”

After the fight, Spence addressed his future while giving Tszyu credit for his performance.

“It was a good fight and congratulation to Tim,” said Spence. “It’s been a great event and everyone has treated me well. It was a good showing by Tim.

For Spence, the defeat raises fresh questions about what comes next. His decision to return after nearly three years away was one of the sport’s biggest stories, yet the layoff appeared to take its toll as the fight progressed. Although he lasted the full 12 rounds, Tszyu’s steady pressure exposed the difficulty of returning against a proven contender without a tune-up first.

“I answered a lot of questions for myself and now it’s time to go home with my family and start a new life. I’ve got my faculties intact and my money is working for itself. I’m thankful to leave this sport with my family by my side.”

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Eyes Boots Ennis After Bloody Title Defense
Sports.content:
His ambition is understandable. Ennis owns the WBA and WBO titles at 154 pounds, making a unification bout one of the biggest opportunities in the division. Eddie Hearn also backed the idea after the fight, pointing toward a possible event in the United States later this year.

The bigger issue is recovery.

Kelly didn’t leave the ring looking like someone ready to begin another training camp. Agyarko landed plenty of hard punches throughout the contest, and Kelly’s injuries weren’t limited to accidental head clashes. He also complained afterward that the referee allowed too much roughhouse work, describing stretches of the contest as feeling like “an MMA fight.”

That criticism comes with some irony. Kelly repeatedly landed rabbit punches during the fight and eventually had a point deducted for hitting behind Agyarko’s head. Both fighters contributed to the physical nature of the contest.

Kelly has made it clear he wants Ennis next. The bigger question is how long it will take for the damage from the Agyarko fight to heal before he can begin preparing for a unification bout.

Sports.title: Errol Spence Jr vs Tim Tszyu Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Callum Peters remained unbeaten with a seventh-round TKO over Ivan Ricardo Actis in their 10-round middleweight contest. After both men traded hard shots early, Peters gradually pulled away by landing the cleaner punches and forcing Actis onto the defensive. Actis refused to go quietly but absorbed sustained punishment, prompting the referee to stop the fight in the seventh round. The victory extended Peters’ knockout streak and handed Actis the first defeat of his professional career.

Paulo Aokuso scored a dramatic 10th-round knockout over Luis Antonio Tejeda to capture the vacant IBF Inter-Continental light heavyweight title. Aokuso started well before Tejeda battled back, hurting the Australian during the middle rounds and forcing him through several difficult moments. After regaining control late, Aokuso ended the fight with a crushing left hand that left Tejeda unconscious in one of the card’s most spectacular finishes. The victory gave Aokuso the biggest win of his career and provided an early Knockout of the Year candidate.

Brandon Grach earned a unanimous decision over Ike Pluto in a spirited five-round heavyweight opener after both fighters accepted the bout on roughly 24 hours’ notice. Grach applied steady pressure throughout while Pluto fired back in an entertaining contest that had the Sydney crowd engaged from the opening bell. The judges scored it 49-45, 49-45 and 48-46 in Grach’s favor after five action-packed rounds. Both heavyweights received praise for stepping in at the last minute and delivering one of the card’s most entertaining fights.

Tina Rahimi made a successful professional debut with a unanimous decision over Sacha Ryan Dryden in a four-round contest. The former Australian Olympian controlled the action with sharp combinations, quick footwork and effective defense while consistently landing the cleaner punches. Rahimi closed the fight strongly, overwhelming Dryden in the final moments to secure scores of 40-36, 40-36 and 39-37. The victory marked an impressive start to Rahimi’s professional career in front of her hometown fans in Sydney.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Claims Keyshawn Davis Has Gone Missing
Sports.content:
Under the WBO order, the winning bid would be split 75 percent to Haney as champion and 25 percent to Davis as the mandatory challenger. The organization has set a minimum bid of $200,000, although the sides remain free to reach their own agreement before the scheduled hearing.

Bill Haney’s latest post appears aimed at increasing the pressure with little time left on the negotiating clock. Rather than discussing specific terms, he questioned Keyshawn Davis’ willingness to complete a deal while portraying the challenger as absent during one of the biggest business opportunities of his career.

No agreement between the camps has been announced, leaving Monday’s purse bid on course unless a deal is reached beforehand, with time still remaining.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Thought Anthony Joshua’s Career Was Over
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua’s dramatic comeback knockout of Kristian Prenga left Eddie Hearn celebrating by the end of the night, but the Matchroom promoter admitted his thoughts were very different after the opening round.

Joshua climbed off the canvas twice before stopping Prenga in the second round at the Jeddah Superdome, surviving a scare that nearly derailed his comeback.



“When he got dropped, I was like, that’s career over,” Hearn said to Charlie Parsons at The Stomping Ground. “I’m kind of thinking to myself, ‘You know what? I’m proud of him for even getting back in the ring.’ If it ends like this, he should be really proud of the fact that he even returned to boxing. He had 24 breaks in his ribs or something. He couldn’t move, was in hospital for weeks and weeks. To even be in the ring was incredible.” Hearn said Joshua’s recovery changed everything. “He held on. He walked onto an uppercut and somehow found a way to recover,” Hearn said. “When he got back to the stool, I felt if he could just find his legs, this guy had thrown a lot of punches in the first round and was going to wear himself out. AJ has incredible knockout power. It doesn’t matter if he’s hurt. He has the ability to take you out with one punch.” Joshua answered those concerns by stopping Prenga in the second round, but Hearn did not ignore the warning signs. He believes the performance should not overshadow the determination Joshua displayed by overcoming the knockdowns and finishing the fight. Share via: Facebook

Ghana News.title: Researchers urged to make academic work useful beyond journals
Ghana News.content:
Research funded with public money should not remain hidden behind academic journals or expensive paywalls, the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED) says, urging researchers to communicate their findings in language that ordinary people can understand and use.

The call was made during a special training workshop organised by USTED’s Publication Board to help researchers, lecturers and senior members transform academic studies into compelling stories for print, radio, television and digital media.

Speaking at the workshop, USTED’s Pro Vice Chancellor, Prof Isaac Boateng, said research should not be judged only by the number of papers published or citations received, but by the impact it creates in society.

“Research that is not communicated effectively is knowledge in prison.”

He said researchers spend months and sometimes years collecting data, analysing evidence and publishing their findings, but much of that knowledge often remains within academic circles.

Prof Boateng urged researchers to see communication as an important part of the research process rather than something considered after publication.

“Do not measure success only by publication. Measure success by transformation.”

He challenged researchers to focus on the real-world impact of their work. “Do not ask merely was my paper published? Ask whose life changed because of my research.”

He said research should contribute to improving livelihoods, strengthening industries and solving problems affecting communities.

USTED seeks to close research communication gap

The Chairman of the USTED Publication Board, Dr Christopher Owusu-Ansah, said the workshop was organised because of the gap between research produced by universities and the wider public.

He said many studies from the Global South are published in international journals where access is often limited by subscription fees and paywalls.

“The research that is done is buried behind paywalls.”

Dr Owusu-Ansah said this was particularly important because a significant amount of research is supported through public resources.

He argued that citizens should have access to research findings that can influence policies and national development.

“It is only proper and fair that the research that is done is also thrown into the public space, not just behind paywalls, so that the public will be able to understand the research that is done and which would help to promote proper policies and national development.”

To help address this challenge, the university invited journalists from the West African Journalists for Environment, Science, Health and Agriculture (WAJESHA) to lead practical sessions on communicating research to wider audiences.

The workshop formed part of WAJESHA’s wider effort to help universities and research institutions communicate science and academic research in ways that can inform public understanding and policymaking.

Turning research into stories people can understand

Drawing on newsroom experience, the trainers demonstrated how academic studies can be turned into stories that meet the needs of newspapers, broadcasters and digital platforms without compromising scientific accuracy.

The training began with a masterclass led by New Media Editor at WAJESHA, Daniel Abugri, who focused on identifying the news value within academic research and helping participants understand what makes a finding relevant to the public.

“A study becomes news when people can see how it affects their lives,” Daniel stated.

Participants were then taken through how to write research in a style that journalists can use during a session led by Director of WAJESHA, Engr. Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen.

He said many researchers produce valuable studies but often struggle to explain their importance beyond academic circles.

“Researchers often write excellent studies but fail to explain why their findings matter to ordinary people.”

The final session, facilitated by Engr. Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen, Daniel Abugri and an independent film producer, Afrifa Smith Charles, focused on adapting research for television, radio and digital platforms.

Afrifa highlighted the difference between academic writing and television storytelling.

“A three-minute video story demands a different approach from a 30-page journal article.”

Together, the sessions guided participants through identifying the news in research, presenting findings in clear language and adapting academic work for different media platforms.

Researchers rethink how they communicate findings

For some participants, the training highlighted the need to move beyond traditional academic communication.

Dr Daniel Nimo at the Department of Interdisciplinary Studies, said the workshop had helped him understand how research findings could be transformed into stories that ordinary people could follow.

“This workshop has been very effective to the extent that it has enlightened some of us to know how we can convert our research work into news where anybody can read to get the understanding,” he indicated.

He said researchers often rely on technical language and statistical explanations that may not be easily understood outside academic environments.

The training, he said, had demonstrated the importance of presenting research in simpler language.

A lecturer at the Civil Engineering Department at the Faculty of Engineering and Technology, Engr Anna Amankwah Minkah, said academic writing is usually designed for specialists within specific fields.

“Most of our writing is tailored to research and academia,” she pointed out.

She said researchers whose work is intended to influence society must communicate differently.

“We should be able to communicate in a way that society will easily grasp what we are trying to say, what our findings are,” she added.

According to her, “this workshop has helped me realise that we need to break it down in the simple, ordinary language so that everybody gets to know what we are finding in our study.”

The final stage of the workshop featured a WAJESHA Capstone Newsroom Simulation, group presentations and participant reflections, allowing researchers to apply the skills gained during the sessions.

For USTED, the objective is to ensure that research does not end with publication but reaches the people whose lives it is intended to improve.

As Professor Boateng reminded participants that, “let us become researchers who write for journals and speak to society.”

Ghana News.title: Unemployed man gets six-month jail term for committing three offences
Ghana News.content:
Bright Oduro, aged 19 years and unemployed, has been jailed for six months by the Asante Abuakwa Circuit Court in the Atwima Nwabiagya South Municipality for committing three offences at Abuakwa.

He pleaded guilty to the charges of unlawful entry, causing unlawful damage and attempted stealing.

He was convicted on his own plea.

Police Detective Chief Inspector Alexander Agbekpornu told the court presided by Mrs Philomena Ansaah Asiedu, that the complainant, Kojo Isaac, a mason and the accused resided respectively at Abuakwa-Boaso and Nsonyameye.

On July 17, 2026, at about 1000 hours, the complainant returned home from work and saw his burglar proof exit gate covered with a black pair of trousers.

He inspected the cloth and detected that the burglar proof, valued at GHS 600.00, has been damaged; so he became suspicious and called his wife from her workplace and told her to go and check in the house, whiles he stood back and watched.

He then saw the accused trying to escape from the house, so he arrested and handed him over to the Abuakwa Police.

In his caution statement, the accused person admitted and told the police that he damaged the burglar proof, entered without any permission, purposely to steal, but after seeing the complainant’s wife, he became afraid and wanted to run away.

After further investigations, he was charged and brought before the court.

Ghana News.title: Chaos mar NDC branch elections in Assin Central Constituency
Ghana News.content:
Violence erupted at the National Democratic Congress (NDC) branch executive elections in the Assin Central Constituency, after a deputy constituency youth organiser aspirant was allegedly assaulted by a group of unidentified men at the Bamboo Factory polling station in Assin Fosu.

The victim, Mr Yaw Owusu, sustained serious injuries and was initially rushed to the St. Francis Xavier Hospital at Assin Fosu before being referred to the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital for specialised treatment.

Mr Owusu said the violence followed a disagreement over alleged electoral irregularities during the branch women’s organiser election.

He claimed election officials initially announced that 17 delegates were present to vote, but 25 ballots were counted after voting, prompting himself and some supporters to question what they believed was over-voting.

He alleged that, shortly after raising concerns, a group of men believed to be affiliated to the opposing camp attacked him with sticks and sharp objects, leaving him with multiple injuries.

“They ended up twisting my neck,” he narrated.

Medical reports indicated that he suffered a fractured neck, eye injury, as well as head and suspected spinal injuries and because of the severity of his condition, he was referred to the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital for further treatment.

The injured aspirant has appealed to the National Executives of the NDC, particularly the Party’s National Chairman, Mr Johnson Asiedu Nketia, to intervene and called on the police to ensure that those responsible for the attack were identified and brought to justice.

The assault has been reported to the Central North Regional Police Command, which has launched investigations into the incident.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi knew he would be convicted – Appiah-Kubi
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Andy Appiah-Kubi has revealed that the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Wontumi, had prior knowledge that he would be convicted before appearing in court on the day judgment was delivered in the Samreboi illegal mining case.

Speaking on Accra-based TV3, Mr Appiah-Kubi, who was formerly Wontumi’s lawyer, said he had even shared details of the expected judgment with him before the court’s decision was announced.

“Chairman Wontumi had prior information that he would be convicted. He told me the content of the judgement. He told me that he will be jailed for twenty years,” he stated.

The lawyer, however, disagreed with the 20-year prison sentence, arguing that the court erred in law by treating Chairman Wontumi and Akonta Mining as one and the same.

According to him, the evidence presented during the trial did not justify the court’s conclusion.

“The evidence on the ground does not support the judgment. Per the company law, the company is different from the owner or shareholder,” he said.

Mr Appiah-Kubi indicated that the issue would form a key part of the appeal against the conviction.

“This will form the basis of our appeal,” he added.

He further disclosed that because Chairman Wontumi anticipated the outcome of the case, he had instructed him earlier that day to file an appeal should the court convict him.

Chairman Wontumi was sentenced by the Accra High Court on July 20 to 20 years’ imprisonment with hard labour after being convicted on illegal mining-related offences.

In her 59-page judgment, Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay said the sentence was intended to serve as a deterrent and underscore the seriousness of environmental crimes.

“The Court takes notice of the gravity of the offences, and the need for deterrence to avert the environmental disaster that might befall the nation the more law enforcement stays aloof and allows illegal mining activities to persist in the country,” she wrote.

The judge also noted that the offences undermined Ghana’s mining regulatory framework and contributed to environmental destruction.

“The offences in this case relate to illegal exploitation of mineral resources, which are the property of the state.

“The conduct of the 1st and 3rd accused persons undermines the regulatory framework for the mining sector and contributes to environmental degradation associated with illegal mining.”

Justice Kocuvie-Tay explained that although the offences were serious, she took into account Chairman Wontumi’s status as a first-time offender when determining the sentence.

“Taking into account the fact that the 1st and 3rd accused persons are 1st-time offenders and generally their plea in mitigation, the court sentences the accused persons as follows: On count 1, the 1st accused is sentenced to serve a term of 20 years imprisonment in hard labour, and also to a fine of 10,000 penalty units; in default serve 3 years in hard labour.”

She added that the court imposed the same sentence on count four, while Akonta Mining, the third accused, was fined 15,000 penalty units on counts three and six, with the custodial sentences to run concurrently.

Ghana News.title: GIMPA graduates tasks to master modern digital tools to be competitive
Ghana News.content:
Nana Oye Bampoe Addo, the Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Finance and Administration, has advised GIMPA graduates to master the construction of digital tools in their fields of disciplines to be competitive in the field of work.

She said modern ICT tools like AI coding and robotics would make them competent and exceptional ahead of their peers in the job market.

Nana Bampoe Addo said this at the weekend during the 26th Congregation of Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) in Accra for graduate and undergraduate students.

She encouraged the graduates to leverage on the knowledge acquired from GIMPA but stay alert to technology disruptions.

“Learn to build, not merely to consume. The world is shifting from mechanical thinking towards systems that run themselves, tracking performance, forecasting markets, and managing entire administrative functions on autopilots,” she said.

She urged the graduates to guard their creativity, their talents, their passion, and their originality, stressing, “Do not let a tool replace your thinking, only extend it as a support.”

Nana Oye Addo said no digital ambition survives without safety, underscoring the government’s intervention to match innovation with protection.

“The cybersecurity authority has sustained operations against cybercrime networks, arresting scores of suspects in coordinated actions with the Ghana Police Service,” she said.

She said the government had treated technology as a pillar of national strategy and not as an afterthought.

“Through the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology, and Innovation, the country has launched Ghana’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025 to 2035, built on eight pillars from education to public sector deployment.”

She said the launch of the National AI Fund, beginning with Ghc 5 billion and scaling to Ghc 50 billion by 2035. We have a planned $250 million National AI Computing Center, which will be the next center for research and enterprise.

The government, she stated, had extended AI training with support from the United Nations Development Planning, which had been extended to ministers, with performance indicators now tracking digital adoption across the sectors.

“We also have a curriculum review committee introducing coding, robotics, and AI from the basic school level,” she said.

Prof Samuel Kwaku Bonsu, Rector of GIMPA, urged the students to strive to keep the spirit and image of the institution in their endeavours.

“Be the best ambassadors of GIMPA; we are here to support you and the nation as a whole,” he said.

The Rector announced that the institute was finalizing the building of a 3,000-seator stadium for sports activities.

Ms Samuela Amma Boakye-Appiah, the overall best graduating student, said the achievement was a testament to the goodness of God.

Ms Boakye-Appiah, who graduated with a Master of Laws degree in International Criminal Law and Justice, said the graduates had been transformed and equipped by solid teaching to impact society positively.

He commended the management of GIMPA for moulding and sharpening their minds and pledged to carry these values with ethical responsibility.

Ghana News.title: Oti High Court adjourns NPP Krachi East Organiser election dispute to October
Ghana News.content:
The High Court in Dambai has adjourned to October 9, 2026, the case challenging the outcome of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Krachi East Constituency Organiser election.

The suit was filed by Mr Justice Mensah, who is contesting the conduct and outcome of the constituency organiser election.

At the hearing, the court directed the defendants, Mr Jacob Addo, the Electoral Commission (EC) and the New Patriotic Party (NPP), to file their affidavits in opposition to the claims contained in the plaintiff’s application.

The court said the respondents must formally respond to the allegations before the substantive issues in the case could be determined.

After hearing preliminary submissions, the presiding judge, Justice Dr Moses Bedima Duut, adjourned the matter to October 9, for further proceedings.

The dispute arose from the recent NPP Krachi East Constituency executive elections, where disagreement emerged over the declaration of the organiser position.

The election became contentious after an initial declaration of results was followed by a recount, which subsequently declared Mr Jacob Addo the winner.

The development sparked protests by some party supporters, leading to the temporary closure of the NPP constituency office, before the matter was referred to the High Court for adjudication.

The outcome of the case is expected to determine the legitimacy of the organiser election and could have significant implications for the party’s leadership in the constituency ahead of future political activities.

The parties are expected to comply with the court’s directives before the case resumes on October 9, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Court issues bench warrant for man accused of threatening EOCO staff
Ghana News.content:
An Accra Circuit Court has issued a bench warrant for the arrest of Kweku Osei Korankye Asiedu, also known as KOKA, a marketer, for failing to appear before it.

Asiedu was expected to answer charges of threat of death and publication of false news.

He is alleged to have threatened to kill staff of the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO).

When the case was called, Asiedu, who is also a communicator for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), was absent.

Chief Inspector Wisdom Alorwu, prosecuting, told the court that the accused had been duly notified to appear but failed to do so, describing his conduct as disrespectful to the court.

After hearing the prosecution, the court issued a bench warrant for Asiedu’s arrest and adjourned the case to August 25, 2026.

The prosecution said the complainants were staff of EOCO.

It said on July 14, 2026, Asiedu was invited for questioning over a video circulating on social media in which he allegedly threatened the lives of EOCO staff.

According to the prosecution, in a video recorded on May 29, 2026, the accused allegedly stated: “We know the officers’ houses, we know where they stay, and we will kill you.”

The prosecution further alleged that on July 13, 2026, Asiedu appeared in another video claiming that there was “an order from above, the Presidency, that no one should bring food to Dennis Miracles Aboagye,” who was then in EOCO custody assisting with investigations.

The prosecution said the statement was false and was intended to incite a breach of the peace, mislead the public and undermine EOCO officials in the lawful discharge of their duties.

It said that following the publication of the video, the driver of the Executive Director of EOCO was allegedly pursued by about 20 unidentified men on motorbikes, who were suspected to have intended to attack him.

The prosecution said the accused’s actions instilled fear among EOCO personnel as they carried out their lawful duties.

Asiedu was subsequently arrested and, during police investigations, allegedly admitted the offences in his caution statement.

Ghana News.title: Vice President Opoku-Agyemang engages Ghanaians in Maryland, United States
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has engaged with members of the Ghanaian community in Potomac, Maryland in the United States of America.

They were hosted by Mr Victor Smith, Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States.

A statement issued by the Office of the Vice President, said the Vice President acknowledged that Ghanaians abroad continued to play an important role in the national economy.

She said the Government remained mindful of their interests, appreciated their sacrifices, and took pride in their positive projection of the image of Ghana out there.

The Vice President spoke about the difficult economic circumstances inherited by the Government and the sacrifices required to stabilise the country.

She said with decisive leadership, prudent management, and the resilience of the Ghanaian people, the government was gradually restoring macroeconomic stability.

She noted that economic growth had exceeded expectations; inflation had eased, and the Cedi had stabilised.

“We are demonstrating our commitment to fiscal discipline by operating with fewer ministers, several of whom are holding parliamentary and ministerial responsibilities without support from deputies,” she said.

She said through the ministry visits, she had received first-hand reports on their work, challenges, and progress.

The Vice President mentioned that the Government was prioritising interventions that served the common good of the people, which included investments in roads and other infrastructure, funding for the nation’s Senior High Schools, and expanded access to the National Health Insurance Scheme.

Other interventions were; increased resources for Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies through the District Assemblies Common Fund, and that clear guidelines were also being applied to ensure that these resources were directed towards the specific needs of communities.

Vice President Opoku-Agyemang also highlighted the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (MahamaCares), which was complemented by the Free Primary Healthcare initiative.

Adding that together, they were intended to treat noncommunicable diseases and strengthen preventive healthcare.

Vice President Opoku-Agyemang spoke about the Government’s efforts to respond to the diverse skills and employment needs of young people through the Youth Employment Agency and other job-creation programmes.

She said across several sectors, including energy, industry, and petroleum, reforms are underway to improve efficiency, strengthen local capacity, and support reliable power generation and economic productivity.

The Vice President said as Ghana advanced towards completing its debt restructuring and strengthens mechanisms such as the Sinking Fund to prepare for future shocks, the Government remained focused on confronting their difficulties honestly and on building greater resilience into the economy.

She encouraged the Ghanaian community to continue playing its role to help build the nation.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Japanese football legend ‘King Kazu’, 59, scores first goal in four years
World.content:
Japanese football icon Kazuyoshi Miura proved that age is just a number as the 59-year-old scored his first competitive goal in nearly four years.

The world’s oldest professional footballer, affectionately known as “King Kazu”, struck in the 52nd minute for Fukushima United on Saturday, as the J-League third division side thrashed Iwaki Furukawa 7-0 to advance in the Emperor’s Cup.

The goal prompted celebrations among teammates on the pitch and the bench before the veteran forward was substituted three minutes later.

It was Miura’s first competitive goal since November 2022, when he scored for Suzuka PG, now Atletico Suzuka, in a Japan Football League defeat by FC Osaka.

Enormous draw for fans

The former Japan international is preparing for a remarkable 42nd season as a professional after extending his loan spell with third-tier Fukushima United until June 2027.

Miura joined the club from Yokohama FC in December and will remain with Fukushima after making six appearances during a shortened 2026 campaign.

With Japan’s professional leagues set to switch from a spring-to-autumn schedule to an autumn-to-spring calendar, Miura will enter his 60s still playing professionally, adding another chapter to one of football’s most enduring careers.

Miura has previously insisted that he will not hang up his boots until he turns 60, and he continues to be an enormous draw for fans in Japan and abroad.

World.title: Photos: Wildfires in France drive 250,000 people from their homes
World.content:
A raging wildfire in southwest France has forced the evacuation of 55,000 more people, taking the total forced out of their homes to 220,000 in one region alone, as the flames creep ever closer to the city of Bordeaux.

Authorities in the Gironde region, where Bordeaux is located, issued overnight evacuation orders on Sunday for five more localities southwest of the historic city.

Gusting winds fed the flames overnight, accelerating the spread of the fire, which has been burning out of control since midweek, the authorities’ statement said.

The Gironde prefect also ordered the partial closure of a major highway heading southwest from Bordeaux.

The city’s mayor said the fire “is still at the gates of the metropolitan area”, having advanced to about 15km (9 miles) from Bordeaux at its closest point.

A second fire burning further south in the Landes region has also forced the evacuation of 30,000 people this week, taking the total driven out of their homes by the blazes to more than 250,000.

In neighbouring Spain, authorities have evacuated 70,000 people this week because of fires west of Madrid.

World.title: The Cockroach Effect: Modi vs India’s Gen Z
World.content:
Protests by India's Cockroach Janta Party suggest the young generation is becoming harder to intimidate and to silence.

New Delhi has been rocked by some of India’s biggest student protests in years, led by a viral movement known as the Cockroach Janta Party. After tens of thousands took to the streets over frustrations sparked by exam leaks, the Indian state mounted a heavy-handed response. Much of the mainstream media coverage has focused on the unrest rather than the grievances behind it, leaving alternative outlets to tell the full story.

World.title: Becoming the story: Injured journalists battle to leave Gaza for treatment
World.content:
Gaza journalists injured or battling illness during the war are demanding urgent medical evacuation, as they struggle to access life-saving treatment abroad.

Gaza City — Every morning, photojournalist Mohammed al-Qahouji tries to piece together a life that the war nearly took from him.

The 40-year-old freelance photographer says returning to journalism has become as much a physical challenge as an emotional one, every assignment interrupted by pain that shoots through his jaw, hand and back.

He has lived with this pain since he narrowly survived an Israeli air raid on January 7, 2024, when he reported on the recovery of the bodies in southern Gaza with Al Jazeera’s Hamza al-Dahdouh and Mustafa Abu Thuraya.

They were making their way back to their car when an Israeli warplane targeted the media crew, killing al-Dahdouh and Abu Thuraya, and seriously injuring al-Qahouji.

“We survived and kept driving because we never imagined that journalists documenting the aftermath would themselves become targets,” al-Qahouji told Al Jazeera.

“The paramedics placed me on top of Hamza al-Dahdouh’s body because they thought I had already died. Only later did they realise I was still alive.”

Stuck in Gaza

The blast tore his face from his eye to a major artery, requiring surgeons to implant titanium plates into his cheeks. His right hand sustained severe tendon and joint damage, with surgeons amputating one finger due to the severity of his injuries.

Injuries to his spine left him with a perpetual numbness in his lower limbs, making it difficult to stand or walk for long periods. More than two years later, his scars remain visible, and he has undergone more than 25 surgeries since then.



Doctors say he needs further reconstructive operations and long-term rehabilitation, but that is only available abroad.

He is now torn between a will to continue documenting Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and seeking specialised medical treatment abroad to end this persistent pain.

In a worn-out apartment he has rented since his original home was destroyed in an Israeli bombing in November 2023, al-Qahouji says he’s torn between continuing to document Israel’s genocidal war and leaving Gaza for life-changing surgery.

“I want to work again. It’s my only source of income, but my body doesn’t allow me to do what I used to,” he said.

“My injuries have taken away nearly 90 percent of my ability to work. Today, my dream is simple: to receive treatment and return to the field where I spent years documenting other people’s stories.”

Evacuations now

Members of the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate (PJS) held a sit-in at their headquarters in Gaza City on Wednesday, calling for the medical evacuation of injured and sick journalists from Gaza.

The party, including dozens of injured journalists, held photos of some of the 263 media workers killed by Israel during the war.

Ahed Farwana, secretary-general of the PJS, says more than 40 Palestinian journalists are currently living with serious war-related injuries or medical conditions that require treatment only available outside Gaza.

The syndicate has submitted medical files and documentation to international organisations, urging them to facilitate the journalists’ evacuation and guarantee their right to return once their treatment is completed.

“The right to medical treatment is a basic human right. It should never be denied because of war, siege or movement restrictions,” Farwana said.

The syndicate holds Israel responsible for preventing injured journalists from leaving Gaza but is also critical of international organisations for failing to do more than issuing “statements of concern”.

“The journalists documented this war from its first day, often at enormous personal risk,” Farwana says. “Today, many of them are no longer asking for anything except the chance to survive.”



For photojournalist Moaz al-Salhi, 34, attending the protest was a deeply personal experience, but he still had to swallow several painkillers to stay on his feet.

“I want to fight for my rights. I won’t stay waiting for death,” he says quietly. “Without the medication, I wouldn’t have been able to stand.”

A life in disease

Al-Salhi was diagnosed with severe Crohn’s disease in 2022 and was due to begin biological treatment in Israel in October 2023 when the war erupted.

He was left without the treatment he desperately needs and stuck in a cycle of repeated medical emergencies.

Al-Salhi scrolls through his phone and shows photographs and medical reports documenting his repeated hospital admissions since then.

Almost every week, his condition deteriorates to the point he loses consciousness and he is rushed again to hospital.

“I keep trying to resist the disease so I can continue working, but every time I think I’m getting better, I collapse again,” he said.

He now carries medication along with his camera equipment as he goes on assignments, but sometimes these roles are reversed, and he is one of the victims in this story.

“There were days when I covered stories with an IV cannula still in my hand. I was exhausted, but I wanted to keep telling people’s stories,” he said. “Now, I have become the story. I’m the one who needs treatment.”

The disease has taken a visible toll. He has lost significant weight and says his body grows weaker after every relapse.

His greatest fear, and that of his family, is that his condition will suddenly become irreversible if he remains trapped inside Gaza without access to specialised care.

“My family is terrified that one day my body simply won’t be able to take any more,” the father of two says. “I don’t want to reach that stage.”

Escaping Gaza

Leaving Gaza is now essential to prevent al-Salhi’s body from completely collapsing.

“I don’t want anything extraordinary,” he says. “I just want the chance to receive treatment, return to my family and go back to doing the work I love.”

Sadly, for al-Salhi and other injured or critically ill patients in Gaza, there are barriers for him to cross to access life-saving treatment abroad.

Israel has imposed a crippling siege on Gaza, restricting access in and out, leaving those in need of urgent medical attention stuck inside the strip.

At the same time, Israel’s systematic destruction of healthcare facilities has left many with medical conditions that might normally be treated in Gaza, helpless.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), more than 18,500 patients in Gaza currently require urgent medical evacuation for specialised care that is unavailable locally.

Since the start of the war, only a fraction of those in need have been able to leave through a limited medical evacuation mechanism. Thousands more remain on the waiting list.



The Rafah crossing – the main route for patients seeking treatment abroad out of Gaza – has been only partially and periodically opened by Israel to allow small numbers of sick Palestinians and their companions to leave for treatment in Egypt or other countries.

Aid agencies have repeatedly warned that restrictions on movement have delayed access to essential treatment for patients with serious injuries, chronic illnesses and conditions requiring specialised care unavailable in Gaza.

World.title: Israel debate boils over in the United States
World.content:

For US politicians, travelling to Israel has become a rite of passage and almost always involves going on an Israeli government-led PR tour of the country.

US Congressman Ro Khanna departed from that pattern this past week when he joined Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

What happened next – a confrontation with Israeli soldiers and the media reaction that followed – revealed a lot about the reality for Palestinians that Israel and its supporters are determined to conceal.
