World.title: Iraqi court seizes IQD 27 billion in Jumaili’s case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s anti-corruption judiciary has seized IQD 27 billion in cash as part of an ongoing investigation involving Adnan Al-Jumaili, the detained former Deputy Oil Minister for Refining Affairs, in one of the country’s latest high-profile corruption cases.

Judicial authorities said the money was recovered during investigations into alleged financial losses linked to projects overseen by the former official and other individuals connected to the case.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the media office of Iraq’s judiciary said Judge Diaa Jaafar, the investigating judge at the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, confirmed the seizure of IQD 27 billion.

According to the court, the funds were discovered after investigators traced financial proceeds allegedly generated through waste and irregularities in projects associated with Al-Jumaili and other suspects.

Officials said the cash had been hidden by several individuals believed to be involved in the case. The court said investigators are continuing to pursue additional suspects and trace other assets that may be linked to the alleged offenses.

Judicial authorities indicated that the investigation remains active as efforts continue to identify everyone involved and recover additional public funds, if any are found.

The judiciary also released photographs showing stacks of newly recovered banknotes arranged in large piles following the seizure. According to the statement, the images document the IQD 27 billion recovered during Sunday’s operation, which authorities said had been concealed by individuals connected to the former deputy minister.

Officials did not disclose how many people are under investigation or provide further details about the locations where the money was found.

The case is among several recent corruption investigations pursued by Iraq’s anti-corruption courts as authorities seek to recover public funds and hold officials accountable for alleged financial crimes.

The judiciary reiterated that investigations remain ongoing and that further legal action could follow as additional evidence emerges.

World.title: Iraq completes initial designs for Development Road Project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has completed the preliminary designs for its flagship Development Road Project and railway corridor, marking a major milestone as the government prepares to advance one of its largest infrastructure initiatives into the implementation phase.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Sunday that the initial designs are now 100% complete, with work shifting to detailed engineering plans covering infrastructure, bridges, railway stations, and technical facilities along the project’s route.

According to a source at the ministry’s media office, engineers have begun preparing the project’s detailed designs to ensure the corridor meets international engineering and construction standards. The next phase includes finalizing plans for the railway network, highways, bridges, stations, and supporting infrastructure before construction begins.

Officials described the transition as a key step toward launching the long-awaited project after completing the necessary preparatory stages.

The announcement follows a recent visit by Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu to Baghdad on July 21, where he held talks with Iraqi officials on strengthening cooperation in transport and communications.

During the meetings, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahb Al-Hassani and his Turkish counterpart agreed to accelerate technical planning and implementation procedures for the Development Road Project.

The ministry said both sides consider the corridor a transformative initiative that could reshape regional trade and economic cooperation. The ministry also revealed that Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has instructed officials to prepare a comprehensive financing mechanism for the project.

Securing funding will be a priority ahead of the project’s implementation and is expected to feature prominently during Al-Zaidi’s upcoming visit to Ankara, where discussions with Turkish officials will focus on advancing strategic cooperation and moving the project toward construction.

The Development Road Project is designed to create a major transport corridor linking Iraq’s ports with regional and international markets. The combined railway and highway network aims to connect the Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq with Turkey and Europe, positioning Iraq as a key logistics hub between Asia and Europe.

Officials say the corridor will significantly improve trade flows while strengthening Iraq’s role in global supply chains. Alongside the engineering work, the Ministry of Transport is preparing the project’s economic model to maximize investment returns and attract local and international partners.

The ministry said the framework will also align with the government’s broader reform agenda, including digital transformation and modern project management systems.

The government views the Development Road Project as one of Iraq’s most important strategic investments. Officials expect it to diversify the economy beyond oil, generate new non-oil revenues, attract foreign investment, and create thousands of jobs across multiple sectors.

By leveraging Iraq’s geographic position between East and West, the project is also expected to strengthen the country’s role as a regional center for transportation, logistics, and international trade.

World.title: Iraq’s non-oil revenues jump to 16%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Eco Iraq Observatory, which studies economic performance indicators, disclosed on Saturday that non-oil income now accounts for 16 percent of Iraq’s overall financial revenues, the highest percentage recorded so far.

According to a statement released by the observatory, this is the first time that the percentage of non-oil earnings has climbed to 16 percent during the months of May and June, having not exceeded five percent in years.

Eco Iraq noted that the proportion originally grew to roughly 10 percent between May 2020 and October 2022, then remained stable at that level during Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s leadership before recently hitting its peak.

The statement highlighted that non-oil revenues are divided into commodity taxes, production fees, general fees, income and wealth taxes, transfer revenues, and other sources.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s income, which it distributes to the federal government in Baghdad, accounts for around 5.5 percent of overall non-oil revenues.

As part of the government’s efforts to diversify the economy and achieve Iraq’s long-term development goals, Mazhar Saleh, the Prime Minister’s Advisor for Financial Affairs, stated in early June that an initiative would be launched. This initiative aims to create an integrated link between enhancing the structure of non-oil revenues within the framework of state finances and diversifying the non-oil GDP.

The Iraqi government established the ambitious goal, referred to as ‘Iraq 2035,’ in May. It includes both public finance reforms and social market economy policies, which aim to facilitate a gradual structural transformation of the national economy, as stated by Saleh.

The vision transforms fiscal policy to ensure that non-oil income accounts for at least 46 percent of total governmental revenues. This will improve budgetary sustainability and reduce the volatility caused by overreliance on oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq to launch ferry routes to Iran, Kuwait, UAE, and Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is preparing to launch a network of regular maritime passenger routes connecting the country with Iran, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia, as part of a broader effort to revive the country’s maritime transport sector and strengthen regional tourism.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the initiative will begin after technical and administrative requirements are completed in coordination with relevant authorities inside Iraq and neighboring countries.

A source at the ministry’s media office told Iraq’s official newspaper that the government has developed a comprehensive plan to operate regional maritime transport services using an expanded fleet of boats and ferries.

The ministry currently operates 40 boats and ferries under its river transport program and has recently added 15 new boats and three ferries to the fleet. The upgraded vessels are expected to provide modern, safe transportation for passengers while supporting Iraq’s growing tourism sector.

According to the ministry, most of the new vessels will be deployed on passenger and tourism routes linking Iraq with Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Iran. Officials said services will begin once all operational approvals, safety procedures, and cross-border coordination have been finalized to ensure the routes meet international maritime safety standards.

The planned connections are expected to facilitate both tourism and commercial travel between Iraq and neighboring countries. The Ministry of Transport believes the new maritime routes will provide an affordable and practical alternative for regional travel, particularly for leisure tourism.

The project is also expected to improve mobility for official delegations and religious visitors while strengthening economic ties with Gulf states and Iran through enhanced passenger connectivity.

Officials described the initiative as a significant step toward revitalizing Iraq’s maritime transport sector after years of limited regional ferry services. The ferry project forms part of a wider government strategy to modernize Iraq’s river and maritime transport infrastructure.

Alongside expanding its fleet, the ministry is investing in the development of ports, docks, and river terminals to improve passenger services and operational efficiency.

The broader vision aims to restore river and maritime transport as an important component of Iraq’s transportation network while supporting economic development, tourism, and greater regional integration.

World.title: Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate accuses BP of sidelining local talent and demands an 85% local hiring quota
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Kirkuk Engineers Syndicate has voiced strong concerns over hiring practices and subcontract awards linked to BP’s operations in the province’s oil fields, alleging that local engineers and businesses are being overlooked in favor of workers and companies from outside Kirkuk.

While welcoming international investment in Iraq’s energy sector, the syndicate warned it would pursue legal action and peaceful protests if local employment requirements are not enforced.

In a statement, the syndicate said it is closely monitoring recruitment procedures and the awarding of secondary contracts related to BP’s projects in Kirkuk.

It argued that the current approach has resulted in several violations, including the exclusion of qualified local engineers despite the availability of experienced graduates and professionals from the province.

The syndicate also claimed that engineering and technical staff are being recruited from outside Kirkuk, while numerous subcontracting and logistics contracts have been awarded to companies based elsewhere.

According to the statement, these practices undermine the local economy and deprive Kirkuk residents of employment opportunities linked to projects operating within their province.

The syndicate stressed that Kirkuk residents bear the environmental and health impacts associated with oil production and should therefore receive priority in employment opportunities.

It called on the Ministry of Oil and the Kirkuk provincial administration to require that at least 85% of jobs across all project stages be reserved exclusively for residents of Kirkuk.

In addition, the syndicate demanded formal representation on the joint recruitment committee to ensure transparency and fairness in hiring decisions. It also urged authorities to use the syndicate’s database of registered engineering graduates when filling vacancies.

Among its proposals, the syndicate called for all job applications to be processed exclusively through the employment office of the Kirkuk Governorate, arguing that a centralized system would improve transparency and ensure equal access to opportunities.

The organization also backed government efforts to distribute employment opportunities fairly among all communities in Kirkuk without discrimination.

The statement concluded with a warning that the syndicate would not remain silent if local engineers continue to be excluded from employment opportunities.

It said it is prepared to coordinate with legislative and executive authorities and pursue all available legal avenues, alongside peaceful protests, to protect the rights of Kirkuk’s engineering community. The statement did not include a response from BP regarding the allegations.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank improves non-bank financial oversight
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – As part of a major institutional reform, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) upgraded its Directorate of Non-Bank Financial Institutions Supervision to a complete General Directorate.

This change intends to increase regulatory control, develop digital solutions, and improve institutional performance in Iraq’s expanding financial industry.

The reform entails significant changes to departments, name practices, and reporting structures.

The newly established general directorate will include all important departments in charge of policy, regulatory structures, digital technologies, and financial service operations.

The Information Technology and Payments Directorate is now known simply as the Information Technology Directorate. Its old financial inclusion and information security sections have been removed and merged with risk management and other operational directorates.

The CBI closed its office for coordinating branch activities. The major branches in Basra, Mosul, and Erbil will report directly to the bank’s deputy governor.

The Human Resources Directorate has directed that all personnel transfers and systemic transitions will be effective by July 30, 2026.

This change corresponds with CBI Governor Nizar Hussein’s increasing regulatory push on financial technology businesses to decrease cash dependency and adhere to international compliance requirements.

World.title: Iran destroys nearly all US military facilities in Iraq’s Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said that the IRGC destroyed nearly all US military installations during recent operations in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Akraminia stated Tehran was now using newer attack drones that were more accurate and sophisticated than the Arash-2, according to Anadolu Agency (AA).

The Iranian official claimed that Iran has severely damaged US military outposts around the region, with many losing most of their operational capabilities.

Akraminia also indicated that Iran is prepared to persist with military operations until the United States acknowledges its inability to impose its will on the nation through violent means.

Akraminia claimed that anti-Iranian Kurdish resistance groups based in Erbil are also no longer able to carry out missions because of the destroyed infrastructure.

Reports mentioned that, while the bases have suffered damage, allegations of complete destruction are greatly overstated.

World.title: Iraq deploys 14 trains to expand passenger rail services
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq will increase rail services and operate 14 trains to transport travelers during the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, expanding capacity on key routes to the holy city of Karbala, according to the Ministry of Transport.

The Ministry said that the increased services would begin on July 26 as part of preparations for one of the world’s greatest annual religious gatherings, when millions of Shia Muslims go to Karbala to mark the 40th day following Imam Hussein’s death.

The concept calls for a double-track railway between Baghdad and Karbala to be operational during the pilgrimage season, enabling trains to travel in both directions without stopping for opposing traffic, boosting punctuality and increasing the number of daily passengers.

Rail services would link Karbala to Baghdad, Basra, Nasiriyah, Diwaniyah, and Souq Al-Shuyoukh, with extra trains deployed under the ministry’s operating plan to meet increased passenger demand.

According to the stated schedule, Iraq Railways will run seven daily services in each direction between Baghdad and Karbala, as well as three daily services between Basra and Karbala.

During the pilgrimage period, regular passenger services between Baghdad and Basra will run as usual.

The Ministry stated that the expanded schedule is intended to improve operational efficiency, reduce traffic congestion, and provide safer and more reliable transportation for pilgrims traveling to and from the holy city.

The Arbaeen pilgrimage is one of Iraq’s greatest annual transportation operations, requiring substantial coordination across rail, road, and aviation networks as officials oversee the flow of millions of local and foreign tourists.

World.title: Can the government take control of foreign-funded assets? FCRA Bill explained
World.content:
In India, the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) is one of those laws that returns to the spotlight every few years â often amid much clamour. But why? The law has repeatedly generated debate over how India should balance scrutiny of overseas funding with the autonomy of NGOs and other civil society organisations.

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha in March, proposes a new framework for managing foreign contributions and assets when an organisationâs registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases. The government says the changes are intended to address administrative and legal gaps, while critics question the breadth of the proposed powers.

The opposition, however, has argued that the proposed changes hand sweeping powers to the government and could allow it to take control of assets built over decades by charitable organisations.

The FCRA Bill treats minorities as enemies and is keen on snatching their properties. DMK MP P Wilson

Several church groups, particularly in the Northeast, have argued that the changes could disproportionately affect Christian institutions that use foreign donations for welfare work.

So, what exactly is changing, why has the Bill become controversial and what does it mean for thousands of organisations that receive money from abroad?

What is FCRA

The Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, popularly known as FCRA, governs how individuals, trusts, NGOs, associations and companies in India can receive and use money, securities or other contributions from foreign sources.





Administered by the Amit Shah-led home ministry, the law does not prohibit foreign donations. Instead, it lays down who can receive them, how they must be accounted for and where they can be spent.

The government has maintained that the purpose behind the tweaking of the legislation is to ensure foreign money enters India through a more transparent and accountable system so that it cannot be diverted towards activities considered âharmfulâ to national interest, democratic institutions or public order.

FCRA... ensures that foreign money enters India through a registered, accountable and disclosed channel... while enabling thousands of organisations to carry out legitimate, impactful work Centre

Under the law, any organisation that wants to receive regular foreign funding must obtain an FCRA registration from the home ministry. For those receiving a one-time grant for a specific purpose can seek prior permission instead.

Therefore, every rupee received has to pass through a designated bank account, be audited and be reported annually to the government.

The law also bars election candidates, legislators, judges, government servants, newspaper editors involved in news reporting and political parties from receiving foreign contributions altogether.

FCRA restricts foreign funding that may threaten India's sovereignty.

The government argues that this is not unique to India. The home ministry has cited foreign-influence registration systems in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia and Canada to argue that such oversight is not unique to India. However, these systems differ in scope and are not direct equivalents of the FCRAâs broader regulation of foreign contributions.

A law that has steadily become stricter

India first enacted the FCRA in 1976 during the Emergency era.

Even then, the central concern was âforeign influenceâ over domestic politics and institutions.

The framework was significantly overhauled in 2010, when Parliament replaced the old law with the present FCRA. One of the biggest changes was introducing a registration system valid for five years, after which organisations had to renew their licences.

In 2020, the law underwent one of its most significant revisions, mandating the organisations receiving foreign funds to route all contributions through a single State Bank of India branch in New Delhi.

How FCRA steadily become stricter

The ceiling on administrative expenses was reduced from 50 per cent to 20 per cent. Organisations were also barred from transferring foreign funds to other NGOs, while office-bearers had to provide Aadhaar or passport details.

Successive amendments have tightened both reporting requirements and operational restrictions. The 2026 Bill extends the framework beyond routine compliance to the management and disposal of assets when an organisationâs registration ends.

What the 2026 Bill proposes

The headline provision in the Bill concerns organisations whose FCRA registration comes to an end.

At present, an organisation may lose its FCRA registration if the government cancels it for violating the law, if the organisation voluntarily surrenders it or if the registration is not renewed.

The 2026 Bill formally introduces the concept of a certificate "ceasing" to exist. This would happen if an organisation fails to apply for renewal, misses the renewal deadline or if its renewal application is rejected.

That change is significant because the Bill links the end of an FCRA certificate with what happens to foreign-funded assets.

The proposed law creates a designated authority to take charge of foreign contributions and assets created using those contributions whenever an organisation's registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases.

Initially, the transfer of assets will be provisional. If the organisation later succeeds in restoring or renewing its registration, the unutilised foreign contributions and assets will be returned.

However, if the organisation fails to regain its registration within the prescribed period, the transfer becomes permanent.

The designated authority will then have the power to manage those assets, transfer them to central or state government departments or dispose of them through sale. The proceeds from such disposal, along with any remaining foreign contribution, will be credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

FCRA regulates foreign funding that may threaten national interest.

The Bill also formally defines "key functionaries" who can be held responsible for violations committed by an organisation. These include directors, trustees, partners, office-bearers and others responsible for managing the institution.

It requires organisations receiving foreign funds through prior permission to receive and utilise those funds within a prescribed period.

Interestingly, the Bill reduces the maximum punishment for violating the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year, a move the government describes as a more proportionate approach to enforcement.

Another provision says no investigation into an offence under the Act may be initiated without the prior approval of the central government. The ministry says this would prevent multiple investigations under a central law; the Bill does not specify the criteria or timeframe for granting such approval.

As of July 15, 2026, the FCRA portal listed 22,498 cancelled registrations, 15,212 expired registrations and 14,449 active certificates, according to PRS Legislative Research.

The government says the lack of a detailed mechanism for handling assets after registration ends has created administrative uncertainty.

Why the controversy?



The government says the designated authority would fill this procedural gap and ensure that permanently vested assets are used for public purposes. Yet it is precisely this argument that has become the biggest point of disagreement.

Critics contest that the Bill goes beyond administrative housekeeping and fundamentally changes the relationship between the government and organisations that receive foreign donations.

They argue that the proposed provisions could permanently deprive charities of assets they created over decades, even in situations where they no longer depend on foreign funding. That disagreement lies at the heart of the political and religious controversy surrounding the Bill.

The central dispute is whether assets created in the past with foreign contributions should vest in the âdesignated authorityâ when an organisation no longer has an active FCRA certificate.

FCRA can be used in 9 different sectors

That is where the government's reasoning and the opposition's objections diverge. Under the proposed law, assets created using foreign contributions will vest in the âdesignated authorityâ not only when an organisation's registration is cancelled or surrendered but also when it simply ceases because the registration was not renewed or the renewal application was rejected.

The government argues this merely formalises an existing principle.

It points out that the 2010 Act already provided for vesting of foreign-funded assets when an FCRA registration was cancelled or surrendered.

According to the ministry of home affairs, the amendment only creates a detailed statutory framework explaining how those assets should be supervised, managed and disposed of, something that the earlier law did not spell out. It also says the initial vesting will be provisional and assets will be returned if the organisation later restores its registration.

Critics, however, believe the practical consequences are far more significant. They argue that an organisation may have built a hospital, school or library years ago with foreign donations but may now be running it entirely through domestic funding. If such an organisation decides not to renew its FCRA registration because it no longer needs foreign contributions, the Bill could still result in those earlier assets vesting with the designated authority.

PRS Legislative Research illustrates this concern through a hypothetical example of a healthcare organisation that built a hospital using foreign donations but later operated it entirely with domestic funds. Under the proposed framework, the hospital could still vest in the âdesignated authorityâ if the organisation's registration ceased and was not restored. The authority would then have the power to transfer it to a government department or dispose of it.

Government sees law as consistent with global trends.

Critics therefore argue that the amendment effectively creates no practical exit route from the FCRA system. An organisation wishing to retain assets originally built with foreign contributions may feel compelled to continue renewing its registration indefinitely, even if it no longer receives foreign funding. Another concern relates to mixed funding.

The Bill says assets created wholly or partly through foreign contributions can vest in the designated authority.

In cases where domestic and foreign funds have both been used to build an asset, organisations may apply to recover the identifiable domestic portion. Critics say that, in practice, separating domestic and foreign contributions within a single building or facility may not always be possible.

While the existing law provides a mechanism to appeal against cancellation of an FCRA certificate, critics note that neither the Act nor the proposed amendment specifically provides an appeal against refusal to renew a certificate before the assets vest.

They also point out that organisations are not guaranteed an opportunity to be heard before renewal is denied.

Why Christian organisations are worried

Although the Bill applies uniformly to all organisations, much of the opposition has come from church groups, especially in the Northeast.The Bill is not religion-specific, but church groups, particularly in Mizoram, have been among its most vocal opponents because many affiliated institutions receive foreign donations for welfare projects.

Many churches and Christian charitable institutions receive foreign donations to run schools, hospitals, orphanages, homes for persons with disabilities and other welfare projects. Leaders fear that if their FCRA registrations lapse or renewal is denied, properties developed over decades using foreign contributions could eventually pass into government control. These concerns have been particularly strong in Mizoram.

FRCRA like rules in different countries.

Chief minister Lalduhoma held consultations with leaders of the Council of Churches Mizoram and the Mizoram Kohhran Hruaitute Committee, after which it was decided that the provisions of the Bill "cannot be accepted in toto". The state government resolved to prepare a memorandum suggesting changes and seek a meeting with Union home minister Amit Shah.

Lalduhoma also said that if the Centre did not accept Mizoram's suggestions, the state's lone Lok Sabha MP from the ruling Zoram People's Movement would oppose the Bill in Parliament.

Congress echos similar concerns



Congressâs Mizoram unit organised protests against the proposed amendment, alleging that Christian institutions would be adversely affected because many charitable organisations in the state depend on overseas donations. Former MP Chella Kumar alleged that the BJP was targeting religious and other minorities while exempting the RSS from the law's purview. Church organisations elsewhere have also stepped up their campaign.

Special prayer services were held across several churches following a call by the Joint Action Forum on Minorities to observe a National Day of Fasting and Prayer against the Bill.

During one such gathering, DMK MP P Wilson compared the asset provisions with the Enemy Property Act and accused the government of targeting minority institutions. "The Enemy Property Act was enacted to snatch the properties of people who left the country after independence.

Similarly, the FCRA Bill treats minorities as enemies and is keen on snatching their properties," he said. A nationwide signature campaign and protests were also announced.

FCRA myths

The government's response

The Centre has strongly rejected allegations that the amendment targets any particular religion or seeks to curb legitimate charitable work.

According to the home ministry, around 16,200 associations received nearly Rs 22,963 crore in foreign contributions during 2024-25.

The ministry cites these figures to argue that the FCRA regulates, rather than prohibits, foreign donations. It says organisations engaged in faith-based welfare activities remain eligible to receive foreign funding and that the law applies equally irrespective of religion, community or ideology.

The government has also tried to address concerns over places of worship.

The Bill requires the designated authority to preserve the religious character of any permanently vested asset, or part of an asset, that is a place of worship.

Govt's clarification on FCRA

The government says the framework concerns foreign contributions and assets created from them after an organisationâs registration lawfully ends. The Bill, however, provides that an asset created partly with foreign contributions would initially vest wholly in the Authority, although the organisation may apply for the return of any distinct or ascertainable portion funded from domestic sources.

The Centre has further defended restrictions on foreign nationals holding key positions in FCRA-registered organisations, arguing that organisations receiving overseas funding should be managed by individuals with a verified connection to India.

Likewise, it said requiring central approval before state-level investigations is appropriate because the FCRA is a central law dealing with foreign funding and national security.

World.title: 'Beginning of accountability': Prashant Kishor on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder and Bankipur assembly by-election candidate

on Sunday described Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as the "beginning of accountability", asserting that sustained public pressure had compelled the government to act.

Addressing reporters, Kishor said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations and demonstrated that public mobilisation could force those in power to respond.

"This is the beginning of accountability. Accountability is being enforced under public pressure. I always say that in this country, the opposition party can be weak. The opposition cannot be weak," he said.

Expressing support for those opposing what he termed the government's "undemocratic behaviour", Kishor said the issue was larger than any single political party.

"We stand with anyone who wants to challenge this government's undemocratic behaviour and their work.

is my friend. He's a prominent academic, environmentalist, and friend of ours. This isn't about a party; people have seen that if people stand up, if the public rises, even those in power will have to bow down," he said.

Referring to the ongoing protests in Delhi, Kishor said they reflected widespread public anger rather than the agenda of any one organisation.





"What you and I are seeing in Delhi wasn't a protest by one Sonam Wangchuk. The thousands of people who came to protest didn't carry CJP flags. They were ordinary young people, frustrated by the daily paper leaks, unemployment, and the crumbling education system," he said.

Commenting on the arrest of Janshakti Janata Dal national president Tej Pratap Yadav, Kishor alleged that the action reflected the government's nervousness.

"Tej Pratap announced his support yesterday, and at 1.30 am last night, Tej Pratap was arrested and sent to Beur Jail. This shows how scared these people are. Under what section was he arrested? Why was he arrested? The police administration should explain this," he was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.

Kishor claimed Pradhan's resignation was only the beginning and suggested that the agitation would continue.

"Dharmendra Pradhan had to leave, and that's not all, this is just the beginning.

This isn't going to stop," he added.

Kishor also raised objections to an order issued by the district magistrate regarding election awareness activities involving Jeevika Didis. He urged the election commission and its observers to take note of the matter and initiate action.

"The District Magistrate issued order. In which he stated that Jeevika Didi, would work for election awareness. We hope that the Election Commission, their observers, will take cognizance of this matter, and take action," he said.

He warned that if no action was taken by Monday, he and his supporters would stage a protest outside the Election Commission's office.

"If action isn't taken by tomorrow, we will go to the Election Commission and sit on a protest at their gate, along with my colleagues," Kishor said.

World.title: 'Don't cry later': Owaisi makes alliance offer to Akhilesh to oust BJP in UP polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

, the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief, expressed apparent willingness to tie up with the INDIA bloc, particularly with

's

, to take on the ruling

BJP

in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh.

During a rally in Moradabad, the Hyderabad Lok Sabha MP said he was ready to "join hands" or "form an alliance" with the Samajwadi Party, which would be cautious about the offer as both parties reach out to the same voter base in the 403-seat Assembly.

Brushing off the BJP's "B-team" tag, Owaisi said he does not want the BJP to continue in power for a third straight term in the state, provided the Samajwadi Party ties up with the AIMIM to avoid a split in votes.

However, an alliance with the AIMIM would be a critical call for the Samajwadi Party as it could further consolidate Owaisi's party in the electorally crucial state.

"I have said this before, and I am saying it again: the Majlis does not want the BJP to form the government again in Uttar Pradesh. I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again.





You say that Owaisi contesting would harm us. I'm ready to fight alongside you," Owaisi said at a rally in Moradabad.

Owaisi said the AIMIM's fight was "never against any religion, nor will it ever be. Our fight is for our honour. Our fight is a fight for justice. Now we don't want to sit on a mat. Now we want equality."

"If Akhilesh sits in front of that chair, then Owaisi will sit cross-legged in front of that chair and talk about rights and justice," he further said.

World.title: 'Jamaati fundamentalists': Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari alleges 'foreign hand' in Kolkata rally violence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday alleged that the violence during a protest rally in Kolkata over the NEET question paper leak was orchestrated by "Islamic fundamentalists," claiming they may have been supported by "foreign forces.

"

Adhikari made the remarks while speaking to reporters in Nandigram after attending a programme to commemorate Kargil Vijay Diwas, marking the 27th anniversary of India's victory over Pakistan in the 1999 Kargil War.

Claiming that those involved in the violence had no connection to the student-led agitation, he said, "There is no connection between these people and the movement. They are not students. They are Jamaati (Islamic) fundamentalists.

Probe agencies will determine whether foreign forces backed them."

"The violence may have been fuelled by resentment over several decisions of the BJP government in the state, including action against unregistered madrassas, implementation of court directions relating to OBC certificates, enforcement of cattle slaughter laws and measures to curb noise pollution," he added.

Referring to the assault on a journalist during the protest, Adhikari alleged that media personnel were "deliberately targeted" and that there were "attempts on their lives."





Clashes erupted between Left-backed protesters and police during the demonstration, prompting security forces to resort to baton charges and fire tear gas shells to disperse the crowd.

The West Bengal government invoked its newly enacted anti-goonda law against those accused of orchestrating the violence during the protest, with the chief minister warning that they would face punishment "their next three generations will remember."

Adhikari had earlier told the assembly that around 70 people identified from the rally were "not students" and had no connection with the agitation over the alleged NEET question paper leak.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann inaugurates 120-bed multi-speciality hospital in Moga
World.content:
Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Saturday inaugurated the 120-bed Capital Hospital in Moga, saying the facility would improve access to advanced healthcare services in the Malwa region.

The hospital, described by the state government as the first National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers (NABH)-accredited multi-speciality hospital in Moga district, will offer specialised treatment for critical illnesses.

The Chief Minister said eligible patients would be able to avail cashless treatment under the Punjab Government's Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna and the Centre's Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY).

He added that the state government continues to expand healthcare services through its network of 1,090 Aam Aadmi Clinics.

In a post on X, Mann said the hospital was equipped with advanced medical facilities and would provide free treatment under the Mukh Mantri Sehat Bima Yojana. He said the facility would reduce the need for people in the Malwa region to travel to other cities for treatment.

Addressing the gathering, Mann said the event was focused on development rather than politics, adding that education and healthcare remained the government's two main priorities.





He said doctors were held in high regard and described healthcare and education as professions dedicated to public service. He added that the government was working to restore public confidence in both sectors.

Referring to the newly inaugurated hospital, Mann said it would provide access to advanced medical equipment and specialist doctors. He also highlighted the state's education reforms, stating that Punjab had moved from 27th place in school education in 2022 to the top position following reforms introduced by the government.

Mann said the government had established Schools of Eminence to strengthen public education. He added that the number of students from government schools qualifying the NEET examination had increased from 82 in 2022 to 881 this year.

The Chief Minister said both the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna and central government health insurance schemes would be available at the hospital. He also highlighted the state's Sadak Surakhya Force, stating that it comprises 1,597 trained personnel supported by 144 vehicles to improve road safety on state and national highways.

According to Mann, road accident fatalities have declined by nearly 50 per cent since the force was launched in February last year.

He also said Punjab had introduced a universal healthcare scheme offering cashless treatment of up to â¹10 lakh annually to every resident family in the state. Mann said beneficiaries had availed treatment worth more than â¹650 crore under the scheme.

The chief minister further said Punjab had established a liver transplant centre in Mohali, describing it as the second such facility in the country after Delhi.

World.title: India issues Black Sea advisory after strike in Ukraine's Odesa, calls maritime corridor 'highly volatile'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs has issued a fresh advisory urging Indian nationals to exercise extreme caution before accepting employment on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the Black Sea region.

The ministry warned that the security situation in the conflict-hit maritime corridor remains "highly volatile", with commercial vessels facing persistent risks from missile and drone attacks.

This comes after a merchant vessel carrying four Indian nationals was struck at Ukraine's Port of Odesa, with two crew members confirmed safe while the status of the other two is still being ascertained, according to the Indian Embassy in Kyiv.

In an advisory issued on Sunday, New Delhi said that the deteriorating security environment has already claimed the lives of five Indian nationals since April 2026.

"The security situation in and around the Black Sea and adjoining maritime areas remains highly volatile due to the ongoing conflict. Commercial vessels operating in or transiting these waters are facing significant security risks, including missile and drone attacks," the Ministry of External Affairs said.





The advisory follows a string of attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea amid the Russia-Ukraine war. On July 18, an Indian seafarer was killed after the merchant vessel MV Omorfi was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, marking the second attack on a ship carrying Indian crew within a week and taking the total number of Indian seafarers killed in the conflict to five. New Delhi had earlier condemned attacks on merchant shipping and called for safe maritime navigation.

Advising seafarers to carefully assess the risks before accepting assignments in the region, the ministry urged them to verify vessel routes, security arrangements, insurance cover, emergency procedures and employment terms.

It also said Indian nationals should "ensure that the terms of employment comply with applicable international maritime standards and provide adequate provisions for medical care, evacuation, repatriation, and compensation in the event of an emergency."

The ministry also stressed the importance of maintaining communication with family members during voyages. "Keep family members informed of your itinerary and maintain regular contact," it said.

It also directed Indian nationals to closely follow safety guidance issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, other Government of India authorities, vessel operators and competent maritime authorities.

"Regularly monitor and comply with advisories issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, and other relevant Government of India authorities, as well as safety instructions issued by vessel operators and the competent maritime authorities," the ministry said.

The advisory added that Indian nationals requiring assistance should remain in touch with India's Embassy and Consulates in the region through the emergency contact numbers provided in the advisory.

World.title: Indian embassy monitors Ukraine's Odesa strike; two Indians safe, search on for two others
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Embassy of India in Ukraine on Sunday said it is closely monitoring the situation after the merchant vessel MV AGN Ragnar was struck at the Port of Odesa on July 25, with four Indian nationals onboard.

In a statement posted on X, the embassy said two of the four Indian crew members have been confirmed safe, while information regarding the remaining two is awaited.

"Embassy of India in Ukraine is monitoring the situation after the vessel MV AGN Ragnar was struck at the Port of Odesa on July 25. Four Indian nationals were on board the vessel. As per the latest information, two have been confirmed safe, and information is awaited regarding the other two nationals.

Search and rescue operations are underway. The Embassy is in constant touch with the concerned authorities," the embassy said.

The mission said it is maintaining close coordination with Ukrainian authorities as search and rescue operations continue. The embassy also shared its Point of Contact for Indian nationals requiring assistance:

Email: cons.kyiv@mea.gov.in

Alternate Email: cons1.kyiv@mea.gov.in

Emergency Contact: +380933559958 (Mr. Aji Kumar, Second Secretary â Consular)

Odesa, Ukraine's largest port on the Black Sea, has been a frequent target of Russian missile and drone attacks since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Commercial shipping in the Black Sea has also faced periodic disruptions despite international efforts to keep maritime trade routes operational.

India has consistently advised its citizens against travelling to Ukraine due to the ongoing conflict and has continued to provide consular assistance to Indian nationals residing in the country.

World.title: 'Who approved pellet guns?' Rahul Gandhi writes Amit Shah over 'barbaric assault' on students
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition

wrote to Union home minister

, demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students protesting "peacefully" at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20.

Calling out the "most shocking" use of "lethal pellet guns," the Congress leader claimed that a 19-year-old student has been undergoing a severe pain and is "likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet guns".

"Security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to you, so I ask:1. As Home Minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? 2. Are the people in plain clothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Who authorized their deployment?" Rahul Gandhi wrote in a letter addressed to Amit Shah.

The Congress leader futher said that it's "government's responsibility to protect protestors and resolve their grievances through dialogue".

"Peaceful protest is crucial to any democracy. It is the government's responsibility to protect protestors and resolve their grievances through dialogue. Such brutal violence destroys every norm, and has outraged the country. Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability.





Their voice will be heard," he further wrote.

Rahul Gandhi on Saturday slammed the government, saying children protesting for their rights receive "pellets" instead of "justice."

In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared a video featuring a youth who was reportedly beaten by the

during Monday's protests against paper leaks.

"Sahil was standing with the Tricolour in his hand, merely asking for a clean, fair exam and the fruit of his hard work--the police raised a gun and badly injured him by firing pellets.

This is not British tyranny; it is the brutality of the Modi government in independent India--where innocent students demanding their rights receive pellets instead of justice," the post read.

More than 118 police personnel sustained injuries, including senior officers holding the ranks of Special Commissioner of Police, Joint Commissioner of Police, Additional Commissioner of Police, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police, and Assistant Commissioner of Police, along with several female police personnel.

During the scuffle, around 60 protesters were also reported to have been injured.

On Friday, the Union Cabinet approved amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to strengthen the anti-paper leak law amid continuing nationwide protests over the NEET-UG row, while the deadlock in Parliament continued for the fifth day.

According to sources, the proposed amendment Bill is likely to be tabled in Parliament on Monday, July 27.

World.title: Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Education Minister
World.content:
Union Minister for Education Pralhad Joshi officially took charge of the Ministry of Education at Kartavya Bhavan on Sunday (July 26, 2026). The Minister also holds charge of the Union Ministries of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy.

Mr. Joshi was appointed as Education Minister after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the post on Saturday (July 25, 2026).

Mr. Pradhan resigned from his post on Saturday (July 25, 2026), following the Cockroach Janta Party-led student protests across the country, demanding his ouster over the NEET paper leak cases.

Union Minister for Education #PralhadJoshi officially took charge of the Ministry of Education at Kartavya Bhavan on Sunday. The Minister also holds charges of the Union Ministries of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy.



✍️@dawalelo… pic.twitter.com/uD5goWsERm — The Hindu (@the_hindu) July 26, 2026

Mr. Joshi chaired a review meeting of the Ministry, in which he assessed the implementation of various schemes and other initiatives. The Union Minister of State for Education, Jayant Chaudhary, also attended the review meeting.

The President directed on Saturday (July 25, 2026) that Mr. Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio, as advised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, an official statement said.

Mr. Joshi currently holds the portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy.

The President, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India, the statement added.

Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Dr. Vineet Joshi, and Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, T. K. Anil Kumar, along with senior officers of the Ministry were present.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Andhra Pradesh launches AI platform to forecast urban floods; Vijayawada first
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has launched City Flood Alert, an AI-powered technology platform developed by the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) with the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) and IIT Gandhinagar. The platform is designed to predict urban flooding before it occurs, enabling authorities to take preventive measures well in advance.

According to a press release by RTGS on Sunday (July 26, 2026), the system combines artificial intelligence, satellite-based terrain mapping, predictive analytics and hydrological modelling to provide rainfall forecasts up to 48 hours in advance and flash flood warnings up to six hours in advance.

The platform will initially be deployed in Vijayawada, where recurring floods, particularly from the Budameru rivulet, have frequently affected low-lying areas.

Using a high-resolution Digital Elevation Model created from satellite imagery and nearly three decades of historical Budameru flood data, the system can identify flood-prone locations, simulate inundation under different rainfall scenarios and detect drainage channels vulnerable to silt accumulation. Once a flood threat is identified, the platform automatically alerts the APSDMA, enabling timely advisories to District Collectors, Municipal Commissioners and field officials for preventive measures, including drain clearance, emergency team deployment and evacuation of vulnerable residents.

Following its rollout in Vijayawada, City Flood Alert will be expanded to all urban local bodies across Andhra Pradesh. By integrating advanced technology with disaster management expertise, the platform marks a shift from reactive flood response to predictive governance, setting a new benchmark for climate-resilient urban management in the State, the release said.

World.title: Cockroach Janta Party protests | Collection of The Hindu’s ground reports
World.content:
The Cockroach Janta Party, a youth movement, organised ‘Chalo Sansad’ (march to Parliament) on July 20, 2026. Thousands of people, led by the CJP, gathered on the opening day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following repeated examination paper leaks in connection with the administration of the National Eligibility and Entrance Test (NEET), among other demands.

In Pictures | CJP protest march to Parliament 1 / 3

Protesters took to the streets of New Delhi, clashing with police who used tear gas and batons to push them back. The protests, which started last month over the leak of medical school entrance exam papers, intensified after activist Sonam Wangchuk, who started a hunger strike on June 28, was forcibly moved to a hospital by police on July 18. Moreover, in the first widespread communications blackout in Delhi since the farmers’ agitation in 2021, mobile internet was switched off throughout Central Delhi, even as demonstrators poured into Jantar Mantar.

The protests have also spread outside the capital, with demonstrations by youth and opposition groups ⁠being held in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Goa, Guwahati, Thiruvananthapuram, Jammu and Ahmedabad.

Read The Hindu’s ground reports from the protest sites.

World.title: Two teenagers killed as lorry hits scooter in Hyderabad, friend survives
World.content:
Two 17-year-old intermediate students were killed after a lorry rammed into the scooter they were riding on while they were on their way to play cricket in Hyderabad on Sunday (July 26, 2026) morning. A third teenager, who was travelling with them, escaped with minor injuries.

The deceased were identified as B. Mahesh and Laxmi Teja, both aged 17. Their friend, B. Kiran, also 17, sustained minor injuries in the accident.

At around 5 a.m. on Sunday (July 26, 2026), they were travelling from Moosapet towards KPHB and had planned to stop for tea before heading to the cricket ground.

Police said the accident was reported at a U-turn when a lorry travelling in the same direction struck the scooter from the side. The impact caused Mahesh and Teja to fall to the left side of the road, where they were run over by the lorry. Kiran fell to the right and escaped with minor injuries.

The lorry driver fled the scene immediately after the accident.

On receiving information, police rushed to the spot, shifted the bodies for postmortem examination and launched an investigation.

A case has been registered, and the lorry has been detained. Efforts are under way to trace the absconding driver.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran army says war to ‘expand further’ if U.S. attacks restart
World.content:
Iran’s army warned on Sunday (July 26, 2026) that the war in West Asia would widen if the United States chose to press ahead with attacks on the Islamic republic, ahead of the visit of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Washington.

The U.S. military has paused its airstrikes on Iran after nearly two weeks of intensifying bombing, while diplomatic efforts have pushed forward to try to avert a return to all-out war. Regional officials involved in the mediation efforts said that concerted diplomacy was under way and that a pause in U.S. strikes and Iranian counterstrikes on neighbouring countries hosting American forces was a “positive signal that helps their efforts to de-escalate.”

The U.S. naval blockade against Iran remains in full effect, the U.S. Central Command said early Sunday (July 26, 2026).

Despite the lull in fighting, tensions are high in the region. Yemen’s Houthi rebels said on Saturday (July 25, 2026) that they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi airstrikes on the strategic Red Sea city of Hodeida. The Iran-backed rebels say they have closed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which has become even more vital for Saudi oil exports since the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: More brick structures, important features unearthed at Keeladi archaeological site in Tamil Nadu
World.content:
In the 11th phase of excavations currently underway in Keeladi, continuous brick structures and over 1,300 artefacts have been discovered.

The Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology (TNSDA) is conducting the 11th phase of excavation at the Keeladi archaeological site, located near Madurai in Sivagangai district. While the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) conducted the first three phases, subsequent phases have been carried out by the TNSDA.

This 11th phase of excavation began on March 18 of this year, south of the area where the on-site museum is located. A total of nine quadrants were dug in this area. Ramesh Masethung, Director of Keeladi Excavations, told The Hindu that continuous brick structures were found across all nine quadrants. He mentioned that these structures, extending towards the west and north, stretch beyond these nine quadrants.

“Brick structures were previously found in the area where the on-site museum is located. In the adjacent area excavated later, no structural remains were found. However, structural remains have been uncovered once again now,” says Mr. Masethung.

Apart from these brick structures, several other important features have come to light during the current excavation. In one quadrant, a terracotta pipeline and a closed drainage system were discovered. In addition to the structural remains, more than 1,300 artefacts have been recovered. These include clay hopscotches, terracotta beads and spindles, iron knives, chisels, swords, and nails, as well as semi-precious stones such as amethyst, carnelian, agate, banded agate, and ivory dice.

Furthermore, tiny gold ornaments measuring less than a centimeter have been found. In addition, intact pots were discovered in four locations, one of which includes a handle. One of these pots features a fish symbol inscribed on its shoulder portion.

“Since an open drainage system was also found in one quadrant, this might have been an industrial area as well. However, this can only be confirmed after the studies are completed,” says Mr. Masethung. He also added that organic materials found here will be sent for carbon dating.

Depending on the rain, this 11th phase of excavation may continue until September.

World.title: PMK founder S. Ramadoss to retire from active politics
World.content:
PMK founder S. Ramadoss has reportedly expressed his willingness to step aside and retire from active politics and said his son and Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) president Anbumani Ramadoss would take care of party affairs here on.

Dr. Ramadoss reportedly made this announcement at a family gathering in Thailapuram on the eve of his 88th birthday on Saturday (July 25, 2026). The decision brings an end to a political career that has seen the highest of highs and lowest of lows and associations with some of the tallest leaders in both State and national parties.

Dr. Ramadoss, who had a falling out with Dr. Anbumani before the election, chose to bury the hatchet when he met the latter recently and embraced him, photos of which were made public. Dr. Ramadoss’s supporters — especially former PMK president G.K. Mani and former MLA R. Arul — who had backed him strongly and antagonised Dr. Anbumani, may find it difficult to reconcile to the new development.

Stalin’s greeting

Former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin wished Dr. Ramadoss on his birthday and said: “Having led numerous struggles for social justice and served as a powerful voice, I wish that your retirement is filled with contentment and joy.”

World.title: Tap ESCO model for improving energy efficiency, Kerala's Energy Management Centre tells institutions, industries
World.content:
Even as a monsoon-season power crisis in Kerala has restated the importance of efficient energy use, the State government agency Energy Management Centre - Kerala (EMC) has invited institutions and industrial and commercial establishments to make use of the Energy Service Company (ESCO) model for implementing energy efficiency projects.

What makes the ESCO model attractive is that entities can implement energy efficiency improvement projects without upfront capital investment. The ESCO undertakes the investment and implementation of the selected energy efficiency measures, and the project cost is recovered from the verified energy cost savings that are generated.

“This approach enables facilities to modernise energy systems, reduce operating costs and lower emissions while minimising the financial burden of initial investment,” according to the EMC, which is also the State Designated Agency (SDA) for Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) programmes in Kerala.

Project cost

The ESCO recovers the project cost through a percentage of the savings in energy cost made by the establishment by implementing such projects, R. Harikumar, Director, EMC - Kerala, said. The projects are cleared subject to their viability and the agreed contractual arrangement.

For the current programme, the EMC is giving priority to large commercial buildings, hotels, hospitals, and industries that focus on chemicals, pharmaceuticals, textiles, food and beverage processing, metals and engineering. Minimum indicative requirements include a monthly energy expenditure of ₹25 lakh or above; heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system capacity of 500 TR (Ton of Refrigeration) or above; and significant hot-water demand with potential for heat-pump applications.

Producing only 30% of its electricity requirement, Kerala is currently battling a peak demand shortage with power curbs on a limited scale. Increase in electricity demand, low water storage in the reservoirs for hydro generation on account of poor southwest monsoon rainfall and the rise in the nationwide demand for electricity due to El Nino-linked warm temperatures have been cited as reasons.

World.title: Malshej Ghat tragedy: 2 youngsters drown at Maharashtra tourist spot, bodies retrieved
World.content:
Malshej Ghat was closed to all vehicular traffic after a newly concretised stretch of National Highway-61 connecting Ahilyanagar and Kalyan developed severe subsidence. (File Photo)

Two youngsters drowned in two separate incidents in the Kalu River near the popular monsoon tourist attraction of Malshej Ghat on Saturday afternoon.

The police have identified the deceased persons as Pavan Sham Sathe, 18, and Raman Vijay Annapure, 20.

Assistant police inspector Sheetalkumar Naik of Tokawade police station in Thane Rural said, “Sathe is a native of Buldhana district, while Annapure hails from Nanded.”

“A prima facie probe revealed that Annapure is a student of engineering at a Pune college. Sathe had come to his brother’s place in Pune. Both of them do not know each other. They separately came from Pune to the Malshej Ghat area with their friends to see the Kalu waterfall,” said Naik.

World.title: Is creatine bad for kidneys? Experts bust 6 common sports nutrition myths
World.content:
Whether you’re trying to build muscle, lose weight or improve your athletic performance, you’ve probably heard plenty of advice about protein powders, creatine and pre-workout supplements. But how much of it is actually true?

Curious, we reached out to Vishnu Menon, founder of Iron Asylum, a prominent health and fitness marketer, looking for some of the most common sports nutrition myths and had medical experts weigh in on the science behind each one. Here’s everything you need to know.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

Myth 1: Supplements can replace a healthy diet

According to Menon, supplements are meant to do exactly what their name suggests—supplement a healthy diet, not replace it. Protein powders, pre-workouts and multivitamins cannot make up for poor nutrition, inadequate sleep or an inconsistent workout routine. Instead, they are designed to “help fill nutritional gaps and support specific fitness goals.”

Medical literature also supports that supplements work best alongside a balanced diet, regular exercise, adequate sleep and hydration. They should be viewed as supportive tools rather than substitutes for healthy lifestyle habits.

Protein powders cannot compensate for poor nutrition, lack of sleep and irregular workout routine (Image: Freepik) Protein powders cannot compensate for poor nutrition, lack of sleep and irregular workout routine (Image: Freepik)

Myth 2: The more protein you eat, the bigger your muscles

“One definitely requires protein so that muscles could recover and rebuild themselves after the workout session, but the intake of lots of it does not necessarily mean the massive gains,” Menon tells indianexpress.com.

He points out that our body has a limit to how much protein it can effectively use for muscle building, making it more important to meet your daily requirement than to consume as much protein as possible.



Vandana Rajput, Consultant, Dietetics, Kailash Hospital & Neuro Institute agrees. “Protein plays a vital role in muscle repair, recovery, and athletic performance, but more is not always better.”

She further explains that protein requirements vary depending on age, body weight, activity level and training goals. Meeting your daily protein requirement through balanced intake spread across the day is more beneficial than consuming excessive amounts.

Myth 3: Creatine is harmful to the kidneys

“This might have to be the oldest sports nutrition myth of al,” says Menon while stating that decades of scientific research have shown that creatine is “possibly the safest and most studied sports supplements” for healthy individuals. When taken in recommended amounts, he says it has not been shown to harm the kidneys and may also help improve strength, power and recovery.

We verified this with Dr Aseem Thamba, Consultant Nephrologist and Kidney Transplant Physician, Zen Multi-speciality Hospital, Chembur, who confirmed that this statement is accurate for healthy individuals. However, people with existing kidney disease or reduced kidney function should always consult their doctor before taking creatine or any other supplement.



Myth 4: All pre-workouts are just caffeine

Healthy non-caffeinated pre-workout meals: fruit-nuts, smoothies, Greek yogurt, oats, whole-grain toast-nut butter (Ai-generated) Healthy non-caffeinated pre-workout meals: fruit-nuts, smoothies, Greek yogurt, oats, whole-grain toast-nut butter (Ai-generated)

Many people assume pre-workout supplements are nothing more than caffeine, but Menon says a well-formulated pre-workout may also contain ingredients such as “citrulline, beta-alanine, electrolytes, tyrosine and taurine”, which are intended to support endurance, hydration, blood flow, focus and overall workout performance. He adds that a good pre-workout should help improve training quality without making users feel excessively jittery or causing a crash afterwards.

However, supplements aren’t the only option before a workout. Rajput says, “A pre-workout meal or snack should provide sustained energy without necessarily relying on caffeine.”

She recommends options such as a fruit with a handful of nuts, fruit smoothies with mixed seeds, a banana with peanut butter, Greek yogurt with fruit, oats with milk, whole-grain toast with nut butter or a yogurt-and-fruit smoothie.

“These foods provide a balanced combination of carbohydrates and protein to support energy levels, endurance, and post-workout recovery.”



Myth 5: Natural always means safer

The word “natural” often creates the impression that a product is automatically safe, but Menon says that isn’t always true. According to him, an ingredient’s safety depends on the ingredient itself, how much is consumed, how it is used and the scientific evidence supporting it—not simply whether it comes from nature or a laboratory.

He also advises consumers to choose brands that are transparent about their ingredients and testing rather than relying on marketing claims.

Rajput echoes this view. “The term ‘natural’ should not be considered a guarantee of safety or effectiveness.”

She explains that while many natural foods and ingredients can be beneficial, some natural supplements may not be suitable for everyone and their quality or composition can vary. It is important to choose products from trusted manufacturers and consult a qualified healthcare professional before adding any supplement to your routine, especially if you have an underlying medical condition or take regular medications.



Also Read | Why your veins look more visible after push-ups and strength training

Myth 6: All supplements are created equal

Don’t judge a supplement by its packaging—check the ingredients, transparency and quality testing (Image: Freepik) Don’t judge a supplement by its packaging—check the ingredients, transparency and quality testing (Image: Freepik)

Two supplement products may look almost identical on the shelf, but Menon says their quality can differ significantly. Factors such as ingredient quality, dosage, sourcing and product testing can vary widely, so consumers should look beyond attractive packaging and carefully read ingredient labels.

The nutritionists agree and stress that a better supplement contains evidence-based ingredients in appropriate amounts. Rather than being influenced by packaging or advertising claims, consumers should prioritise quality, scientific evidence and their own requirements.

As Menon points out, supplements are not miracle solutions or shortcuts to fitness. Experts agree they work best when combined with a balanced diet, a structured training routine, adequate rest and consistency. Making informed, science-backed choices—not following social media myths—is the best way to support long-term health and performance.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

World.title: ‘I’ll come back to meet my fellow cockroaches’: Last night at Jantar Mantar
World.content:
Close to midnight on Saturday, six men began dismantling the makeshift iron stage at Jantar Mantar. The celebrations that erupted hours earlier after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation had subsided, and the long queues at the Kerala House and Tolstoy Marg entrances had thinned.

Yet, several supporters lingered. Some climbed police barricades, fanning those who had stayed back. Others sat in groups sharing food, while a few took photographs beside candles lit in memory of students who died by suicide after the alleged NEET paper leak. Many simply stood looking at the now-empty stage that, for 36 days, had united them under the Cockroach Janta Party banner around one demand — Pradhan’s resignation.

One of them was Vivek Kumar, aka Viru Bhai, who had turned 20 on Saturday. When The Indian Express last met him in early July, he had quit his job at a mall in Gurgaon, joking that he was pursuing a course in “politics” at the protest site.

Volunteers cleaning the protest site, after their demands were met at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on Saturday. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha) Volunteers cleaning the protest site, after their demands were met at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on Saturday. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)

After spending over a month at Jantar Mantar, Vivek found it difficult to leave. This year’s birthday, he said, had brought him nearly 15 times as many wishes as last year’s.

“Andar se rona aa raha hai, ek connection sa feel ho gaya tha yahan (I feel like crying. I’d started to feel a real connection here),” he said. “Nobody came with ego or attitude, they were real and memorable people. Even my family wouldn’t have given such love. I love these people,” Vivek added.

Students cheering who were demanding resignation from the education minister, after their demands were fulfilled, at Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi on Saturday, July 25, 2026. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha) Students cheering who were demanding resignation from the education minister, after their demands were fulfilled, at Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi on Saturday, July 25, 2026. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)

He glanced towards the stage, where he had spent weeks volunteering, and said he feels proud to have been part of the movement. “In 10-15 years, I’ll tell my children their father helped bring about the education minister’s resignation on his birthday and they’d better study,” he said, laughing.

Vivek, who dreams of starting his own political party in his hometown of Hajipur in Bihar, was set to board a train home on Sunday at 6 pm. “Right now, I’m still learning, I’ll go back and join a party campaign in Bihar… In a week, I’ll go to Manipur… I met a supporter here who asked me to come and help them raise their voice,” he added.



Just then, two people passed by carrying a stack of laddoos. Insisting that everyone take a sweet each, Vivek said, “This sweet is needed as a lot of bitterness has ended.”

Across the site, many sat on the ground reflecting on the past few weeks.

“All my friends are jealous that we were here when Pradhan resigned. They said: ‘You should have called us, we would have also come’,” said a bare-chested 21-year-old Imtiaz Ali, smiling as he checked out the views on the Instagram stories he had posted throughout the day’s celebrations.

Jantar Mantar Protest Live Updates | Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union Education Minister

Police leaving the protest site, after protest got over and demands were met at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on Saturday, July 25, 2026. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha) Police leaving the protest site, after protest got over and demands were met at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on Saturday, July 25, 2026. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)

After a day of dancing, sloganeering and cake-cutting, Ali and his three friends settled onto the Tolstoy Road footpath for the night, debating which song would best fit the reels they had shot.



“On Thursday evening, we were just having tea at our adda when we decided enough was enough. We had to come to Delhi, even if it meant getting beaten by lathis to support our peers,” said Ali, who travelled nearly 24 hours from Murshidabad in West Bengal with three of his friends.

They were among around a hundred people sleeping on the pavements outside Jantar Mantar.

Along the Kerala House stretch, supporters unfolded mosquito nets side by side while checking train schedules for the journey home. Others still milled around the protest site for one last look at the camp that had become the heart of the movement which had created history.

For Santosh Nirala, a 42-year-old mason from Sarangarh in Chhattisgarh, the journey ended in a twinge of disappointment.



He and a friend were attending a wedding and boarded a train to Delhi 15 minutes after the ceremony ended on Saturday.

Workers Dismantle the main stage of the protest site at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on Saturday, July 25, 2026. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha) Workers Dismantle the main stage of the protest site at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi on Saturday, July 25, 2026. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)

While passing through Agra Junction, they read the news. “A passenger sitting opposite me told me the minister had resigned. I said, ‘Wait, let me check.’ I couldn’t believe it. The first person I video-called was my daughter,” said Santosh, adding that she took the NEET exam this year.

“We missed it by a few hours,” he said. “I’m not a student, but my children are. There are many things that need to be corrected…”

A few hours later, senior police officers along with their teams reached the site and requested the supporters to leave as the garbage that had piled up for over a month had to be cleared.



Soon, garbage trucks rolled in. By around 1 am, the protest site, where a two-month-old online satirical platform had grown into one of the country’s first large-scale Gen Z-led protest movements, witnessing fiery speeches, songs and slogans, had fallen silent.

Vivek remained standing, leaning against a stone pillar, his eyes fixed on the empty space where the stage had stood. “I’ll come back to meet my fellow cockroaches,” he added.

World.title: The story of Hiresh Madan: From classroom mentor to education entrepreneur
World.content:
For Hiresh Madan, education has never been just a profession. It has been a lifelong mission to help students realise their academic and career aspirations.

Founder of Hitbullseye and the Mind Tree School Group, Madan has spent nearly three decades building an education ecosystem that has guided lakhs of students. What began with helping classmates prepare for examinations has grown into one of North India’s leading education enterprises.



Roots that shaped the vision
